critique.verdict: STRUCTURALLY COMPLETE, STATUSES MOSTLY SOUND. No missing units and no missing results within units — every enumeration was verified contiguous and endpoint-correct against the mmd sources, and the shortfalls vs the notes' totals (~121 BG / ~113 Pf) are artifacts of the notes, not survey gaps. The defects found are all status-labeling problems concentrated in the appendix scaffold units: one clear wrong status (Huppert App Prop 2 is proven sorry-free in the overlooked SemilinearField.lean), two internal partial-vs-missing inconsistencies on identical opaque-Prop scaffolds (FeitSibley Lem 1/2; BG App.E E.1/E.2), one cross-unit classification conflict (Isaacs 5.13 mathlib vs BG 1.18 formalized for the same Burnside theorem), one questionable formalized claim (Isaacs 6.23), and one unflagged sorried surface under a formalized/none label (BG Cor 14.9 frozen mis-encoding). Fix those seven items and the survey is reliable as a gap map for the full-formalization phase.

units.summary: Isaacs Ch.1 (Sylow Theory, results 1.1-1.46) is essentially complete: 45 of 46 numbered results are either fully covered by mathlib (18 results — all of classical Sylow E/C/D theory, orbit-stabilizer, Frattini argument, nilpotency TFAE, central-series comparison) or formalized sorry-free in the repo at full book strength (27 results), with the single gap being the equality-case clause of Lemma 1.43 (inequality proved; the equality consequences exist only inline for lattice members, effort S). The repo's genuinely new contributions beyond mathlib are: the strong Sylow counting congruence 1.16, the p-group normal-series lemmas 1.19/1.23 (with the normal form of Cor 1.24 living in the BG tree as normal_subgroup_card_pow_le_of_pGroup), the O_p(G) (`opCore`) and Fitting subgroup (`fitting`) definitions with extensive API (mathlib has neither), the small-order nonsimplicity theorems 1.30-1.36 including the full G ≅ S₄ classification for order 24, Brodkey theory 1.37-1.40, and the complete Chermak-Delgado theory 1.41-1.46 (factored into OddOrder/GroupTheory/ChermakDelgado.lean, with 1.42's equality condition even strengthened to an iff). Two structural notes: the formalization is often stronger or differently factored than the book (1.36 produces an explicit normal subgroup; 1.33 gives an explicit MulEquiv to Perm (Fin 4)), and mathlib-covered results are deliberately not wrapped (per project wrapper policy), with the correspondences recorded in section docstrings whose cited mathlib names I verified all exist in the pinned mathlib. Minor cosmetic point: Cor 1.24's Ch01 docstring cites only the weak (non-normal) mathlib form and does not cross-reference the full normal version already proved in BG S01_Solvable.lean. Slim verification pass: I attempted to refute and instead CONFIRMED the sole partial label (Lem 1.43 — inequality standalone at ChermakDelgado.lean:101, but the equality-case consequences J = HK and C_G(D) = C_G(H)C_G(K) exist only inline under lattice-membership hypotheses in chermakDelgadoLattice_sup_eq_mul, the centralizer-product clause never at set level, and pinned mathlib has no ChermakDelgado file), and read the actual Lean statements of the three most load-bearing formalized results — Thm 1.16 (card_sylow_modEq_one_of_max_inter), Thm 1.19 (IsPGroup.normal_inf_center_nontrivial), and Cor 1.28 (fitting + normal/characteristic/isNilpotent instances + nilpotent_normal_le_fitting) — confirming all three at full book strength, so no status changes were made.

results.name: Dihedral group basics: two involutions generate a dihedral group; index-2 cyclic characterization
results.notes: More is present than first surveyed, but the label 'partial' stands. Ch02 (Theorem211Wielandt.lean) proves the Matsuyama-facing essence: t inverts every element of ⟨s·t⟩ and ⟨s,t⟩ = ⟨st⟩ ∪ ⟨st⟩·t. CORRECTION: the DihedralGroup identification is NOT missing — Ch06_FrobeniusActions/DQSDRecognition.lean has dihedralIsoOfInverting (private, general finite group, no 2-group hypothesis): ⟨c⟩ of index 2, involution a outside with a·c·a⁻¹ = c⁻¹ ⇒ P ≃* DihedralGroup (orderOf c), i.e. 2.14(a)'s 'D is dihedral' clause in stronger (iso-type) form; public wrapper dihedralOrQuaternion_of_invertingConjugation carries an unused IsPGroup 2 hypothesis. Genuinely missing as stated: (a)'s easy iff direction (all of D−C involutions ⇒ c^t = c⁻¹), and (b)'s explicit packaging C ≠ 1, s,t ∉ C, |D:C| = 2. Remaining gap is small (S).

results.notes: All primes p, arbitrary normal N, as in the book. Book text does not tag it Lemma/Theorem explicitly in the OCR; it is Lemma 2.16 in print.

results.name: p'-kernel quotient: P̄ nontrivial and N_Ḡ(P̄) = image of N_G(P); images of p-locals are p-local
results.notes: All three assertions of the book statement covered (nontriviality, normalizer equality, p-local corollary).

results.name: Zenkov: minimal member of {A ∩ B^g} lies in F(G) (A, B abelian)
results.notes: Minimality stated as ≤-minimality over all g (book's 'minimal member'), general g₀; full strength. Book remark that this generalizes Brodkey 1.37 holds — repo Ch01 has Brodkey separately.

results.name: Abelian A with |A| ≥ |G:A| in nontrivial G meets F(G) nontrivially
results.notes: Exact book statement: A.index ≤ Nat.card A ⇒ A ⊓ fitting G ≠ ⊥.

results.name: Lucchini: cyclic proper A has |A : core_G(A)| < |G : A|
results.notes: Full theorem lives in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch04_Commutators/ForwardFromCh02.lean (import-order: K=⊥ case needs Ch.4 commutator machinery); Ch02 holds the K>⊥ correspondence reduction. Statement is full book strength ((A.normalCore.subgroupOf A).index < A.index; explicit abelian hypothesis is redundant given cyclicity but harmless). The 'in particular K > 1' remark is derived inline where used (Ch03 Horosevskii). CAUTION: comments in Ch02/Main.lean §2D and Ch03/Basic.lean still call the K=⊥ case an 'axiom' — stale; lucchini_K_bot_aux is now a proven private theorem and the file is sorry-free.

results.name: Socle Soc(G) = join of all minimal normal subgroups
results.notes: Both mathlib-absent; defined in Basic.lean with the API needed for Thm 2.6 (isMinimalNormal_le_socle, socle_ne_bot_of_nontrivial, characteristic-style transport). Structural facts about socles (direct product of simples) are Problems 2A.5-2A.7, not numbered results, and are not formalized.

results.name: p-local and local subgroups (normalizers of nontrivial p-subgroups)
results.notes: Mathlib-absent; matches the book definition verbatim.

results.name: Normal closure H^G = ⟨H^x : x ∈ G⟩
results.notes: Used directly in the zipper-lemma applications (2.8, 2.11, 2.12).

units.summary: Isaacs Ch.2 (Subnormality, results 2.1-2.20) is essentially completely formalized and sorry-free: 16 of 20 numbered results have full-book-strength Lean statements in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch02_Subnormality/{Basic,Theorem211Wielandt,Main}.lean, 3 more (2.4, 2.7, and the subnormality/normal-closure definitions) are covered directly by mathlib (Subgroup.IsSubnormal.inf, Subgroup.commute_of_normal_of_disjoint) per the repo's no-wrapper policy. The only gap is Lemma 2.14 (dihedral structure of a group generated by two involutions): its Matsuyama-facing essence is in Ch02 and — beyond what the original survey recorded — the DihedralGroup identification exists in Ch06 (dihedralIsoOfInverting), leaving only (a)'s easy iff direction and (b)'s explicit C≠1/s,t∉C/|D:C|=2 packaging unstated — a small (S) task. Notable factoring differences: Lucchini 2.20's full theorem lives in Ch04_Commutators/ForwardFromCh02.lean for import-order reasons (stale comments in Ch02/Ch03 still call its K=⊥ case an 'axiom', but it is now a proven theorem with zero sorries and zero axiom declarations), and the repo goes beyond the book by deriving the single-element Baer-Suzuki p-core theorem (baerSuzuki_pCore) from Baer 2.12. End-of-section Problems (2A.x-2D.x) are not formalized, consistent with the project formalizing numbered results only. Slim-pass verification: re-read Thm 2.5, Thm 2.9, and Thm 2.12 statements and confirmed full book strength; for Lem 2.14 the 'partial' label is confirmed but its notes were corrected — the repo DOES identify the inverting index-2-cyclic configuration with mathlib's DihedralGroup via Ch06_FrobeniusActions/DQSDRecognition.lean (dihedralIsoOfInverting, general finite group), so only the trivial iff direction and part (b)'s index/membership packaging remain missing.
units.unit: Isaacs Ch.2 Subnormality

results.name: Uniqueness of split extension given N, H and the action (unique iso extending matching isos)
results.notes: Repo/mathlib state the canonical internal form: N normal with complement K gives G ≅ N ⋊ K. The book's two-abstract-groups form (compatible isos N≅N₀, H≅H₀ extend to a unique iso G≅G₀) follows by composing two such isos but is not literally stated; the uniqueness clause is implicit.

results.name: Existence of the semidirect product realizing a given action via automorphisms
results.notes: mathlib's SemidirectProduct is the construction; the repo adds Isaacs-form restatements (inl(N) normal, inl(N)/inr(H) complements, conjugation = action) in Ch03_SplitExtensions/Basic.lean.

results.name: Horosevskii: o(σ) < |G| for σ ∈ Aut(G), G nontrivial finite
results.notes: Full proof present (Basic.lean), via Lucchini Thm 2.20 (OddOrder.Isaacs.Ch04.lucchini_index_normalCore_lt_index) in the semidirect product Γ = G ⋊ ⟨σ⟩. Sorry-free (stale TODO in docstring notwithstanding).

results.name: Abelian p-subgroup of Aut(G) with p ∤ |G| has a regular orbit on G
results.notes: Stated as ∃ g : G with trivial P-stabilizer (standard regular-orbit formulation); proved via Brodkey (Isaacs Thm 1.37, Ch.1). The trailing 'in particular |P| < |G|' remark is not separately stated but is a one-line consequence.

results.name: Schur-Zassenhaus, abelian case: abelian normal Hall subgroup is complemented and all complements conjugate
results.notes: Existence is mathlib (general case subsumes abelian). Conjugacy: repo OddOrder/Mathlib/SchurZassenhausConj.lean has private abelian_sz_conjugacy (built on mathlib Subgroup.exists_smul_eq for QuotientDiff) and the public full Thm 3.12 subsumes the abelian case.

results.name: Crossed homomorphism basics: φ(1)=1, kernel is a subgroup, fibers are cosets, |G:K|=|φ(G)|
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): only trace is a correspondence-table row in Ch03_SplitExtensions/Basic.lean:451 pointing at mathlib's OneCocycle (GroupCohomology.LowDegree), which covers only abelian-coefficient cocycles and none of the kernel/fiber facts. Proof device for Thm 3.5, bypassed because the mechanized SZ proof uses mathlib's QuotientDiff route instead. Self-contained if ever wanted.

results.name: Transversal difference function d(S,T): cocycle identity, translation, d(S,Sn)=n^|G:N|
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): same situation as 3.6 — proof machinery for Thm 3.5. mathlib's SchurZassenhaus uses the equivalent smul_diff/QuotientDiff device internally but the book-form lemma is not stated anywhere in repo or mathlib.

results.name: Schur-Zassenhaus existence: normal Hall subgroup is complemented
results.notes: Full book strength in mathlib (Mathlib.GroupTheory.SchurZassenhaus).

results.name: G solvable iff G^(m) = 1 for some m (derived series characterization)
results.notes: mathlib takes the derived-series condition as the definition of IsSolvable, so the book's equivalence is definitional on one side; the normal-abelian-series direction is what mathlib's solvability instances encode.

results.name: Solvability closure: subgroups, quotients, extensions (derived series functoriality)
results.notes: All five parts covered by Mathlib.GroupTheory.Solvable instances/theorems; solvable_of_ker_le_range gives extension closure (part e).

results.name: Solvable minimal normal subgroup is abelian; if finite, elementary abelian p-group
results.notes: Stated for a finite solvable ambient G (book: arbitrary G with M solvable minimal normal, plus an infinite-abelian clause). Covers every downstream use in the book and repo; SchurZassenhausConj.lean carries additional internal copies of both halves.

results.name: Schur-Zassenhaus conjugacy: complements of a normal Hall subgroup are conjugate when N or G/N is solvable
results.notes: Statement re-verified in source (SchurZassenhausConj.lean:1292, ~1300-line file): hypotheses Nat.Coprime (Nat.card N) N.index and IsSolvable N ∨ IsSolvable (G/N), conclusion ∃ n ∈ N conjugating K to K' — full book strength, conclusion stronger than book (conjugator lies in N).

results.name: Hall E-theorem: finite solvable G has a Hall π-subgroup for every π
results.notes: Statement re-verified in source (Basic.lean:991): [Finite G] [IsSolvable G] (π) → ∃ H, IsHallSubgroup π H — full strength, |G|-strong induction following Isaacs. Built on the repo's IsHallSubgroup definition (general π-Hall theory is repo-implemented, not mathlib).

results.name: Hall C-theorem: all Hall π-subgroups of a finite solvable group are conjugate
results.notes: Statement re-verified in source (Basic.lean:1364): ∃ g, H.map (conj g) = K under IsHallSubgroup hypotheses — full strength. Bonus beyond the numbered results: the Hall D-theorem (Problem 3C.1 in the book) is also fully proved as OddOrder.Isaacs.Ch03.hall_D (Basic.lean:1664).

results.name: Converse of Hall E: G with a p-complement for every prime p is solvable
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch07_ThompsonSubgroup/ForwardFromCh03.lean is still docstring-only — the solvable_of_pcomplement_exists signature at its line 13 sits inside the module docstring's code fence, and the namespace (lines 55-57) is explicitly empty. The blocking dependency, Burnside p^a q^b, is now proved sorry-free (OddOrder.Isaacs.Ch07.burnside_p_pow_q_pow), so this is unblocked: |G|-induction + Hall intersections + Burnside.

results.name: Coprime indices: G = HK and |H : H∩K| = |G : K|
results.notes: Verified partial (slim pass): Theorem315.lean:32 proves only H ⊔ K = ⊤ from coprime indices. The index-equality clause |H:H∩K| = |G:K| is not stated anywhere in the repo (relIndex greps show only unrelated uses); mathlib's relIndex API (inf_relIndex_left, relIndex_mul_index) puts it within easy reach.

results.name: Wielandt: three solvable subgroups with pairwise coprime indices force G solvable
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): solvable_of_three_subgroups appears only inside the module docstring of Ch07/ForwardFromCh03.lean (namespace intentionally empty). Requires Burnside p^a q^b for the simple case — now available (burnside_p_pow_q_pow) — plus a minimal-counterexample induction.

results.name: A subnormal series with π/π' factors already makes G π-separable
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): full inventory of IsPiSeparable lemmas shows only quotient/normal-subgroup/complement closures (quotient_isPiSeparable, normalSubgroup_isPiSeparable, Subgroup.isPiSeparable_of_isPiSeparable, isPiSeparable_compl) plus one specialized extension case, isPiSeparable_of_normalPSubgroup_quotient_hasNormalPComplement (Ch07). The general series characterization / extension-closure of the piFittingSeries-based IsPiSeparable definition is absent; its downstream role in the book is otherwise covered.

results.name: Finite solvable groups are π-separable for every π
results.notes: Instance form, proved by strong induction on the π-Fitting series (Main.lean).

results.name: π-separable groups have Hall π-subgroups
results.notes: Full strength; generalizes hall_E_exists exactly as in the book (minimal normal subgroup + Schur-Zassenhaus).

results.name: Hall-Higman Lemma 1.2.3: π-separable with O_π'(G)=1 implies C_G(O_π(G)) ≤ O_π(G)
results.notes: Statement re-verified in source (Main.lean:642): [Finite G] [IsPiSeparable π G], oPiCore π' G = ⊥ → centralizer (oPiCore π G) ≤ oPiCore π G — exact full book strength (flagged FT-critical in the repo), plus the C_G(O_π) = Z(O_π) corollary. A solvable specialization also exists in BG §1 (hall_higman_solvable_specialization).

results.name: π-separable with abelian Hall π-subgroup has π-length ≤ 1
results.notes: Verified partial (slim pass, statement+proof read at Main.lean:720): the Lean theorem concludes only ⁅O_{π',π}(G), O_{π',π}(G)⁆ ≤ O_π'(G) — a strictly weaker fact whose proof indeed uses no Hall-Higman (just O_π(Ḡ) ≤ abelian Hall image). The genuine book conclusion (H̄ = O_π(Ḡ), equivalently G = O_{π',π,π'}(G)) is unproved: BG §1 defines HasPiLengthOne (S01_Solvable.lean:1273) and pLengthOne, but grep shows no theorem producing either. Closing the gap is short since hall_higman_1_2_3 is available.

results.name: Coprime action: (a) A-invariant Sylow p-subgroup exists; (b) two A-invariant Sylows are conjugate by an element of C_G(A)
results.notes: Lives in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch04_Commutators/ForwardFromCh03.lean (not the Ch03 tree). Hypotheses match the book exactly ((|A|,|G|)=1 and IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G). Sorry-free.

results.name: Glauberman's Lemma: compatible coprime actions on a transitive G-set have (a) an A-invariant point, (b) C_G(A)-transitivity on A-invariant points
results.notes: Both parts at full book strength, via the Γ = G ⋊ A construction and Schur-Zassenhaus existence + conjugacy, exactly as in Isaacs pp. 98-99.

results.name: A-invariant Sylow D: an A-invariant p-subgroup lies in an A-invariant Sylow p-subgroup
results.notes: Full strength. The repo also proves a strictly stronger Hall-subgroup generalization for solvable groups: OddOrder.BG.Ch1.S01.aInvariant_piSubgroup_le_aInvariant_hall (used by OddOrder.GroupTheory.exists_aInvariant_complement_of_normal_isHall).

results.name: K ↦ K ∩ C_G(A) is a bijection from A-invariant classes of G onto classes of C_G(A)
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): re-searched ConjClasses/invariant-class/class-bijection and the full declaration list of Ch04/ForwardFromCh03.lean (contains exactly the Tier-1 cluster, nothing more); OddOrder/GroupTheory/CoprimeConjugacy.lean header confirms it is Peterfalvi (2.1) coset-conjugacy material, not this. Isaacs's proof is a half-page application of 3.24(a)+(b), both formalized, so this is a short exercise.

results.name: A-invariant (left/right) cosets of an A-invariant H are exactly those meeting C_G(A)
results.notes: The sharp form matches the book's hypothesis ((|A|,|H|)=1, A or H solvable). One coset orientation is stated (gN with c = g*n); the mirror form is trivially symmetric as the book itself notes. The easy converse direction (cosets meeting C are invariant) is implicit in usage.

results.name: Fixed points come from fixed points: C_{G/N}(A) = image of C_G(A)
results.notes: Both an elementwise form (Ch04/ForwardFromCh03.lean) and a subgroup-equality form plus a cardinality product formula (OddOrder/GroupTheory/CoprimeFixedPoints.lean). Full strength with the sharp (|A|,|N|)-coprime hypothesis.

results.name: Coprime action trivial on G/Φ(G) is trivial on G
results.notes: Full strength (Frattini non-generating + Cor 3.28).

results.name: Faithful coprime action remains faithful on G/Φ(G)
results.notes: Stated in the classically equivalent practical form: A faithful on G and trivial on G/Φ(G) forces A = 1 (the book's contrapositive).

results.name: Hartley-Turull: coprime action can be replaced by an action on an abelian group with the same fixed-point counts for every B ≤ A, hence orbit-size-preserving
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): Hartley/Turull/orbit-size greps hit only unrelated character-theory files; Main.lean:770 explicitly lists 'Thm 3.29-3.31 orbit structure' as not-implemented Tier 2. One proof ingredient exists — the multiplicativity |C_K(B)| = |C_{G'}(B)|·|C_{G/G'}(B)| step is essentially OddOrder.GroupTheory.card_fixedSubgroup_eq_mul — but the invariant-Sylow direct-product reduction, Lemma 3.32, and the derived-length induction are absent. Multi-day but all prerequisites (3.23-3.28) are formalized.

results.name: For an A-invariant P ∈ Syl_p(G), P ∩ C_G(A) is a Sylow p-subgroup of C_G(A)
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): fixedSubgroup+Sylow/Hall greps return zero hits; Sylow occurrences in CoprimeAction.lean, CoprimeFixedPoints.lean and BG S01_Solvable.lean are all unrelated (Lem 1.14 helpers). Isaacs's proof is 4 lines from Cor 3.25 + Thm 3.23(b), both formalized — a genuinely short gap, and the key prerequisite for 3.31.

results.name: Equal fixed-point counts for all B ≤ A on two finite A-sets yield an A-equivariant bijection
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass): fixed-point-count/equivariant greps hit only unrelated BG/representation files. Purely combinatorial induction on |Ω| (removing minimal orbits); self-contained with no group-theoretic prerequisites, but the equivariant-bijection bookkeeping is fiddly in Lean. Needed only for the orbit clause of 3.31/3.34.

results.name: Coprime action with coprime orbit sizes m, n has an orbit of size mn
results.notes: Verified missing (slim pass, no counterpart under number or descriptive searches). Depends on 3.31 (abelian replacement), 3.16's index clause, 3.27, and the transfer-like τ map argument; roughly 2-3 days once 3.31-3.33 exist. Not used on the FT path (Isaacs cites it only toward Ch.8 material).

results.name: Cyclic extension uniqueness: matching data (N≅N₀, g↦g₀, g^m, conjugation) gives a unique isomorphism G ≅ G₀
results.notes: Verified partial (slim pass, statement read at Main.lean:1156): only the uniqueness half is proved (two homomorphisms agreeing on N and at the generator lift coincide — a mild generalization of the book's uniqueness clause), plus a generator-lift lemma (Main.lean:1123). The existence-of-isomorphism half (constructing θ from the compatibility data) is absent; its own docstring marks existence as 'Phase 4 予定'.

results.name: Cyclic extension existence: given a ∈ N, σ ∈ Aut(N) with σ(a)=a and σ^m = conj(a), there is G ⊇ N with G/N cyclic of order m, g^m = a, x^g = σ(x)
results.notes: Verified partial (slim pass, statement read at Main.lean:1278): the construction (N ⋊_σ ℤ quotiented by the central element (a⁻¹, m)) is fully proved with clauses zpowers(gN₀) = ⊤, g^m = ι a, conjugation = σ. But the ∃-statement omits |G/N₀| = m — as stated it is satisfiable by degenerate witnesses (e.g. the trivial group when a=1, σ=id) — and the 'unique up to isomorphism' clause is not assembled. The actual constructed group does have order-m quotient, so strengthening is a statement+small-proof fix.

results.name: Hall π-subgroup, p-complement, π-number (named definitions of §3C)
results.notes: Repo-built (general π-Hall theory is not in mathlib): IsHallSubgroup π H := prime factors of |H| in π and of [G:H] outside π, with a substantial API (quotient/pullback/complement/conjugation-action lemmas across Basic.lean and Theorem315.lean). p-complement = IsHallSubgroup {q | q ≠ p}.

results.name: π-separable / π-solvable groups, O_π(G), π-length (named definitions of §3D)
results.notes: π-separability is defined via the upper π-Fitting series reaching ⊤ (equivalent to the book's normal-series definition for finite groups; the equivalence itself is the unproved Lem 3.18). O_π(G) = oPiCore with normal/characteristic instances and a rich API. General π-length is not defined — only the length-one predicate HasPiLengthOne (BG §1); 'π-solvable' as a separate general-π notion is not defined (unused: for π={p} it coincides with p-separability, which is covered).

results.name: Wreath product H ≀ G (base group, regular wreath product)
results.notes: Verified (slim pass): the pinned mathlib does ship Mathlib/GroupTheory/RegularWreathProduct.lean (regular wreath product only); no wreath content anywhere in OddOrder/. The book's general form over an arbitrary G-set Ω is absent from both. Isaacs uses it only for examples/problems (3A.9), and nothing in the repo consumes it, so this is a low-priority gap.

units.summary: Ch.3 is very thoroughly covered: 27 of 36 numbered results are fully formalized or mathlib-covered, including the FT-critical Hall E/C theorems (plus Hall D, which the book leaves as Problem 3C.1), Hall-Higman 1.2.3, Schur-Zassenhaus (existence = mathlib; the conjugacy Theorem 3.12 is repo-proved at full strength for both solvability cases, with the stronger conclusion that the conjugator lies in N), and the whole Glauberman coprime-action "Tier 1" (3.23-3.25, 3.27-3.30) — which lives in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch04_Commutators/ForwardFromCh03.lean and OddOrder/Mathlib/SchurZassenhausConj.lean, not in the Ch03 directory. The main gaps are (a) the two Burnside-gated solvability criteria 3.15 and 3.17, whose placeholder file is still intentionally empty even though Burnside p^a q^b is now proved sorry-free in Ch.7 (burnside_p_pow_q_pow), so both are unblocked; and (b) the coprime-orbit "Tier 2" cluster 3.26, 3.31-3.34 (class bijection, Hartley-Turull, orbit-size product), entirely missing though all Glauberman ingredients exist. Four results are weaker than the book: 3.22 proves only a commutator containment rather than genuine pi-length <= 1 (BG's HasPiLengthOne def exists with no theorem), 3.16 lacks the |H:H∩K|=|G:K| clause, 3.35 has only the uniqueness half, and 3.36's existence statement omits the |G/N|=m clause (degenerate witnesses satisfy it). The crossed-homomorphism machinery 3.6/3.7 was never formalized because mathlib's QuotientDiff proof route made it unnecessary; pi-Hall/pi-separable theory is repo-built (IsHallSubgroup, IsPiSeparable via an upper pi-Fitting series) and is in places stronger than the book (e.g. a Hall-subgroup generalization of Cor 3.25 in BG §1). Slim verification pass (2026-07-16): all 15 flagged missing/partial labels were re-attacked by book-number and descriptive-content greps and every one stands — no status changed (Ch07/ForwardFromCh03.lean remains a docstring-only placeholder whose theorem signatures sit inside code fences; the only near-miss is a specialized extension-closure instance isPiSeparable_of_normalPSubgroup_quotient_hasNormalPComplement noted under 3.18) — and the three most load-bearing formalized results (3.12 SZ-conjugacy, 3.13/3.14 Hall E/C, 3.21 Hall-Higman 1.2.3) were read in source and confirmed at full book strength.
units.unit: Isaacs Ch.3 Split Extensions (Hall, Schur-Zassenhaus) — mmd lines ~1306-2124, results 3.1-3.36

results.name: H and K normalize [H,K]; [H,K] normal in ⟨H,K⟩
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean. Full book strength for arbitrary groups, no normality assumptions (mathlib's Subgroup.commutator_normal instance requires both subgroups normal, so repo version is genuinely needed).

results.name: Image of [H,K] under quotient hom = commutator of images
results.notes: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Commutator/Basic.lean:274, verified. Stated for arbitrary f : G →* G', which subsumes the bar-convention quotient statement. Repo docstrings record the correspondence; no wrapper written (project policy).

results.name: K ≤ N_G(H) iff [H,K] ≤ H; in particular H ⊴ G iff [H,G] ≤ H
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean; iff at full strength for arbitrary groups. The 'in particular' clause is mathlib Subgroup.commutator_top_left_le_iff (verified at Commutator/Basic.lean:214).

results.name: Class-2 p-group: exponent of P/Z(P) divides exponent of P'; Φ(P) ≤ Z(P) if P' elementary abelian
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean. Formalized STRONGER than book: stated for any group of class ≤ 2 and any exponent n (book: p-group, n = p^e). All three clauses including the Φ(P) ≤ Z(P) conclusion.

results.name: For p-group P, N ⊴ P: P/N elementary abelian iff Φ(P) ≤ N
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean. Full iff for finite p-groups (book implicitly finite: proof uses fundamental theorem of abelian groups). Forward direction proved via ZMod-p vector-space duality.

results.name: A ⊴ G abelian, G/A cyclic: G' = [A,G], G' ≅ A/(A∩Z(G)), |A| = |G'|·|A∩Z(G)|
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean. All three clauses covered, but G'=[A,G] and the range identity carry [Finite G] where the book states them for arbitrary G (finiteness is only needed for the cardinality clause); the isomorphism is factored as range/ker of the hom θ(a)=[a,g] (commutatorRightHom) + first-iso rather than an explicit MulEquiv. Heavily cited chapter hub (5 in-chapter cites + Ch.5/Ch.7 use).

results.name: A ⊴ P abelian of order p^m, P/A cyclic, |A∩Z(P)|=p ⇒ nilpotence class of P equals m
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean. Full induction on m, exact class equality (Group.nilpotencyClass P = m). The unnumbered maximal-class discussion following 4.7 (dihedral/quaternion have maximal class) is not formalized here, but it is expository, not a numbered result.

results.name: p > 2, class ≤ 2: (a) {x : x^p = 1} is a subgroup; (b) x ↦ x^p is a homomorphism if commutators have p-th power 1
results.notes: Main/CommutatorBasics.lean. Stronger than book: stated for any group of class ≤ 2 with p odd (book: p-group). Includes the commutator-collection formula (xy)^n = x^n y^n [y,x]^(n(n-1)/2) as mul_pow_of_class_le_two.

results.name: Hall–Witt identity [x,y⁻¹,z]^y [y,z⁻¹,x]^z [z,x⁻¹,y]^x = 1
results.notes: Four equivalent forms in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Commutator/Basic.lean:95-118, each doc-tagged 'The Hall-Witt identity' (verified).

results.name: Three subgroups lemma: [X,Y,Z]=1 and [Y,Z,X]=1 imply [Z,X,Y]=1
results.notes: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Commutator/Basic.lean:163 (verified). Repo uses it directly per no-wrapper policy.

results.name: Three subgroups lemma modulo a normal subgroup N
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:34. Full strength (arbitrary G, N normal), proved by pushing through G/N.

results.name: Lower central series additivity [G^i, G^j] ≤ G^{i+j}
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:77. In mathlib indexing: ⁅lcs i, lcs j⁆ ≤ lcs (i+j+1) (mathlib lcs n = Isaacs G^{n+1}). Full strength, arbitrary groups.

results.name: Every weight-n commutator of copies of G is contained in G^n
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:114-147 covers only the LEFT-ASSOCIATED element-commutator form. The book statement is about arbitrarily bracketed weight-n subgroup commutators (e.g. [[G,G],[G,G,G]]); that form is absent — needs a small bracketing-tree datatype + trivial induction from Thm 4.11 (already formalized). The consequence actually needed downstream (4.13) is proved directly. VERIFIED (slim pass): grep for bracketing-tree/weight-commutator datatypes across OddOrder/ found nothing beyond iterLeftCommutator; partial label stands.

results.name: G^(r) ≤ G^{2^r}; nilpotent of class m ⇒ derived length ≤ 1 + log₂ m
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:165-205. Both clauses: derivedSeries G r ≤ lcs (2^r - 1) (strictly stronger than mathlib's derived_le_lower_central) and lcs m = ⊥ → derivedSeries (Nat.log 2 m + 1) = ⊥.

results.name: M(G) = subgroup generated by elements in conjugacy classes of size ≤ n₂ (second-smallest class size)
results.notes: No Lean counterpart, re-verified in slim pass: grepped 'Mann', 'Ishikawa', 'M(G)', small/second-smallest class, class-size generation across OddOrder/ — only hits are the explicit skip comment (Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:221, 'BG/Peterfalvi 直接被引用 0 ⇒ Phase 1 skip') and unrelated Schur-multiplier M(G) discussion in Ch05_Transfer/Basic.lean. Prerequisite for 4.14/4.15/4.18/4.19.

results.name: Mann: G finite nilpotent ⇒ nilpotence class of M(G) at most 3 (contains Ishikawa's theorem)
results.notes: Confirmed missing (slim pass: no Mann/Ishikawa/class-≤3 content outside BG-numbered files, which are different results). Immediate from 4.15 + 4.16 once those exist. Whole Mann cluster (M(G) def + 4.14/4.15/4.17/4.18/4.19) is roughly one M-sized job; deliberately skipped during the FT phase as it has no downstream citations in BG/Peterfalvi.

results.name: G with a self-centralizing normal subgroup ⇒ M(G) nilpotent of class ≤ 3
results.notes: Confirmed missing (slim pass; note BG Lemma 4.15 hits in S04_PGroupsSmallRank.lean are an unrelated extraspecial-commutator result). Short proof from 4.18 + three-subgroups lemma (mathlib) + M^4 ≤ [K,M,M] = 1. Blocked only on 4.17/4.18 and the M(G) definition.

results.name: Finite nilpotent G: maximal normal abelian A satisfies A = C_G(A); hence nilpotent groups have self-centralizing normal subgroups
results.notes: Lives OUTSIDE the chapter tree: OddOrder/GroupTheory/CriticalSubgroup.lean:166, cited as Gorenstein 5.3.12 (same statement). Statement re-read in slim pass: hypotheses are [Finite P] + IsPGroup p P — p-group form only; book states finite nilpotent G. The proof (pass to G/A, minimal normal in center, cyclic-over-central extension abelian) works verbatim for nilpotent — generalization is under a day. p-group form suffices for all current repo consumers (SCN.lean, critical subgroups, BG S04).

results.name: K abelian normal, x noncentral ⇒ |C_G(x)| < |C_G(y)| for y = [k,x]
results.notes: Confirmed missing (slim pass: grepped centralizer-cardinality comparisons — card_centralizer hits are all Peterfalvi S03/S04 fiber-counting, unrelated; the θ(t)=[t,x] hom pattern exists only in the 4.6 commutatorRightHom context). Core counting lemma of the Mann cluster. Needs: θ : K → K hom, θ(K) ⊴ H = K·C_G(x), |θ(K)| = |H : C_H(x)|, conjugacy-class-size comparison inside θ(K). Mathlib + repo (ConjClassCardinality.lean) have the needed index/class-size API; estimate 1-2 days.

results.name: K abelian normal ⇒ [K, M(G)] ≤ Z(G)
results.notes: Confirmed missing (slim pass). Direct from 4.17 (elements of small classes map commutators into smaller classes = center). Requires M(G) definition.

results.name: For any finite G, the nilpotence class of F(M(G)) is at most 4
results.notes: Confirmed missing (slim pass: no class-≤4 Fitting bound anywhere in OddOrder/). Short argument from 4.18 + Thm 4.11 (formalized) + repo Fitting subgroup (OddOrder.Isaacs.Ch01.fitting exists). Blocked on 4.17/4.18/M(G).

results.name: [G,A] is the unique smallest A-invariant normal subgroup with trivial induced action on the quotient
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean. [G,A] implemented as actionCommutator (φ : A →* MulAut G) = closure {g·(φ a)g⁻¹}; normality instance actionCommutator.normal, A-invariance IsAInvariant.actionCommutator, quotient-action triviality iff — together the full characterization. Design: dual tracking with ⁅inl G, inr A⁆ inside the semidirect product Γ = G ⋊[φ] A (actionCommutator_map_inl bridges).

results.name: TFAE: all right cosets of H A-invariant / all left cosets A-invariant / [G,A] ≤ H
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:1008. Coset invariance expressed at element level ((φ a)x·x⁻¹ ∈ H resp. x⁻¹·(φ a)x ∈ H) — equivalent to the book's coset formulation.

results.name: A faithful on G with [G,A,...,A]_m = 1 ⇒ A solvable of derived length ≤ m−1
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:244-293. Chain hypothesis phrased as iterCommutator inl.range inr.range m = ⊥ in Γ = G ⋊[φ] A. Both the faithful form and the book's proof-internal non-faithful form (derivedSeries A (m−1) ≤ φ.ker). Arbitrary (possibly infinite) groups — full strength.

results.name: A faithful with [G,A,A] = 1 ⇒ A abelian
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:80-134. Hypothesis phrased as actionCommutator φ ≤ fixedPointsOfMulAut φ (= A trivial on [G,A]); full strength.

results.name: A finite faithful on finite G with [G,A,...,A] = 1 ⇒ A nilpotent (P. Hall direction, qualitative)
results.notes: Main/ChainNilpotent.lean (a whole 1052-line file for this induction). Also the non-faithful form A^∞ ≤ ker φ, with G^∞ formalized as lowerCentralSeriesInfty. Hall's quantitative class bound m(m−1)/2 is explicitly not proved in the book either.

results.name: [G,A,A] = 1 ⇒ [G,A] abelian
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroups.lean:1043. Arbitrary groups, three-subgroups argument in Γ = G ⋊[φ] A, full strength.

results.name: A a p-group with [G,A,...,A] = 1 ⇒ [G,A] is a p-group
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:823. Finite A, G as in book; strong induction on |G| via O_p-core and coprime fixed-point lifting (Cor 3.28 analog from Ch03).

results.name: Finite A with [G,A,...,A] = 1 ⇒ [G,A] nilpotent
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:933. Induction on |A| via Sylow generation + Fitting subgroup, exactly the book's proof.

results.name: Coprime action, A or G solvable ⇒ G = C_G(A)·[G,A]
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:350. Statement re-read in slim pass and confirmed full book strength: [Finite A] [Finite G], Nat.Coprime |A| |G|, IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G ⇒ fixedPointsOfMulAut φ ⊔ actionCommutator φ = ⊤ — hypotheses match the printed 4.28 exactly. FT-critical (= BG Prop 1.6(a)).

results.name: Coprime action ⇒ [G,A,A] = [G,A]
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:394. Retains hypothesis IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G, whereas the printed 4.29 is UNCONDITIONAL (the book's proof removes solvability by reducing to the cyclic subgroup ⟨a⟩). The reduction machinery exists (iterCommutator_inl_inr_restrict_eq_bot) and is used exactly this way inside 4.30's proof (restrict to Sylow p-subgroups), so stating the unconditional version is a short derivation; also always dischargeable since coprimality forces one factor to have odd order (repo's FT).

results.name: A faithful with [G,A,...,A] = 1 ⇒ every prime divisor of |A| divides |G|
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:608. Full strength; proof restricts the chain to a Sylow p-subgroup and collapses via 4.29.

results.name: Thompson P×Q lemma: A = P × Q on p-group G, C_G(P) ≤ C_G(Q) ⇒ Q trivial on G
results.notes: Main/BaerTrick.lean:1105. Statement re-read in slim pass and confirmed full book strength: φ : P × Q →* MulAut G, IsPGroup p G, IsPGroup p P, ¬p ∣ |Q|, element-level C_G(P) ≤ C_G(Q) hypothesis ⇒ actionCommutator (φ.comp (prodRightHom P Q)) = ⊥ — external direct-product form equivalent to the book's internal statement. Supporting infrastructure prodLeftHom/prodRightHom + invariance lemmas.

results.name: p-group P acting on nontrivial p-group G: [G,P] < G and C_G(P) > 1
results.notes: Main/BaerTrick.lean:705,740. Both halves; strict inequality expressed inside Γ = G ⋊[φ] P via inl-identification.

results.name: G p-solvable ⇒ O_{p'}(H) ≤ O_{p'}(G) for every p-local subgroup H
results.notes: Main/BaerTrick.lean:1311. Formalized STRONGER than book: hypothesis is IsPiSeparable {p} (p-separable), weaker than the book's p-solvable. O_{p'} expressed as oPiCore of the complement set; p-local as Ch02.IsPLocal. Uses Hall–Higman 1.2.3 route as in book.

results.name: Fitting: coprime action on abelian G ⇒ G = C_G(A) × [G,A]
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:1006. Internal direct product factored as sup = ⊤ (4.28, G abelian hence solvable) plus inf = ⊥ (via the averaging hom θ(g) = ∏_a (φ a)g = fittingProductHom, exactly the book's map). For normal subgroups of an abelian group this is the full direct-product statement. Problem 4D.6's refinement (θ(G) = C_G(A), ker θ = [G,A]) not stated but not a numbered result.

results.name: p'-group A on abelian p-group G fixing every element of order p ⇒ A trivial on G
results.notes: Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean:1052. Full strength (= BG Prop 1.6(e)); FT-critical.

results.name: p > 2, p-group G, p'-group A fixing every element of order p ⇒ A trivial on G
results.notes: Main/BaerTrick.lean:692. Statement re-read in slim pass and confirmed full book strength: p ≠ 2, IsPGroup p G, ¬p ∣ |A|, (∀ g, g^p = 1 → ∀ a, φ a g = g) ⇒ actionCommutator φ = ⊥ (= BG Thm 1.11, FT-critical); strong induction reduces to class ≤ 2 then transports through the Baer trick to the abelian case 4.35.

results.name: Baer trick: odd-order class ≤ 2 group admits abelian addition x+y = xy√[y,x] with (a) x+y = xy when commuting, (b) additive order = multiplicative order, (c) Aut(G) ⊆ Aut(G,+)
results.notes: Main/BaerTrick.lean. Complete: sqrtOdd infrastructure, commutativity/associativity, CommGroup instance on type synonym BaerMul G, part (a) baerAdd_eq_mul_of_commute, part (b) npow_eq_pow/pow_eq_one_iff/isPGroup_iff, part (c) automorphism transport including action lift A →* MulAut (BaerMul G).

results.name: Strong P×Q lemma: p > 2, P ≤ A p-group, Q ⊴ A p'-group, C_G(P) ≤ C_G(Q) ⇒ Q trivial on p-group G
results.notes: Main/BaerTrick.lean:1557. Full strength (P need not be normal); strong induction + Baer trick as in book.

results.name: Lower central series G^k and its final term G^∞
results.notes: G^k = mathlib lowerCentralSeries with index offset 1 (mathlib lcs n = Isaacs G^{n+1}; offset documented in CommutatorBasics.lean header). G^∞ formalized in Main/ChainNilpotent.lean:111 as lcs at index Nat.card A, with the fixed-point property ⁅G^∞,⊤⁆ = G^∞ proved. The surrounding unnumbered facts (nilpotent iff G^m = 1, class = lcs length) are mathlib.

results.name: Omega subgroups Ω_r(P) = ⟨x : x^{p^r} = 1⟩
results.notes: Lives outside the chapter tree in OddOrder/GroupTheory/OmegaSubgroup.lean (header cites Isaacs Ch.4 §4D / Thm 4.36 as motivation). General r supported.

units.summary: Isaacs Ch.4 (Commutators, results 4.1-4.38 + Hall-Witt identity) is essentially complete: 30 of 39 surveyed items are fully formalized sorry-free in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch04_Commutators/Main/{CommutatorBasics,ThreeSubgroups,ThreeSubgroupsCoprime,BaerTrick,ChainNilpotent}.lean, 3 are pure mathlib (4.2, 4.9 three-subgroups, Hall-Witt), and several are formalized STRONGER than the book (4.4/4.8 generalized from p-groups to arbitrary class-≤2 groups, 4.33 under p-separable instead of p-solvable, 4.13 strictly stronger than mathlib's derived_le_lower_central). The chapter's [G,A] machinery is factored differently from the book: actionCommutator (φ : A →* MulAut G) with a parallel ⁅inl G, inr A⁆ view in the semidirect product Γ = G ⋊[φ] A, and iterated chains [G,A,...,A] as iterCommutator on inl/inr ranges. The one real gap is the Mann/Ishikawa cluster 4.14-4.19 (M(G) generated by small conjugacy classes, class ≤ 3/≤ 4 bounds): deliberately skipped during the FT phase (zero BG/Peterfalvi consumers, per an explicit skip comment in ThreeSubgroups.lean); of it only 4.16 exists, in p-group form as centralizer_eq_self_of_maximal_abelian_normal in GroupTheory/CriticalSubgroup.lean (book states nilpotent G) — the whole cluster is roughly one M-sized job whose core is the counting lemma 4.17. Minor deviations: 4.12 covers only left-associated element commutators (arbitrary-bracketing subgroup form is an S job from the already-proved 4.11), 4.29 retains a solvability hypothesis the printed statement omits (S to close via the existing cyclic/Sylow restriction machinery), and 4.6 carries [Finite G] where the book is general. Supporting definitions Ω_r(P) and G^∞ are formalized (OmegaSubgroup.lean, ChainNilpotent.lean); M(G) is not. Slim verification pass: no status changed — all flagged missing/partial labels (4.12, M(G) def, 4.14, 4.15, 4.17, 4.18, 4.19) were confirmed by fresh multi-format number and descriptive-name greps across OddOrder/ (the only M(G)/Mann hits are the skip comment and unrelated Schur-multiplier and BG-numbered 4.15/4.17 results; Coq has no Mann analog), 4.16's p-group specialization was confirmed by reading the statement (IsPGroup p P hypothesis at CriticalSubgroup.lean:166), and the three most load-bearing formalized items 4.28, 4.31, 4.36 were re-read at statement level and confirmed at full book strength.
units.unit: Isaacs Ch.4 Commutators (references/isaacs/finite-group-theory.mmd lines 2124-2799)

results.name: Transfer map independent of choice of transversal

results.name: p ∣ |G' ∩ Z(G)| implies Sylow p-subgroup nonabelian
results.notes: OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch05_Transfer/Basic.lean. Full book strength ([Finite G], p ∣ Nat.card (commutator G ⊓ center G) → ¬IsMulCommutative P). Sorry-free.

results.name: Z ≤ Z(Γ)∩Γ' implies Sylow p of Γ/Z noncyclic for p ∣ |Z| (Schur multiplier corollary)
results.notes: VERIFIED partial (slim pass): only the weak form is proved — Sylow_p(Γ) nonabelian (Basic.lean:198-213; docstring explicitly says ここでは前段の Sylow_p(Γ) 非可換のみ実装). The book's conclusion that Sylow p of the QUOTIENT Γ/Z is noncyclic is absent; repo-wide grep for quotient-Sylow-noncyclic / Schur-multiplier content found nothing (Ch06 noncyclic lemmas are unrelated 2-group structure). Docstring sketches the missing route via MonoidHom.isMulCommutative_of_isCyclic_of_ker_le_center + P∩Z ≤ Z(P).

results.name: Transfer-evaluation lemma (orbit decomposition of pretransfer)
results.notes: Mathlib expresses V(g) as a product over ⟨g⟩-orbits on G/H with exponents = orbit sizes (minimalPeriod), which is parts (a)(b)(c); (d) (n_t ∣ o(g)) is inherent since minimalPeriod divides orderOf. Numbered '5b. Lemma' in the Nougat OCR but it is Lemma 5.5 (proof header says 'Proof of Lemma 5.5').

results.name: Transfer to central subgroup of index n is g ↦ g^n (and is a homomorphism)
results.notes: Transfer.lean:232-239: transferCenterPow G : G →* center G with coe = g ^ (center G).index. Book states it for any central subgroup Z of finite index; mathlib states it for Z(G) itself, and the repo reproves the general central-element pattern inline where needed (h_key + transfer_eq_pow in 5.3/5.18 proofs). Content fully available.

results.name: Schur: Z(G) of finite index implies G' finite
results.notes: Basic.lean. Exact book statement, derived from repo 5.8 (finitely many commutators) + mathlib's Schreier-route bound card_commutator_le_of_finite_commutatorSet (a strengthened Schur with explicit bound, hypothesis Finite (commutatorSet G)). Sorry-free.

results.name: Every commutator is [s,t] for transversal representatives of Z(G); finitely many commutators if index finite
results.notes: Stated via quotient-representative form (Quotient.out of G⧸Z(G)) instead of an explicit right transversal — equivalent content, avoids a transversal bridge API. Both halves of the book statement present.

results.name: |G:Z(G)| = n implies n-th power of every commutator (indeed every element of G') is 1
results.notes: Formalized in the stronger subgroup form (every g ∈ commutator G) plus the literal commutator form. Uses mathlib transferCenterPow.

results.name: Dietzmann: finite conjugation-closed X of bounded exponent generates a finite subgroup
results.notes: VERIFIED missing (slim pass): Basic.lean:226-228 docstring says 形式化保留 (deferred); fresh grep of Mathlib/** for Dietzmann empty; repo-wide grep for conjugation-closed / finitely-many-conjugates finite-generation content finds only unrelated Peterfalvi coherence-family and BG conjugation-action material. Repo deliberately bypassed it: Schur 5.7 is obtained via mathlib's closureCommutatorRepresentatives/Schreier route, so Dietzmann is not needed downstream. Self-contained combinatorial proof; the product-rewriting/minimality argument over lists is fiddly in Lean, est. 1-3 days.

results.name: Hall subgroup H: v(H) = v(G), i.e. |H : H∩ker v| = |G : ker v|
results.notes: Stated in the equivalent form ker(transfer ϕ) ⊔ H = ⊤ (with ker normal this is exactly v(H)=v(G) by the second iso theorem), and GENERALIZED from target H/H' to any finite abelian A with |A| ∣ |H| — stronger than book. π-Hall via repo IsHallSubgroup.

results.name: N_G(P) controls G-fusion in C_G(P) (Burnside fusion argument)
results.notes: Element form: x,y ∈ C_G(P) G-conjugate ⇒ ∃ n ∈ N_G(P) conjugating x to y. Full book strength; sorry-free. Not in mathlib.

results.name: Burnside normal p-complement theorem (P ≤ Z(N_G(P)))
results.notes: [critic 補正] repo 自身が hasNormalPComplement_of_sylow_normalizer_le_centralizer (Ch05_Transfer/Basic.lean:690, Isaacs 5.13 docstring 付き) を保持し BG Thm 1.18 対応表もこれを指す。mathlib ker_transferSylow_isComplement' も存在 (両方 formalized 扱い)。

results.name: Cyclic Sylow p-subgroup for the smallest prime divisor has a normal p-complement
results.notes: Transfer.lean:339ff, verified: 'A cyclic Sylow subgroup for the smallest prime has a normal complement.'

results.name: All Sylow subgroups cyclic implies solvable (Z-groups solvable)
results.notes: Mathlib/GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/ZGroup.lean instance [Finite G] [IsZGroup G] : IsSolvable G, verified.

results.name: Z-group structure: G' and G/G' cyclic with coprime orders (metacyclic)
results.notes: All four pieces verified in ZGroup.lean (lines 136,146,284,319); the semidirect-product characterization even exceeds the book statement.

results.name: Cyclic Sylow p-subgroup: p divides at most one of |G'| and |G:G'|
results.notes: Basic.lean, statement ¬p ∣ Nat.card (commutator G) ∨ ¬p ∣ (commutator G).index — exact book strength. Proof via Schur-Zassenhaus + Ch.4 Fitting decomposition adapter + Burnside, sorry-free. (Name violates the repo no-number naming convention, cosmetic only.)

results.name: Abelian Sylow P: G' ∩ P ∩ Z(N_G(P)) = 1
results.notes: Strong form in element shape (x ∈ commutator G, x ∈ P, x commutes with all of N_G(P) ⇒ x = 1) — exactly the book's triple-intersection triviality. Sorry-free.

results.name: Sylow 2-subgroup a direct product of cyclics with one strictly largest ⇒ G not simple
results.notes: Only the special case B = ⊥ (Sylow 2-subgroup itself cyclic) is formalized; the book's general P = A × B with A strictly largest cyclic factor (via the characteristic subgroup {x^{a/2}}) is not. Docstring notes the generalization route via the same 5.18 strong form. Completing needs the direct-product decomposition bookkeeping, 1-3 days.

results.name: ker(transfer to Sylow p) = A^p(G)
results.notes: Stated for mathlib's transferFocal (transfer into P ⧸ Foc(P)) rather than the book's v into P/P'; since A^p(G) ≤ ker v ≤ ker transferFocal = A^p(G) (transfer functorial in the target), this is equivalent content. A^p(G) itself is the repo's new APrime definition (⨅ of normal K ⊇ G' with p-power index) with normal/characteristic/index-p-power API; O^p(G) likewise (OPrime) — neither in mathlib.

results.name: Focal Subgroup Theorem: Foc_G(P) = P∩G' = P∩A^p(G) = P∩ker v
results.notes: VERIFIED at full strength (slim pass): focalSubgroupTheorem (Basic.lean:1376) packages the three equalities commutator G ⊓ P = Foc ∧ APrime p G ⊓ P = Foc ∧ ker transferFocal ⊓ P = Foc, i.e. the full 4-way book statement. The G'∩P and ker legs are mathlib's GroupTheory/Focal.lean; the repo adds the A^p leg. Downstream entrypoint cited by BG as Thm 1.17. Sorry-free.

results.name: H controls G-fusion in P ⇒ H controls p-transfer (A^p(H) = H ∩ A^p(G), G/A^p(G) ≅ H/A^p(H))
results.notes: Stated in the A^p-equality form APrime p H = (APrime p G).subgroupOf H without a separate ControlsPTransfer predicate; the index equality |G:A^p(G)| = |H:A^p(H)| (⇔ the book's quotient isomorphism) is established inside the proof. Full strength.

results.name: Abelian Sylow P ⇒ N_G(P) controls p-transfer
results.notes: A^p-equality form over N_G(P); direct composition of 5.22 with 5.12. Sorry-free.

results.name: Nilpotent maximal subgroup of a finite simple group is a p-group
results.notes: VERIFIED missing (slim pass): Basic.lean:35 and :1083 both mark 5.24 as 保留 (deferred, no BG/Peterfalvi citation); greps by number, by nilpotent+maximal+simple, and by isPGroup-of-maximal descriptive guesses across OddOrder/ (incl. GroupTheory/**) find nothing — Ch07's step1_unique_maximal_containing_nilpotent is different content (Thompson §7D uniqueness step, not this Wielandt-style statement). All proof ingredients are formalized (5.12 fusion control, 5.22 A^p equality, Sylow arguments), so this is assembly work, under a day.

results.name: Normal p-complement exists iff Sylow p-subgroup controls its own fusion
results.notes: VERIFIED at full strength (slim pass): Main.lean:378 states HasNormalPComplement p G ↔ P.ControlsOwnFusion for any Sylow P; underlying predicates checked sound — HasNormalPComplement = ∃ normal N complementing EVERY Sylow p (Basic.lean:318), ControlsOwnFusion = P.ControlsFusionIn P (Main.lean:91). Both directions fully proved (the hard ⇐ via OPrime, APrime=⊤, focal theorem, lower-central-series iteration). Sorry-free.

results.name: Frobenius normal p-complement theorem (3 equivalent conditions)
results.notes: VERIFIED at full strength (slim pass): Main.lean:955 states the full iff — HasNormalPComplement p G ↔ ∀ p-subgroup X, N_G(X)/C_G(X) is a p-group ((1)⇔(3)); the (1)⇒(2) and (2)⇒(3) links are separate lemmas (5.27), so the full 3-way equivalence is recoverable. Not in mathlib. Plus the pre-5.29 criterion (q-subgroups normalizing ⇒ centralizing) as a packaged entry point. Sorry-free.

results.name: Frobenius easy implications (1)⇒(2)⇒(3)
results.notes: Part 1 is the strong form (every subgroup of a p-nilpotent group is p-nilpotent), as in the book's proof. Sorry-free.

results.name: Key Frobenius lemma: under (3), any two Sylow p-subgroups conjugate by c ∈ C_G(P∩Q)
results.notes: Main.lean:674, complete strong-induction proof (Steps 1-11 read in full: normalizers-grow, N=SC decomposition, double IH, c = x·y⁻¹·z assembly). The old '骨格のみ' docstring note is stale — body is fully proved, sorry-free.

results.name: No prime divisor q of m dividing any p^e−1 (e ≤ a) ⇒ normal p-complement
results.notes: Exact book hypotheses (|G| = p^a·m, p ∤ m, no q ∣ m divides p^e−1 for 1 ≤ e ≤ a). Orbit-counting helpers included. Sorry-free.

results.name: p odd, all elements of order p central ⇒ normal p-complement
results.notes: Via Frobenius criterion + Isaacs Thm 4.36 (Ch.4). Exact book strength (p ≠ 2, orderOf g = p → g ∈ center). The unnumbered p=2/x⁴=1 remark after 5.30 is not formalized (book leaves it as a remark).

results.name: Pretransfer and transfer map V, v : G → H/H'
results.notes: Mathlib works with left transversals and an arbitrary abelian target ϕ : H →* A; book's H/H' is the ϕ = Abelianization.of instance.

results.name: Focal subgroup Foc_G(H)
results.notes: Mathlib/GroupTheory/Focal.lean (complete file with API: normality in H, ≤ commutator, transfer surjectivity, iso theorem).

results.name: A^p(G) and O^p(G) with basic API (normal, characteristic, p-power index, A^p = G'O^p analog)
results.notes: Not in mathlib; defined as infima of the defining normal-subgroup families with full supporting API. The in-text identity A^p(G) = G'·O^p(G) is not stated as a standalone lemma but its uses are covered by APrime_le/commutator_le_APrime + index lemmas.

units.summary: Isaacs Ch.5 is one of the most completely covered units in the repo: of the 30 numbered results, 9 are fully covered by mathlib (transfer construction 5.1/5.2, transfer-evaluation 5.5, central transfer 5.6, Burnside 5.13, cyclic-Sylow-smallest-prime 5.14, and the whole Z-group cluster 5.15/5.16, plus the focal-subgroup definitional layer in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Focal.lean), and 17 more are formalized sorry-free at full book strength in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch05_Transfer/{Basic,Main}.lean — including the entire Frobenius normal p-complement section 5.25-5.30 with the hard Lemma 5.28 fully proved (its '骨格のみ' docstring is stale). The formalization is factored differently from the book in places, always soundly: 5.20-5.23 are stated via a new A^p(G)/O^p(G) (APrime/OPrime) infimum API and mathlib's transferFocal (target P⧸Foc instead of P/P'), and 5.11 is generalized to arbitrary abelian transfer targets. Real gaps are exactly four: Dietzmann's theorem 5.10 (missing, deliberately bypassed since mathlib's Schreier route proves Schur 5.7 without it; M), the nilpotent-maximal-subgroup theorem 5.24 (missing but all ingredients present; S), the quotient-Sylow-noncyclic half of Cor 5.4 (partial; S), and Cor 5.19 which is proved only for cyclic Sylow 2-subgroups instead of the book's direct-product-with-strict-largest-factor form (specialized; M). Surprise findings: mathlib now has a complete Focal Subgroup Theorem file (commutator_inf_eq_focalSubgroup) that the repo builds on rather than duplicating, and the repo's Frobenius theorem 5.26 plus the 5.25 fusion criterion are substantial mathlib-absent developments that BG Ch.1 cites directly (Thm 1.17/1.18 entrypoints). Slim verification pass: no labels changed — the missing/partial flags on Cor 5.4, Thm 5.10, and Thm 5.24 were each confirmed by number-citation and descriptive-content greps across OddOrder/ (including GroupTheory/** and other book trees; the only nilpotent-maximal hit, Ch07's step1_unique_maximal_containing_nilpotent, is different content), and the load-bearing formalized statements 5.21, 5.25, and 5.26 were read in source and confirmed at full book strength with sound underlying predicates.

units.unit: Isaacs, Finite Group Theory, Ch.6 Frobenius Actions (results 6.1-6.24; mmd lines 3313-3713)
units.summary: Isaacs Ch.6 is one of the most thoroughly formalized Isaacs chapters: 19 of 24 numbered results are fully formalized sorry-free, mostly in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch06_FrobeniusActions/ (7 files, ~8.5k lines), and nothing in the chapter is in mathlib (Frobenius actions/groups are a from-scratch repo implementation, with only DihedralGroup/QuaternionGroup and the IsZGroup API reused). The formalization is frequently STRONGER or differently factored than the book: 6.11-6.14 conclude explicit MulEquiv classifications onto concrete D/Q/SD groups; 6.23 is covered by the strictly stronger Thm 7.1 (fully proved in Ch07_ThompsonSubgroup); 6.18 factors through IsZGroup + mathlib; the repo adds extra-book API (IsFrobeniusGroup transport across isomorphisms, conjugate complements, the 2|A|+1 ≤ |N| bound, and Huppert V.8.18(b) normality in OddComplement.lean); 6.22 lives in the BG tree as BG Thm 3.7 in a prime-order-complement pair form (formalized_specialized). The genuine gaps are: Thm 6.7 (kernel-side complement existence via Schur-Zassenhaus, S — all tools present), the chapter's headline Thm 6.24 (Frobenius kernels nilpotent, M — every ingredient including Thompson 7.1 is already proved, only the induction glue is missing), plus three small statement-level gaps: the standalone (2)=>(1) direction of Thm 6.4, the composed even-case statement of Cor 6.17, and the uniqueness (vs. proved normality) conclusion of Thm 6.19 (each S). Note Main.lean's in-file status table is stale (it claims 6B/6C largely undone while 6.8-6.21 are in fact formalized). Slim verification pass: all five flagged labels (6.4/6.17/6.19 partial, 6.7/6.24 missing) were confirmed after number- and content-based refutation greps across OddOrder/GroupTheory and the BG tree, and three load-bearing formalized results (6.11, 6.21, and 6.23-via-7.1) were read in source and confirmed at full book strength, so no statuses changed; only verification evidence was added to notes (e.g. 6.4's (1)⇒(4) is proved despite a stale 'deferred' module docstring, and 6.19's uniqueness name exists only in a docstring).

units.unit: Isaacs Ch.7 The Thompson Subgroup
units.summary: Isaacs Ch.7 is COMPLETELY formalized: all 8 numbered results (Thm 7.1, Lem 7.2-7.4, Thm 7.5-7.6, Lem 7.7, Thm 7.8) plus the J(P)/E(P) definition have sorry-free Lean proofs at full book strength, spread across ~12k lines in OddOrder/Isaacs/Ch07_ThompsonSubgroup/ (13 files) plus the shared OddOrder/GroupTheory/ThompsonSubgroup.lean. Two results are formalized STRONGER than the book: Lem 7.4 holds over any field of characteristic ≠ 2 (book: finite fields of odd order), and Thm 7.5/7.6 assume only p-separability (IsPiSeparable {p}) where the book assumes p-solvability. The only hypothesis deviations are epsilon-trivial (Lem 7.7 adds P ≠ ⊥; Thm 7.8 adds p ≠ q, whose excluded case is a p-group). Main caution for future readers: many docstrings still call proof steps 'local axioms' from earlier scaffolding phases, but a repo-wide grep confirms zero actual axiom declarations and zero sorries in the chapter — every step lemma (including the Burnside 9-step core noNonsolvableSimplePaQb) is a proved theorem. Burnside p^a q^b is absent from mathlib, so this chapter's character-free proof is genuinely new formalized content.

units.summary: Isaacs Ch.8 (Permutation Groups, results 8.1–8.44) has no repo formalization at all — no Ch08 directory exists, nothing in OddOrder/GroupTheory covers it, and the repo never uses mathlib's IsBlock/IsPreprimitive/IsMultiplyPretransitive API (the BG §16 ConjSharplyTransitiveOn machinery and the sorried Peterfalvi Suzuki appendix, whose doubly-transitive hypotheses are opaque scaffold Props that this chapter's material would eventually discharge, are the only adjacent things). The surprise is how much mathlib now covers at full strength or stronger: all of the blocks/primitivity theory (8.11–8.16), both Jordan theorems including the general multiple-primitivity form (8.17–8.22, Chambert-Loir's Jordan.lean/MultipleTransitivity.lean/MultiplePrimitivity.lean), Iwasawa's criterion (8.30), A_n simplicity for general n ≥ 5 plus the S_n normal-subgroup classification (8.27–8.28, added 2026-04, making the repo's pre-formalization note stale), and the SL/PSL projective-space action with faithfulness, 2-transitivity, primitivity, and the degree formula (8.3, 8.29) — 19 of 44 results are status mathlib. The genuine gaps are: the §8A automorphism-action cluster (8.4–8.10, including the regular-normal-subgroup lemma 8.5 and the Passman–Isaacs half-transitive theorem 8.9), the p-cycle Jordan theorem 8.23 (an explicit proof_wanted in mathlib) with its helpers 8.24–8.25, Bochert's theorem 8.26, the PSL simplicity chain 8.31–8.33 (mathlib has transvection Gaussian elimination and SL(2) commutator lemmas but no generation/perfectness/simplicity statements — a prime upstream candidate), and the entire §8D orbital/subdegree/common-divisor-graph theory 8.34–8.44, for which mathlib has no concepts at all. Total new work is roughly: a handful of S items assembling existing mathlib pieces, plus four M-sized clusters (half-transitive, p-cycle+Bochert, PSL simplicity, §8D orbital theory). Slim verification pass: all 25 flagged missing labels were confirmed after refutation attempts (book-number greps for Isaacs 8.x in multiple formats plus descriptive-name greps — transvection, Bochert, Passman, half-transitive, subdegree, orbital, PSL/GL simplicity, semidirect/sharply/regular transitivity, three-cycle, elementary-abelian cover — across all OddOrder trees and notes; the only transvection content is BG §10's unrelated GL(2,p) lemma), and the load-bearing mathlib labels 8.2 (verified iff-form statement by Read), 8.17/8.19, 8.23 proof_wanted (Jordan.lean:462), 8.27, and 8.30 were verified against mathlib source; no status changed.

units.unit: Isaacs Ch.9 More on Subnormality (F*(G), automorphism tower, Thompson–Wielandt, Bartels)
units.summary: Isaacs Ch.9 is essentially unformalized: all 31 numbered results (9.1–9.31) lack full-strength Lean counterparts, and none of the chapter's signature concepts (quasisimple, component, layer E(G), semisimple group, F*(G), automorphism tower, subnormal closure, strong conjugacy) exist in the repo or in mathlib. This is a documented deliberate skip — notes/isaacs/ch09_more_subnormality.md records a 2026-05-23 audit showing zero uses of any Ch.9 concept in BG or Peterfalvi (FT's group is ultimately solvable, where F*=F), and fresh greps confirm the repo state matches that audit. The chapter is not entirely from scratch, though: the solvable specialization of Bender's Thm 9.8 is fully proved as BG Prop 1.3 (centralizer_fitting_le_fitting), and scattered infrastructure lowers entry costs — socle (Ch02), Thm 2.6 (the hub cited 5x by §9A proofs), S^∞ as lowerCentralSeriesInfty (Ch04), O^p as OPrime (Ch05), the n!-theorem (Ch01), ker(conjNormal)=centralizer and a |G/C| ≤ |Aut C| embedding (Ch06/Ch07), plus mathlib's IsSubnormal/IsPerfect/MulAut.conj. Surprises: Lemma 9.31 (Sylow ∩ subnormal) is missing even from mathlib despite being a basic general fact, and the Nougat-missing page 302 was verified against the PDF to contain only §9D definitions, so the enumeration is complete. Effort estimates are marginal in document order (each assumes earlier chapter results exist); the natural clusters are §9A F*-theory (~1 wk), §9B tower (~1-1.5 wk), §9C Thompson–Wielandt (~3-4 days on top of A+B), §9D Bartels (~1-1.5 wk). Slim verification pass: all flagged missing/partial labels and the Thm 9.8 specialization (statement read) were confirmed; the only substantive correction is to Lem 9.6's notes — BG Lem 1.1 (isMinimalNormal_le_fitting_and_isElementaryAbelian) does prove 'minimal normal ⟹ elementary abelian' for solvable G at full strength, contrary to the earlier note — plus minor path/name enrichments (ChainNilpotent.lean lives under Main/, two additional private conjNormal-kernel variants for 9.11).
