results.notes: Three-line assembly from 10.1 + 10.14 + 10.15 once those exist. NOT the same as the repo's 'Huppert' results: BG Prop 4.11 / Thm 4.12 (S04c_Prop411.lean, S04b_Thm412.lean) are Endliche Gruppen I Satz III.11.6/III.13.7, and Peterfalvi/Appendices/Huppert.lean is the doubly-transitive Huppert - all different theorems (re-verified by grepping all Huppert hits).

results.name: Metacyclic groups are closed under quotients (a) and subgroups (b)
results.notes: (b) is formalized sorry-free in OddOrder/GroupTheory/IsMetacyclic.lean at full generality; (a) quotient closure has no Lean counterpart (verified: file has exactly of_isCyclic, isCyclic_commutator, subgroup, isSolvable; 149 lines). mathlib has no metacyclic API at all. Remaining work is easy.

results.name: For p > 2, C_p wr C_p is not a homomorphic image of a metacyclic group
results.notes: Short given 10.13(a) and 10.3(b); repo already has IsMetacyclic.isCyclic_commutator, the key ingredient. Verified missing.

results.name: P normal Sylow, nonabelian metacyclic, p > 2 implies p divides |N:N'|
results.notes: Induction on |P| using Maschke (10.17, formalized), Isaacs Thm 4.8(a) (formalized, CommutatorBasics.lean:1495) and Thm 6.11 (unique-subgroup-of-order-p, available via isCyclic_of_subgroups_card_prime_unique in Ch06). All prerequisites exist; body is a solid page of argument. Verified missing.

results.name: Maschke, group form: K acts on V = U x W, U abelian K-invariant, u -> u^m bijective on U, then a K-invariant complement N with V = U x N exists
results.notes: The book's general form (V an arbitrary group, U possibly infinite with bijective m-power map) has no Lean counterpart. mathlib's Maschke (Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Maschke.lean) is the module version; the repo's OperatorMaschke.lean proves only the elementary-abelian coprime corollary (= 10.17) directly via modules, bypassing 10.16. Also checked OddOrder/GroupTheory/AInvariantComplement.lean — that is invariant Schur-Zassenhaus (coprime Hall complement), a different theorem. Verified missing.

results.name: Maschke for coprime automorphism action on an elementary abelian p-group: every invariant subgroup has an invariant complement
results.notes: OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/OperatorMaschke.lean:287, sorry-free. Statement re-read and confirmed at full book strength: phi : A ->* MulAut E, IsElementaryAbelian p E, Coprime |A| |E| (equivalent to book's p not dividing |K| since E is a p-group), invariant U gives invariant W with U inf W = bot and U sup W = top. Extra hypotheses [Finite E] (Isaacs's standing finiteness convention) and p | Nat.card E (excludes only the trivial E, where the book statement is vacuous). Proved via mathlib representation invtSubmodule machinery, not via 10.16.

results.name: Principal ideal theorem (Furtwangler): the transfer G -> G'/G'' is trivial
results.notes: Immediate corollary of 10.25; the real cost is the S10C group-ring chain 10.19-10.27. Absent from mathlib (no group-ring augmentation-ideal transfer theory). Verified: zero hits for Furtwangler/principal-ideal; all repo 'augmentation' hits are character-theory averaging idempotents (WielandtKernelFPF, CenterSimplesOrbit), unrelated. Flagged in notes/meta/ch08_10_audit_2026_05_23.md as a HIGH-value mathlib upstream candidate (class field theory).

results.name: The augmentation ideal Delta(G) of Z[G] has Z-basis {g - 1 : g /= 1}
results.notes: No Delta(G) construct anywhere in repo (verified; MonoidAlgebra is used only for character theory); straightforward over mathlib MonoidAlgebra/Finsupp basis API.

results.name: G/G' isomorphic to Delta(G)/Delta(G)^2 via g -> (g-1)
results.notes: Standard two-directional construction (homomorphism phi plus the Z-basis-defined theta); no counterpart in repo or mathlib. Verified missing.

results.name: Components of elements of Delta(K)Delta(G) w.r.t. a transversal lie in Delta(K), with component sum in Delta(K)^2
results.notes: Generator-wise computation once the t-component additive maps are defined. Verified missing.

results.name: Delta(K)^2 = Delta(K)Delta(G) inter Delta(K) = Delta(K)Delta(G) inter Z[K]
results.notes: Immediate from 10.21. Verified missing.

results.name: Image of Delta(K) in Delta(G)/Delta(K)Delta(G) is isomorphic to K/K'
results.notes: Composition of 10.22 with 10.20 applied to K. Verified missing.

results.name: For K normal in G, the transfer image v(G) is isomorphic to Xi(Delta(G)-bar), Xi = left multiplication by a transversal sum
results.notes: The bridge between mathlib's MonoidHom.transfer and the group-ring model; requires the pretransfer computation mod Delta(K)Delta(G). Verified missing.

results.name: For G' <= K <= G, v(g)^{|K:G'|} = 1 for the transfer v : G -> K/K'
results.notes: Assembly of 10.24 + 10.26 + 10.27 with the |A:UA| = |G:G'| index computation; generalizes 10.18. Verified missing.

results.name: Module over commutative ring: |A : UA| = m finite implies some r in R with rA = 0 and r = m*1 mod U
results.notes: Classical-adjoint determinant trick; mathlib has Matrix.adjugate and adjugate_mul plus Nakayama-style relatives (Submodule.exists_sub_one_mem_and_smul_eq_zero_of_fg_of_le_smul) but not this exact statement. Verified missing in repo.

results.name: epsilon annihilating Delta(G)-bar has augmentation m divisible by |G:K|, and (m/|G:K|) Xi = 0
results.notes: Component analysis using 10.21 plus transitivity of the dot action on the transversal. Verified missing.

results.name: Alperin-Kuo: g^{|G : G' inter Z(G)|} = 1 for all g in G
results.notes: Short given 10.8 + 10.18 + mathlib MonoidHom.transferCenterPow (= Isaacs 5.6, verified present in pinned mathlib Transfer.lean). Verified: zero Alperin/Kuo hits in repo. Repo's nearby-looking Ch05 lemmas (pow_index_center_eq_one_of_mem_commutator = Isaacs Cor 5.9) are a different result.

units.summary: Isaacs Ch.10 (results 10.1-10.28) is almost entirely unformalized: of 28 numbered results, only Corollary 10.17 is fully formalized (as the operator-Maschke theorem exists_aInvariant_complement_of_isElementaryAbelian in OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/OperatorMaschke.lean, built for BG's needs) and Lemma 10.13 is half done (subgroup closure of metacyclic in OddOrder/GroupTheory/IsMetacyclic.lean; quotient closure missing). All three headline clusters are missing: Yoshida's theorem 10.1 with its wreath-recognition and transfer chain (10.3-10.11, including transitivity of transfer 10.8 and Mackey transfer 10.10, both absent from mathlib as well), Huppert's metacyclic-Sylow theorem 10.12/10.15, and the entire section-10C group-ring machinery culminating in the principal ideal theorem 10.18 and Alperin-Kuo 10.28. This matches the chapter's zero forward citations from BG/Peterfalvi (repo grep hits for 'Theorem 10.x' are all BG section 10, a different book); the repo's three other 'Huppert' results (BG 4.11/4.12, Peterfalvi appendix) are distinct theorems and must not be confused with 10.12. Two mitigating surprises: mathlib's RegularWreathProduct.lean (Sylow.mulEquivIteratedWreathProduct) substantially cheapens the C_p wr C_p recognition step of 10.4, and the chapter's Isaacs-internal prerequisites (Thm 4.7, 4.8(a), 6.11, Ch.5 transfer/focal API) are already formalized, so section 10A+10B is mostly assembly-hard rather than prerequisite-blocked; section 10C needs a new augmentation-ideal Delta(G) API from scratch (a good future mathlib upstream candidate). Slim verification pass: refutation greps (wreath/pretransfer/Mackey-transfer/augmentation-ideal/Furtwangler/Alperin-Kuo/metacyclic-quotient, plus descriptive-name and cross-tree searches over GroupTheory/Algebra/BG/Peterfalvi and pinned mathlib) confirmed every flagged missing/partial label with no upgrades; the 10.17 Lean statement was re-read and confirmed at full book strength, and 10.13's file was confirmed to contain subgroup closure but no quotient closure.
units.unit: Isaacs Ch.10 More Transfer Theory

results.name: HK is a subgroup iff HK = KH (permutable subgroups)
results.notes: VERIFIED partial: forward direction (HK=KH => ↑(H⊔K) = HK as sets) is proved in the repo but private to Ch02 Basic.lean (used for Isaacs Thm 2.8); mathlib Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Pointwise.lean (read directly) covers only the normalizer/normal special cases (set_mul_normalizer_comm, coe_mul_of_left/right_le_normalizer, mul_normal, normal_mul). The converse (HK subgroup => HK=KH) is stated nowhere in repo or mathlib. Easy: publicize the repo lemma and add the 3-line converse.

results.name: Product formula |HK|·|H∩K| = |H|·|K|
results.notes: VERIFIED at full book strength by reading the statement: Nat.card (↑H * ↑K : Set G) * Nat.card ↥(H ⊓ K) = Nat.card H * Nat.card K, for arbitrary subgroups with HK the set product (not assumed a subgroup) — multiplicative form avoids division and also holds for infinite groups (both sides 0). Flagged in-file as a mathlib-upstream candidate (target Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coset/Card.lean). mathlib itself only has relIndex partial analogues.

results.name: Dedekind's lemma: H ≤ U => HK ∩ U = H(K ∩ U)
results.notes: Subgroup.mul_inf_assoc (A ≤ C => ↑A * ↑(B ⊓ C) = ↑A * ↑B ∩ C; verified present at Algebra/Group/Subgroup/Pointwise.lean:306) is exactly X.3 at set level; inf_mul_assoc is the mirror. Repo additionally has normal-hypothesis lattice (join) forms.

results.name: Direct-diamond correspondence: X ↦ X∩K injects {X : H≤X≤HK} into {W : D≤W≤K}, image = {W : WH=HW}
results.notes: VERIFIED missing: re-grepped repo for 'diamond', interval/coset correspondence patterns, and all OrderIso uses in OddOrder (all are isCoatom_iff transport along MulAut.conj or module-lattice isos — none is this statement); mathlib's MapSubtype.orderIso and comapMk'OrderIso are different statements. Short order-theoretic derivation from X.1 + X.3; never needed on the FT path.

results.name: Frattini subgroup = set of nongenerators
results.notes: VERIFIED partial by reading mathlib GroupTheory/Frattini.lean and Order/Radical.lean in full: forward direction is frattini_nongenerating (K ⊔ Φ(G) = ⊤ => K = ⊤, equivalent to the book's ⟨X∪Φ⟩<G form; repo has a finite specialization eq_top_of_sup_frattini_eq_top in BG/S01_Solvable.lean). The element-level converse (u a nongenerator => u ∈ Φ(G)) exists in neither mathlib nor the repo (repo mem_frattini hits are unrelated p-group power/commutator lemmas); it is a 10-line coatom argument.

results.name: Subgroups of cyclic groups: H = ⟨g^m⟩ with m minimal, m divides every n with g^n ∈ H; all subgroups cyclic
results.notes: Cyclicity of subgroups is a mathlib instance; the generator/divisibility bookkeeping is covered by the zpowers/orderOf API (Nat.card_zpowers etc.). Not stated as one literal theorem but fully covered.

results.name: Finite cyclic group of order n has exactly one subgroup of each order d ∣ n, and no others
lean_names: cyclic_subgroup_eq_of_card_eq (OddOrder/BG/Ch3_MaximalSubgroups/S10_LocalLemmasCore.lean:63, uniqueness for arbitrary equal card)
results.notes: VERIFIED by reading both statements. Factored differently from the book: existence of the order-d subgroup is mathlib (ker of powMonoidHom d has card gcd(d,n) = d when d∣n); uniqueness is the repo lemma cyclic_subgroup_eq_of_card_eq ([Finite C] [IsCyclic C], Nat.card H₁ = Nat.card H₂ => H₁ = H₂ — full generality, proof routes both through the powMonoidHom kernel). Repo docstring itself notes a duplicate in S10_BetaRadical to be hoisted.

results.name: Lagrange: cosets partition G, all of size |H|; |H| divides |G| and |G|/|H| = |G:H|
results.notes: Parts (a)-(c) are the coset API in Mathlib/GroupTheory/Coset/Basic.lean (leftCosetEquivSubgroup, QuotientGroup.leftRel/eq); (d) verified as card_subgroup_dvd_card + card_eq_card_quotient_mul_card_subgroup.

results.name: o(g) divides |G| for finite G
Index multiplicativity: H ≤ K ≤ G => |G:H| = |G:K||K:H|
results.notes: mathlib version (relIndex K * K.index = H.index, verified at GroupTheory/Index.lean:107) holds for arbitrary groups, stronger than the book's finite statement.

results.name: |K : H∩K| ≤ |G:H|, with equality iff HK = G
results.notes: VERIFIED partial: the inequality is mathlib-derivable via relIndex_le_of_le_right (verified at Index.lean:391; note it carries a relIndex ≠ 0 side hypothesis, harmless in the finite case) — this exact derivation appears in repo Isaacs/Ch06 Lemma615.lean:397. The equality-iff-HK=G clause is stated nowhere in repo or mathlib; it follows in a few lines from the repo's X.2 product formula.

results.name: Coprime indices |G:H|, |G:K| => HK = G
results.notes: VERIFIED partial by reading the statement: the join form (Nat.Coprime H.index K.index => H ⊔ K = ⊤) is formalized sorry-free and widely cited (Ch05 Transfer, BG S12). The book's stronger set-product form (every g = hk, i.e. ↑H * ↑K = univ) is stated nowhere in repo or mathlib (repo set-product-univ hits are all IsComplement' constructions); it follows from the counting in X.2 + X.11. mathlib has only the card-coprime disjointness lemma (disjoint_of_coprime_natCard), not the index-coprime supremum.

results.name: Two cyclic groups of the same finite order are isomorphic (generator ↦ generator)
Aut of a cyclic group is abelian; |Aut(G)| = φ(|G|) for finite cyclic G
results.notes: mulAutMulEquiv : MulAut G ≃* (ZMod (Nat.card G))ˣ gives commutativity (target is a CommGroup) including the infinite case (ZMod 0 = ℤ); card_mulAut is the totient count.

results.name: Characteristic subgroup of a normal subgroup is normal
results.notes: Stated as: N ⊴ G, K ≤ N characteristic => (K.map N.subtype).Normal — full book strength.

results.name: Normality TFAE: H ⊴ G iff Hx = xH iff right cosets are left cosets iff (Hx)(Hy) = Hxy iff cosets closed under multiplication
results.notes: (1)↔(2)/(3)/(4) is normal_iff_eq_cosets; (5)/(6) are embodied in the QuotientGroup group structure (QuotientGroup.mk_mul). Not a literal 6-way TFAE but every implication used downstream exists.

results.name: Homomorphism basics: θ(1)=1, θ(x⁻¹)=θ(x)⁻¹, ker ⊴ G, θ(x)=θ(y) iff Nx=Ny, injective iff ker=1
Homomorphism (first isomorphism) theorem: G/ker θ ≅ θ(G)
N/C theorem: C_G(H) ⊴ N_G(H) and N/C embeds in Aut(H)
results.notes: normalizerMonoidHom : normalizer H →* MulAut H with ker = centralizer; composing with quotientKerEquivRange gives the embedding. Fully in mathlib (Mathlib/GroupTheory/Subgroup/Centralizer.lean).

results.name: Second (diamond) isomorphism theorem: H∩N ⊴ H and NH/N ≅ H/(H∩N)
Correspondence theorem: subgroups of G containing ker θ biject with subgroups of θ(G); preserves index, normality, quotients
results.notes: comapMk'OrderIso is the lattice bijection (stated for the canonical quotient; the arbitrary-surjection form follows via quotientKerEquivOfSurjective). Part (b) = index_comap_of_surjective; part (c) = Normal.comap/map + third isomorphism theorem.

results.name: Internal direct product criterion: G = M₁⋯M_r with M_i ⊴ G is direct iff (M₁⋯M_{k-1}) ∩ M_k = 1 for all k
results.notes: VERIFIED partial: mathlib packages internal direct products via iSupIndep + injectivity of noncommPiCoprod (and has the unnumbered pre-X.23 fact commute_of_normal_of_disjoint). The repo has two adjacent special cases (coprime-card normal families => iSupIndep; injectivity => iSupIndep in the commutative case) but the book's literal prefix-intersection iff-criterion is stated nowhere; deriving prefix-condition => iSupIndep is a short but genuine argument.

results.name: An internal direct product is isomorphic to the external direct product of its factors
results.notes: In mathlib's packaging the iso is MulEquiv.ofBijective (Subgroup.noncommPiCoprod hcomm) using range = ⨆ Mᵢ = ⊤ plus injectivity — exactly how Sylow.directProductOfNormal builds it (repo Isaacs Ch01 Basic.lean replays the same assembly). No single named general theorem, but given mathlib's definition of internal direct product the statement is essentially the assembly of these named pieces.

units.summary: The Isaacs appendix (pp. 325-343, results X.1-X.23, fully present in the mmd at lines 5915-6253) is the elementary-group-theory compendium, and as expected coverage is nearly total: 17 of 23 results are fully covered (14 by mathlib at full strength with verified declaration names, 3 by the repo — the product formula X.2 in OddOrder/Mathlib/Subgroup.lean, the cyclic-subgroup uniqueness X.7 in BG/S10_LocalLemmasCore, and X.12's join form in Isaacs/Ch03). The 6 remaining entries are all partial/missing on inessential clauses only: X.1's converse direction (its useful direction exists but is private in Ch02), X.4's direct-diamond bijection (missing entirely, the only wholly absent result), X.5's element-level nongenerator converse, X.11's equality-iff-HK=G clause, X.12's set-product strengthening, and X.22's literal prefix-intersection iff-criterion (mathlib factors internal direct products through iSupIndep/noncommPiCoprod instead); every gap is S-effort and none was ever needed on the FT path. Surprising finds: mathlib is stronger here than notes/meta/mathlib_coverage.md suggests — it now has Frattini nongenerating (frattini_nongenerating), the correspondence theorem as a lattice OrderIso (QuotientGroup.comapMk'OrderIso), and the N/C theorem (Subgroup.normalizerMonoidHom with computed kernel). The repo never cites appendix numbers (no 'Isaacs X.n' docstrings), so all matching was by content; OddOrder/Mathlib/Subgroup.lean is effectively the appendix's upstream-candidate home and already flags X.2 for a future mathlib PR. Closing the whole unit to 100% would be at most 2-3 days of routine work. Slim verification pass (2026-07-16): all six flagged labels (X.1/X.5/X.11/X.12/X.22 partial, X.4 missing) survived active refutation — grepped OddOrder/** (all book trees, GroupTheory, Algebra, Mathlib dirs) by citation formats and content-derived names, and read mathlib's Frattini.lean, Order/Radical.lean, Index.lean, and Subgroup/Pointwise.lean directly; the load-bearing formalized entries X.2 and X.7 were confirmed at full book strength by reading their Lean statements, so no status changed and only note-level enrichments were added (X.22 gains two repo partial-support lemmas; X.11's mathlib inequality carries a benign ≠0 side condition).

results.name: narrow p-group (no E_{p^3}, or C_R(R0)=R0×R1 with R1 cyclic)
results.notes: OddOrder/GroupTheory/NarrowPGroup.lean. First disjunct encoded as pRank R p ≤ 2 (equivalent to 'no elementary abelian subgroup of order p^3'); second disjunct matches the book (|R0|=p, R1 cyclic, R0⊓R1=⊥, C_R(R0)=R0⊔R1). Rich API in BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S05_Narrow*.lean.

results.name: TI-subset / TI-subgroup
results.notes: OddOrder/GroupTheory/TISubset.lean. IsTISubset A L: any g conjugating A into A lies in L; IsTI H is the specialization with A = H\{1}, L = N_G(H) — equivalent to the book's H ∩ H^g = 1 for g ∉ N(H).

results.name: G has p-length one (G = O_{p',p,p'}(G), including p'-groups)
results.notes: Two equivalent encodings exist: PLength.lean encodes it as p ∤ |G/O_{p',p}(G)| (the working definition used by all Lemma 1.21 transfer lemmas), S01_Solvable.lean §1G as O_{π',π,π'}(G) = ⊤. Matches the book's convention that p'-groups have p-length one.

results.name: A acts in a prime manner / regularly on G
results.notes: BG/Ch3_MaximalSubgroups/S13_PrimeAction.lean, in the subgroup-internal form the later chapters consume (C_N(g) = C_N(X) for all g ∈ X#, resp. C_N(g) = 1). Defined where first used (§13) rather than in §1; full book content.

results.name: Z-group (all Sylow subgroups cyclic)
results.notes: Mathlib/GroupTheory/SpecificGroups/ZGroup.lean, verified in the pinned mathlib. Repo uses it directly per no-wrapper policy.

results.name: solvable minimal normal subgroup lies in Z(F(G)) and is elementary abelian
results.notes: S01_FrattiniBurnside.lean, sorry-free. Conclusion is full (M ≤ F(G) ∧ M ≤ C_G(F(G)) ∧ elementary abelian = M ≤ Z(F(G))), but hypothesis is [IsSolvable G] where the book only requires M itself solvable inside an arbitrary finite G. All BG uses are inside solvable ambient groups, so the gap is only literal; generalizing is a small standalone task.

results.name: P. Hall: F(G*) = intersection of chief-factor centralizers (over 𝒟 and over 𝒟*)
results.notes: S01_FrattiniBurnside.lean, sorry-free. Factored as forward inclusion (F(G*) centralizes every chief factor of G) plus reverse inclusion (any G-normal H ≤ G* centralizing all chief factors inside F(G*) satisfies H ≤ F(G*)); together these give the book's double intersection identity, stated without an explicit intersection-set object.

results.name: P. Hall: C_G(F(G)) ≤ F(G) for finite solvable G
results.notes: S01_FrattiniBurnside.lean:195, sorry-free, full strength; statement re-verified this pass ([Group G][Finite G][IsSolvable G] ⊢ centralizer F(G) ≤ F(G)). Proved directly via a minimal-normal-not-in-F argument (not via Prop 1.2). Ambient subgroup form also available in BG/Ch2_Uniqueness/S08_CenterFittingOpcore.lean.

results.name: coprime automorphism group of solvable G acts faithfully on F(G)
results.notes: S01_FrattiniBurnside.lean, sorry-free. Stated in the equivalent kernel form: if a coprime action fixes F(G) pointwise then it is trivial on G. The book's 'faithful on F(G)' follows by restricting φ to C_A(F(G)); this is the form BG §8 consumes (also ambient form in S08_CenterFittingOpcore.lean).

results.name: A-invariant Hall theory for coprime operator groups: (a) existence, (b) embedding, (c) C_G(A)-conjugacy, (d) C_{G/H}(A) = image of C_G(A), (e) [G,A] ≤ O_π(G)
results.notes: All five parts sorry-free at full book strength; statements re-verified this pass. (a)(b)(c)(e) in S01_FrattiniBurnside.lean use [IsSolvable G] + Coprime |A| |G|, exactly the book's hypotheses (mmd L400); (a)(c) via Glauberman fixed-point lemma on the transitive G-set of Hall π-subgroups, (b) by the book's minimal-normal induction, (e) via IsComplement' K H. Only part (d) (Isaacs Cor 3.28, Ch04_Commutators/ForwardFromCh03.lean, plus subgroup form in S03h_Thm38.lean) carries the strictly weaker hypothesis IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G — more general than the book, not weaker.

results.name: coprime action decompositions: (a) G = C_G(A)[G,A], (b) [G,A,A]=[G,A], (c) [G,A,A]=1 ⇒ trivial, (d) abelian G = C_G(A) × [G,A], (e) abelian p-group + p'-A fixing order-p elements ⇒ trivial
results.notes: All five parts sorry-free, full strength (= Isaacs Lem 4.28/4.29, Thm 4.34, Cor 4.35 in Ch04_Commutators/Main/ThreeSubgroupsCoprime.lean). (b)(c) are stated in the semidirect-product Γ = G ⋊[φ] A iterCommutator form; (d) packaged as IsComplement' (internal direct product). Hypotheses use IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G, weaker than the book's.

results.name: Frattini basics: (a) nongeneration, (b) R/Φ(R) elementary abelian, (c) Φ(R)=1 iff elementary abelian, (d) Φ(R)=⟨R',x^p⟩
results.notes: All four parts sorry-free: (a) is the finite specialization of mathlib's frattini_nongenerating; (b)(c⇒)(d⊇) live in the shared OddOrder/GroupTheory/FrattiniPGroup.lean; (c⇐)(d⊆) via Isaacs Lem 4.5 in S01_Solvable.lean.

results.name: Burnside: coprime operator group centralizing R/Φ(R) centralizes the p-group R
results.notes: S01_Solvable.lean, sorry-free, full strength (operator-group form plus a single-automorphism element form used by Thm 3.6 and Lem 4.17). Proof via Isaacs Cor 3.29.

results.name: stabilizer of a normal series of a π-group: A/C_A(G) is a π-group
results.notes: S01_Solvable.lean, sorry-free. Formalized as the coprime core: a coprime operator group stabilizing a normal chain acts trivially — both the 2-step instance and the full multi-step chain version. The book's packaging ('A/C_A(G) is a π-group' for arbitrary A) is not stated literally; it follows elementwise (π'-elements act coprimely), which is exactly how §5/AppA consume it. Closing the literal gap would be a short exercise (q-element lifting).

results.name: coprime A on nilpotent G with C_G(C_G(A)) ≤ C_G(A) acts trivially
results.notes: S01_Solvable.lean, sorry-free, full strength, following the book's N_G(C)-stabilization argument via Lemma 1.9.

results.name: p odd: p'-operator group trivial on Ω₁(G) is trivial on the p-group G
results.notes: S01c_Omega1Rigidity.lean, sorry-free, full strength (plus an A-invariant-subgroup form). Independent Isaacs route isaacs_thm_4_36 also exists; engine is isPGroup_autFixerOfOrderP in GroupTheory/CriticalSubgroup.lean (Gorenstein 5.3.10).

results.name: p odd: p'-operators fixing every order-p element of C_G(E) act trivially on the p-group G
results.notes: Two independent sorry-free proofs (S01c_Omega1Rigidity.lean and S01_Solvable.lean), both full strength; rigidity input to BG Lemma 10.3.

results.name: Thompson critical subgroup: characteristic H with [H,G] ≤ Z(H), class ≤ 2, exponent p, C_{Aut G}(H) a p-group

units.unit: BG §1 Elementary Properties of Solvable Groups
units.summary: BG §1 is essentially complete: all 22 numbered results (Lem 1.1–Lem 1.22) have sorry-free Lean counterparts, spread across OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S01* + PLength* files, the Isaacs Ch03–Ch06 tree (Prop 1.5(d), 1.6(a)(b)(d)(e), Thm 1.11, 1.17, 1.18, Prop 1.16(1)), OddOrder/GroupTheory (Frattini, critical subgroup, TI, narrow), and mathlib (§1F: Cor 1.19 and Maschke are deliberately left to mathlib per the no-wrapper policy). The only genuine gap is Lemma 1.21(d) (p-length one ⇔ ⟨p-elements⟩ has a normal p-complement), which is unformalized and never consumed downstream — effort S. Three results are stated in equivalent-but-not-literal forms worth noting: Lem 1.1 assumes IsSolvable G where the book only needs M solvable, Lem 1.9 exists as the coprime chain-stabilizer engine rather than the 'A/C_A(G) is a π-group' packaging, and Prop 1.15(a) is stated as C_G(O_{p',p}) ≤ O_{p',p} / its O_{p'}=1 specialization rather than via a Sylow subgroup T of O_{p',p}(G) (a 5-line corollary of formalized pieces). In several places the formalization is stronger than the book: Prop 1.16 works for any coprime noncyclic abelian A (book: p-group on p'-group), Hall–Higman is proved in general π-separable form with no O_{π'}=1 hypothesis, the Isaacs-side coprime-action lemmas (Prop 1.5(d), Prop 1.6) need only IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G, and Lemma 1.21 has an extra dual transfer lemma. All §1 preamble definitions (narrow, TI-subset, p-length one, prime/regular manner, Z-group) are formalized or covered by mathlib. Verification pass: confirmed the Lem 1.21 partial label by refutation attempts against the Coq analog p_elt_gen_length1 (no p-element-generated-subgroup/O^{p'} content anywhere in the repo; OpResidual.lean is opPi, not the residual); re-read and confirmed full book strength for the load-bearing Prop 1.3, Prop 1.5, and Thm 1.13 statements, correcting only the Prop 1.5 note (parts (a)(b)(c)(e) use exactly the book's IsSolvable G hypothesis; only part (d) has the more general IsSolvable A ∨ IsSolvable G).

results.name: Schur/absolute irreducibility: (a) abs. irred. iff Hom_FG(M,M)=F; (b) faithful + Hom_FG=F implies E(G)=Hom_F(M,M); (c) finite F: K=Hom_FG(M,M) is a finite field, M abs. irred. over K
results.notes: VERIFIED partial. GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/AbsolutelyIrreducible.lean proves, sorry-free, the algebraically-closed instance (Burnside: E(G) = End_F V for f.d. irreducible), which is the only shape BG uses downstream (Prop 2.2, Thm 2.5, Thm 3.16). The book's actual statement is wider: no 'absolutely irreducible' predicate is defined anywhere (pinned mathlib also lacks one — IsAbsolutelyIrreducible grep = 0 hits), so (a)'s iff over an arbitrary field is absent and (b) with the Hom_FG=F hypothesis over a general field is absent. Slim-pass finding: Peterfalvi/Appendices/SemilinearField.lean (Pf App I Prop 2) proves the 2.1(c) Schur+LittleWedderburn content — End_{k[T]}(M) is a finite field over which M is simple and 1-dimensional (endField / isSimpleModule_end / finrank_end_eq_one / natCard_end_eq) — but only for COMMUTATIVE T (isSimpleModule_end genuinely uses commutativity), so (c) for general G remains open. Completing needs: define absolute irreducibility (base-change or Hom=F), prove the iff via Jacobson density (mathlib core exists), and (c) via LittleWedderburn for noncommutative G — mostly library-building, ~M.

results.name: Clifford for cyclic quotient: M irred FH-module, M ≅ M^x for all x, F alg. closed, G/H cyclic: (a) M ≤ L_H irreducible L implies L_H ≅ M; (b) the H-representation on M extends to G
results.notes: (a) is fully assembled and sorry-free: CliffordAlgClosed.lean (conjugates permute simple constituents, conjugate span, isotypic structure) + SkolemNoether.lean + CliffordMultiplicityOne.lean's restriction_isIrreducible (restriction of irreducible ρ to normal H with G=⟨H,x⟩ is irreducible), instantiated for extraspecial H in CliffordConjugateChar.lean; heavily consumed by Thm 2.5 and BG Thm 3.5. However the Lean (a) carries an extra hypothesis [NeZero (Nat.card H : k)] (char k ∤ |H|) that the book does not have — Clifford's theorem is characteristic-free in the book. (b) exists only over ℂ: CyclicCharacterExtension.lean builds cyclicExtension (a genuine representation of K extending ρ on H, Isaacs CTFG 11.22 construction) and the character-level extension theorem; the book wants any algebraically closed F. Both restrictions are harmless for every BG/FT use. Stale docstrings in S02_RepresentationsBasic.lean still say 2.2 is 'gated on Isaacs Ch.6 Clifford' — the code has long since overtaken them. Generalizing (a) to arbitrary characteristic + (b) to arbitrary alg-closed F ~M.

results.name: Fong–Swan corollary: G solvable, M absolutely irreducible FG-module implies dim M divides |G|
results.notes: VERIFIED partial. The characteristic-0 content is covered by the stronger classical theorem finrank_dvd_card (ClassSumAlgebra.lean, sorry-free): over ℂ the degree of ANY finite group's irreducible representation divides |G| (no solvability needed; Isaacs CTFG Thm 3.11 via algebraic integers); the character-level twin exists as ZIrr.exists_natDegree_charValue_one_dvd_card. The book's actual point — arbitrary field, in particular char p ∣ |G|, absolutely irreducible, solvable G — is absent (no absolute-irreducibility predicate; the inductive proof needs characteristic-free Clifford, see Prop 2.2 notes). Coq formalized it (rank_abs_irr_dvd_solvable, BGsection2.v:121) and notes it is not used in the FT proof; BG's own forward use is 0 (2026-05-23 audit). Effort M (rides on the same generalizations as 2.1/2.2).

results.name: Eigenspace/endomorphism-block decomposition under a finite-order operator g with primitive h-th root ε: parts (a)-(h),(j),(k) (dim E_m = Σ nᵢnᵢ₊ₘ, sum-of-squares identity, outlier structure, n₀ > 0 unless h = q+1)
results.notes: VERIFIED at statement level in this pass: (a) cyclicEigenspaceFin_isInternal_of_pow_eq_one takes an arbitrary field F, IsPrimitiveRoot epsilon h, and g^h = 1 — exactly the book's hypotheses; (g) finrank_cyclicEndConjEigenspaceFin gives dim E_m = Σᵢ nᵢnᵢ₊ₘ; (h) sum_sq_sub_finrank_cyclicEndConjEigenspaceFin is the ℤ sum-of-squares identity; (j)/(k) prop24j/prop24k are the pure ZMod h combinatorics with prop24j_fin/prop24k_fin Fin-transports consumed by ExtraspecialThm25. All ten parts (book skips (i)) proved sorry-free at full book strength, spread over EigenspaceUnderCyclicAction.lean, EigenspaceBlockDecomp.lean, CyclicEndConjCount.lean. (k) is stated in the contrapositive normal form the Thm 2.5 assembly consumes (n₀ = 0 ⟹ q = h−1), equivalent to the book's (k). Proof factoring differs from the book (matrix picture replaced by internal direct sums + a trace 'keystone'), but content is complete.

results.name: Extraspecial P of order p^{2n+1} ⋊ cyclic H of order h with C_P(x)=Z(P) for x ∈ H^#, char F ∤ |G|: h divides p^n ± 1, and if h ≠ p^n + 1 then C_V(H) ≠ 0 for every faithful irreducible FG-module V
results.notes: Fully-grounded group-level version, sorry-free, in ExtraspecialThm25Final.lean (assembled from ExtraspecialThm25.lean/Thm25Group.lean eigenspace-keystone machinery + CliffordConjugateChar discharge of the V_P-irreducibility hypothesis): divisibility as dim V ≡ ±1 (mod h) and the C_V(H) part as C_V(x)=0 ⟹ h = dim V + 1 (exact contrapositive of the book). dim V = p^n (Gor 5.5.5) is separately proved (sq_finrank_eq_card_quotient_center, ExtraspecialFaithful.lean), so the book's 'h ∣ p^n ± 1' form is recoverable. Specializations vs the book: (1) stated over an algebraically closed F only — the book allows any F with char ∤ |G| and descends via the rank(x−1) base-change argument (2.8); that bridge exists as BaseChange.lean's finrank_invariants_baseChangeRepresentation but the general-F wrapper was never assembled (downstream consumers Thm 3.4 / Thm 15.7 only need alg-closed); (2) requires an actual faithful irreducible ρ as input (fine for all uses); (3) cyclic H encoded as a generator x with closure(P ∪ {x}) = ⊤. Assembling the general-field book statement ~S.

results.name: Odd-order G faithful on 2-dimensional V over F: (a) char F ∤ |G| ⟹ G abelian; (b) char F = p ∣ |G| ⟹ Sylow p-subgroup abelian and contains G'
results.notes: VERIFIED at statement level in this pass: odd_two_dim_abelian takes arbitrary field F, finite G with Odd |G|, finrank F V = 2, faithful ρ, and char-away as (∀ q prime, q ∣ |G| → ¬CharP F q), concluding Std.Commutative on G; odd_two_dim_sylow_abelian takes CharP F p with p ∣ |G| and concludes, for EVERY Sylow p-subgroup P, that P is abelian AND commutator G ≤ P — both parts exactly the book. Full book strength, sorry-free, in S02_Representations.lean (with the ~2600-line supporting spine split across S02_RepresentationsBasic.lean and S02_FixedSubmodules.lean: determinant-kernel G*, rank-one line pair stay-or-swap, unipotent q=p branch, Maschke q≠p branch, Burnside normal-complement step, strong induction). The book's proof page (p.29) was missing from the mmd (MISSING_PAGE_FAIL:29) and was recovered from the PDF during formalization. Actively consumed downstream exactly where the book cites it: AppA_PStabilityBasic.lean (Thm A.1), S04_PGroupsSmallRank / S04_SmallRankBasic (Lem 4.17), §3.

results.name: p ≠ q primes, P ≅ (Z/p)², Q ≅ (Z/q)², Q ⊆ Aut(P): (a) q ∣ p−1; (b) some α ∈ Q^# acts as a power map x ↦ x^r with r^q ≡ 1, r ≢ 1 (mod p)
results.notes: VERIFIED missing (refutation attempted and failed). Re-checked in this pass: every '2.7' citation in OddOrder/ is Isaacs Lemma 2.7 (disjoint normal subgroups commute — unrelated), Peterfalvi (2.7) adjoint formula, BG Theorem 12.7, or displayed equation (12.7)/(2.7); descriptive greps (power-map automorphism, q ∣ p−1, abelem, dvd_sub_one across GroupTheory/**) hit only strictly weaker or unrelated material. Closest existing infra: GroupTheory/PRank.lean's prime_dvd_prime_sq_sub_one_of_orderOf_mulAut (q ∣ p²−1 for a prime-order automorphism of rank-≤2 elementary abelian — weaker than (a), no (b)) and SingerField.lean's isCyclic_and_card_dvd_card_sub_one_of_faithful_irreducible (abelian faithful irreducible ⟹ cyclic of order ∣ |M|−1 — supplies the 'noncyclic Q cannot act irreducibly' step but nothing is assembled). Coq analog regular_abelem2_on_abelem2 (BGsection2.v:1048) is likewise unused in the rest of the Coq FT proof — pure book-completeness item. Proof route: Q abelian noncyclic ⟹ reducible on the 2-dim F_p-space (Singer), two Q-eigenlines with scalar characters of order dividing q, faithfulness ⟹ Q ↪ μ_q × μ_q forces q ∣ p−1 and yields a diagonal α.

units.unit: BG §2 General Results on Representations (Prop 2.1 – Lem 2.7, pp. 9–16, mmd L586–795 + PDF p.29 for the Nougat-missing page)
units.summary: BG §2 contains 7 numbered results and is in strong shape: the two hard theorems that the FT critical path actually consumes — Prop 2.4 (all ten eigenspace/block parts, pure linear algebra at full generality) and Thm 2.6 (odd-order 2-dim representations, both parts at full book strength) — are completely formalized and sorry-free, as is a fully-grounded Thm 2.5 (specialized to algebraically closed fields; the book's general-field descent bridge exists in BaseChange.lean but was never assembled into a wrapper). The formalization is factored very differently from the book: almost everything lives in ~15 shared modules under OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/ (EigenspaceUnderCyclicAction, EigenspaceBlockDecomp, CyclicEndConjCount, ExtraspecialThm25*, Clifford*, AbsolutelyIrreducible), with only Thm 2.6 in the BG tree itself, and the S02_RepresentationsBasic planning docstrings are badly stale. The main gaps are foundational-generality ones with zero FT-path consumers: no absolute-irreducibility predicate exists (so Prop 2.1's iff/(c) for general G and the positive-characteristic half of Lemma 2.3 are open), Prop 2.2(a) carries a char ∤ |H| hypothesis the book doesn't have and 2.2(b) is ℂ-only, and Lemma 2.7 is entirely missing (cited nowhere else in BG and unused in the Coq FT proof). Slim verification pass: all three flagged labels CONFIRMED after refutation attempts (Prop 2.1 partial, Lem 2.3 partial, Lem 2.7 missing — with one new finding folded into Prop 2.1's notes: SemilinearField.lean's endField/finrank_end_eq_one proves the 2.1(c) finite-field-endomorphism content for commutative groups only), and both 'formalized' results (Prop 2.4, Thm 2.6) had their actual Lean statements read and confirmed at full book strength.

results.notes: OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S03e_Thm35.lean (1719 lines) + weight-space Clifford-theory support (S03e_WeightSpan.lean). The hardest result of §3 (engine of BG Thm 10.6); full minimal-counterexample proof through equations (3.6)-(3.38). hasPLengthOne p G := G/O_{p',p}(G) is a p'-group (correct notion); IsZGroup = all Sylow subgroups cyclic (matches). Sorry-free.

results.notes: OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S03c_Thm37.lean. STRONGER than the book: no odd-order hypothesis is needed or assumed (the book's proof never uses oddness, and the Lean proof confirms this). Hypothesis packaged as IsFrobeniusGroup G K R, interconvertible with the book's C_K(R)=1 for prime-order R via Lemma 3.1. A subgroup-pair form (used by BG Thm 11.3) is also provided. Sorry-free.

results.name: Solvable Frobenius G=KR acting on nonidentity nilpotent M coprimely, C_M(K)=1, C_M(x)=C_M(R) for x in R#: (a) |R|=p prime, (b) |M|=|C_M(R)|^p, (c) C_M(R) cyclic implies K' ⊆ C_K(M)
results.notes: Split over S03g_Thm310{,Core,Module,General,ElemAbelian}.lean, all sorry-free. Coverage: (a)+(b)+(c) fully proved for M an ELEMENTARY ABELIAN p-group with general (possibly non-abelian) solvable kernel K (the K₀-reduction Case 2 + reducible-module Case 1 induction are done at module level, incl. base change from ZMod p to its algebraic closure); (a) additionally proved for general NILPOTENT M but with ABELIAN kernel (conjugation form used by BG Prop 14.2(g)). What is NOT assembled is the book's exact packaging: general nilpotent M + general kernel for all of (a)(b)(c) via the Case 1 induction on a G-invariant normal series of M plus Lemma 1.9 for (c). All FT-path consumers (Prop 14.2(g), Thm 15.2 step 4, Cor 15.5) needed exactly the specialized forms that exist. Remaining work is a group-level induction gluing the existing elementary-abelian leaf: ~1-3 days.

units.summary: BG §3 (Actions of Frobenius Groups, mmd L795-1359) contains exactly 10 numbered results (Lemmas 3.1-3.3, Theorems 3.4-3.8, Proposition 3.9, Theorem 3.10), formalized across 15 sorry-free files OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S03*.lean (~13,250 lines). Nine of the ten are formalized at full book strength, including the two hardest: Theorem 3.6 (p-length one, a 3,822-line minimal-counterexample proof through equations (3.6)-(3.38) with a separate orbit-parity terminal file) and Theorems 3.4/3.5, which even include general-field versions via base change and faithfully-flat descent exactly as the book's remark on algebraic closure requires. Two results are strictly STRONGER than the book: Theorem 3.7 (Frobenius kernel nilpotency) is proved without the odd-order hypothesis, and Proposition 3.9 drops the p'-group hypothesis on the acted-on group. The only gap is Theorem 3.10, which is formalized in the specialized forms the FT path consumed — parts (a)(b)(c) for elementary abelian M with general kernel, and part (a) for nilpotent M with abelian kernel — but the book's exact packaging (general nilpotent M, general kernel, all three parts) is not assembled; the missing piece is a routine Case 1 induction over a normal series of nilpotent M gluing the existing elementary-abelian leaf (est. 1-3 days).

units.summary: BG §4 (Lemma 4.1–Theorem 4.20, 20 numbered results + the section's definition block) is one of the most completely formalized BG units: all files are sorry-free, and every apex result — Prop 4.11 (Huppert metacyclic), Thm 4.12, Lem 4.13/4.14 (via the Gorenstein 4.15(ii) precursor chain in S04d/S04e), Thm 4.16 (Blackburn classification, blackburnRankTwoClassification), Lem 4.17, Thm 4.18, and Thm 4.20(a)(c) — is proved, spread across S04*-leaves in BG/Ch1_Preliminary plus shared leaves (SCN, PRank, IsMetacyclic, IsExtraspecial, CentralProduct, NarrowPGroup). Several statements are strictly stronger than the book: Lem 4.15 and Prop 4.4(a) are p-general, Lem 4.17 drops the book's solvability hypothesis, and Thm 4.16 needs no faithfulness of the action. The gaps are concentrated in small "normal-refinement" utility results the FT path never needed: Prop 4.4(b) (C_G(A)=A×H for A∈SCN(Sylow)), the normal half of Lem 4.5(a) and the noncyclic half of 4.5(c) in general (only abelian-center resp. rank≥3 cases exist), Prop 4.6 (whose content is 4.5(c)), and Thm 4.20(b); additionally Thm 4.12(b)(c) carry a removable extra IsSolvable A hypothesis, Cor 4.19 exists only in its post-O_{p'}-reduction form, and 4.20(c)'s series package records factor cardinality rather than Sylow isomorphism and does not record the ascending-prime ordering. Closing the whole unit to full book strength is roughly one M-sized task (Gorenstein 5.4.10 for 4.5/4.6) plus three S-sized ones (4.4(b), 4.19 wrapper, 4.20(b)/packaging). Slim verification pass: no corrections needed — all four flagged labels (Prop 4.4 partial, Lem 4.5 partial, Prop 4.6 missing, Thm 4.20 partial) survived targeted refutation attempts (number and descriptive-content greps across OddOrder/GroupTheory, Isaacs, and BG trees found nothing beyond the already-recorded special cases, and the source docstrings explicitly confirm the deferrals), while the three load-bearing formalized rows checked in source (Lem 4.7, Thm 4.16, Thm 4.18) were confirmed at full book strength.

results.name: Structure of solvable odd-order A ≤ Aut(R), R narrow: A/O_p(A) abelian p'-group; p'-element orders divide p-1 (r≥3); prime |A| ∤ p(p-1) ⇒ |A| ∣ (p+1)/2, and R=[R,A] nonabelian ⇒ |R|=p³

All three parts (a)(b)(c) including both halves of (c). (a) rendered as commutativity of A/O_p(A) plus p ∤ |A/O_p(A)|. Uses critical-subgroup Thm 1.13 + stability chain Lemma 1.9 for r≥3, and §4 machinery (Lem 4.14/4.17, Blackburn Thm 4.16) plus Gorenstein 5.4.1 content for r≤2. results.name: Solvable odd G with narrow Sylow p-subgroup (p-length one if r(S)≥3): p largest prime of |G/O_{p'}(G)|; normal p-complement if p=3 or p minimal; G' has normal p-complement; p'-subgroups of G' lie in O_{p'}(G'); G/O_{p',p}(G) abelian p'-group
results.notes: S05_NarrowPGroups.lean. All five conclusions (a)-(e) present: (a) as ∀ q ∈ primeFactors(|G/O_{p'}(G)|), q ≤ p (that p itself divides the quotient is immediate from p ∣ |G| and p ∤ |O_{p'}(G)|); (e) as commutativity of G/O_{p',p}(G) plus hasPLengthOne p G for the p'-part. The p-length-one hypothesis is conditional on r(S)≥3 exactly as in the book. r(S)≤2 branch delegates to Thm 4.18 (S04.solvable_structure_of_pRank_le_two); r(S)≥3 branch runs Thm 5.5 on G/O_{p'}(G) via private core56. Sorry-free, full strength.

results.name: Solvable odd G, E elem-ab p-subgroup of F(G) with r(C_{F(G)}(E)) ≤ 2 ⇒ G' ≤ F(G)

units.summary: BG §5 (Narrow p-Groups, pp. 44-49) is COMPLETE: all 7 numbered results (Lem 5.1, 5.2, Thm 5.3 incl. part (d), Cor 5.4, Thm 5.5, 5.6, 5.7) are formalized sorry-free at full book strength, plus the narrow/E*(R)/W/T definitional layer. The formalization is factored differently from the book: predicates and generic facts about W = Ω₁(Z₂(R)) and T = C_R(W) live in the shared module OddOrder/GroupTheory/NarrowPGroup.lean (reused by BG §6/§10/§16 and Peterfalvi §9), while the numbered results sit in a 4-file prefix-split chain S05_NarrowSCN → S05_NarrowCharacterization → S05_NarrowAutomorphisms → S05_NarrowPGroups, with proofs decomposed into ~30 public support lemmas (often per-part and slightly stronger than the book, e.g. Thm 5.3(a) proved per-E without the narrowness hypothesis). One deliberate deviation: the dependence on the still-general BG Lemma 4.5(a)/(c)-noncyclic is bypassed by proving W noncyclic directly under r(R) ≥ 3, which suffices for every §5 use. Note the S05 directory also houses §4 material (Thm 4.20(a)/(c) branches and the Hall-radical form in S05b_Thm420Hall.lean) that belongs to the §4 unit, not §5; conversely no §5 gap exists — this unit needs no further work.

results.name: Hall & Higman: O_{p',p}(G) contains every abelian normal subgroup of a Sylow p-subgroup S (G solvable odd order)
results.notes: Verified at statement level: thmA4b in OddOrder/BG/AppA_PStability.lean (L1385, docstring '= Gorenstein 6.5.2 翻訳 = BG Thm 6.1') takes [Finite G], p ≠ 2, IsSolvable G, Odd (Nat.card G), P ∈ Syl_p, A ≤ P with P ≤ N_G(A), [IsMulCommutative A] and concludes A ≤ O_{p',p}(G) — full book strength. The p ≠ 2 hypothesis loses nothing: for p = 2 in an odd-order group the Sylow subgroup is trivial, so the book statement is vacuous there too. Coq analog odd_p_abelian_constrained likewise identifies 6.1 with A.4(b). S06_Additional.lean additionally has J(P)-instance corollaries under reduced hypotheses; its header table line '一般形 TODO' for 6.1 is stale (the general form lives in AppA). Sorry-free.

results.notes: The literal book statement with Thompson's J(S) is proved only in a reduced case: normalJ_normal_of_odd (S06_Additional.lean, via Isaacs Thm 7.6 normal_J) gives J(P) ⊴ G under the extra hypotheses O_{p'}(G) = ⊥ and P = C_G(Z(P)). The full-generality result is instead the book's own designated substitute (BG's Remark after 6.2 / Theorem B.4, Puig's L(S)): zCenter_lOdd_sup_oPiCore_normal in OddOrder/BG/AppB_Thm62.lean (L208, statement verified: p ≠ 2, IsSolvable G, Odd card, arbitrary S ∈ Syl_p ⟹ (Z(L(S)) ⊔ O_{p'}(G)).Normal) — exactly mirroring the Coq formalization (Puig_center_p'core_normal in BGsection6.v, which also never proves the J(S) form). All downstream BG uses (§7-§9, App A-C) go through the L(S)/reduced-J versions, so nothing is blocked; classified specialized only because the J(S) statement at full generality has no Lean counterpart. Sorry-free.

results.name: (a) normal Hall H ≤ G' with complement K ⟹ H = [H,K] and C_H(K) ≤ H'; (b) G' nilpotent, |G/G'| prime ⟹ G' Hall and G' = [G,K] for every complement K
results.notes: Verified partial. Part (a) fully formalized in S06_Additional.lean, in two declarations (L307, L394): first conclusion ⁅H,K⁆ = H proved WITHOUT coprimality (stronger than the book, whose Hall hypothesis supplies it); second conclusion C_G(K) ⊓ H ≤ derivedInG H with the coprime hypothesis (= book's Hall condition). Heavily cited downstream (Thm 10.6, Cor 10.7(a), §12, §15). Part (b) is missing — refutation attempted and failed: number greps ('6.3(b)', 'Lemma 6.3'), descriptive greps (nilpotent derived + prime index + Hall, 'der1'), and Coq-name grep (prime_nil_der1_factor) all find no Lean counterpart anywhere in OddOrder/ including GroupTheory/**. Coq has it (BGsection6.v L98) but comments 'apparently not used later'; nothing in the repo consumes it. Missing part is a short reduction to (a) (nilpotent G' splits as O_p × O_{p'}; a p-group with derived subgroup of index p is cyclic of order p): under 1 day with existing opCore/Hall infra.

results.name: Conjugation of H-invariant π-subgroups: H π'-subgroup normalizing π-subgroups J₁, J₂ (G₀ normal Hall, G₀/F(G₀) and (G/G₀)/F(G/G₀) nilpotent) ⟹ ∃ x ∈ ⟨J₁,J₂⟩ centralizing H with ⟨J₁ˣ,J₂⟩ a π-group
results.notes: Verified missing — refutation attempted and failed: every 'Thm 6.4'/'Theorem 6.4' hit in OddOrder/ is Isaacs Thm 6.4 (the Frobenius-group four-condition equivalence in Isaacs/Ch06_FrobeniusActions/FrobeniusGroup.lean), a different theorem; the OpResidual.lean:26 mention is verified to be a motivational docstring note ('BG §6 (Thm 6.4) relies on O_π machinery'), not a formalization; descriptive greps (J₁/J₂, two π-subgroups, normal Hall + nilpotent-over-Fitting) find nothing. The Coq formalization explicitly skips it: BGsection6.v L13 'Theorem 6.4 is not proved, since it is not needed for the revised proof of the odd order theorem'. Nothing in the repo cites it, so it is a pure full-coverage item. Proof is a page-long induction on |G|+|H| using minimal normal subgroups, coprime-action Hall machinery (Prop 1.5 / Isaacs 3.23, all available in the repo) and F(G); estimate 1-3 days.

results.name: Solvable factorization G = KU, K ⊴ G, H ≤ U, (|H|,|K|) = 1: (a) H ∩ G' = H ∩ U'; (b) N_G(H) = C_K(H)·N_U(H); (c) H^g ≤ U ⟹ g = cu with c ∈ C_K(H), u ∈ U
results.notes: All three statements read and verified at full book strength in S06_Additional.lean (L485, L825, L664): [IsSolvable G], K.Normal, K ⊔ U = ⊤ (= G = KU for K normal), H ≤ U, Nat.Coprime (card H) (card K). (a) is the equality H ⊓ G' = H ⊓ ⁅U,U⁆; (c) uses BG's convention H^g = g⁻¹Hg encoded as H.comap (MulAut.conj g) and yields g = c·u with c ∈ C_G(H) ⊓ K; (b) is a genuine set equality of coset products, derived from (c) as in the book. Supported by a reusable Hall-conjugacy engine exists_conj_eq_of_isHall_subgroupOf (shared with Thm 7.4(d)). Widely used downstream (§8, §10, §13). Sorry-free.

results.name: p-length one local structure: (a) S ≤ SO_{p'}(G) = O_{p',p}(G) and G = O_{p'}(G)N_G(S); (b) S ≤ G' ⟹ S ≤ N_G(S)'; (c) Y ⊆ S, Y^x ⊆ S ⟹ x = cg, c ∈ C_G(Y), g ∈ N_G(S); (d) Q p-subgroup ⟹ ∃ x ∈ C_G(Q ∩ S), Q^x ≤ S
results.notes: Statements read and verified: all four lettered parts formalized in S06_Additional.lean under [Finite G] [IsSolvable G] + hasPLengthOne p G. Part (a) splits into the foundation equality O_{p',p}(G) = O_{p'}(G) ⊔ S (L954 — this piece is proved with `omit [IsSolvable G]`, i.e. without solvability, slightly stronger than the book, matching Coq) and the Frattini factorization ⊤ = O_{p'}(G) ⊔ N_G(S) (L1033; subgroup sup with a normal factor = the book's set product). Parts (b)-(d) are derived from Lemma 6.5 exactly as in the book ((b) at L1057 via 6.5(a) with K = O_{p'}(G), U = N_G(S)). Sorry-free.

results.name: E ∈ ℰ_p*(G) maximal elementary abelian (p odd), L a p'-subgroup normalized by E, G solvable of p-length one ⟹ L ≤ O_{p'}(G)

Proof follows the book's O_{p'}-quotient reduction (thm67_reduced + a maximal-elementary-abelian quotient-lift lemma isMaximalElementaryAbelian_map_mk'). The file-header table marking 6.7 as TODO is stale. Matches Coq plength1_norm_pmaxElem. The book's remark that p-length one is removable (Thompson) is not formalized, but the book itself states 6.7 with the hypothesis. Sorry-free.

units.summary: BG §6 contains 7 numbered results; 5 are fully formalized and sorry-free, mostly in OddOrder/BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S06_Additional.lean. The formalization is factored differently from the book in two notable ways: Thm 6.1 lives in AppA_PStability.lean as thmA4b (the book itself identifies Thm 6.1 with Thm A.4(b)), and Thm 6.2 follows the book's own remark (and the Coq formalization) by proving the general form with Puig's L(S) instead of Thompson's J(S) — Z(L(S))·O_{p'}(G) ⊴ G in AppB_Thm62.lean — with the literal J(S) form only in a reduced case via Isaacs Thm 7.6. The gaps are Lemma 6.3(b) (missing part; part (a) is proved in both conclusions, the first even without the coprimality the book's Hall hypothesis supplies) and Theorem 6.4 (entirely missing; the Coq odd-order formalization also deliberately skips it as unneeded for the revised proof, and nothing in the repo consumes it). The S06 file's header comparison table is stale — it marks 6.3(b)-6.4 and 6.7 all as TODO, but Lemma 6.6 (all four parts) and Thm 6.7 are in fact fully proved later in the same file. Verification pass: both flagged labels (6.3 partial, 6.4 missing) were confirmed after refutation attempts (number, descriptive-content, and Coq-name greps across OddOrder/ including GroupTheory/**, all negative — every 'Thm 6.4' hit is Isaacs Thm 6.4 on Frobenius groups, and OpResidual.lean's mention is motivational only); statement-level reads confirmed full book strength for Thm 6.1, Lem 6.5, Lem 6.6, and Thm 6.7, with one note refinement — the Lem 6.6 foundation equality is actually proved WITHOUT solvability (omit [IsSolvable G]), matching Coq rather than merely the book.

The unit lives in two files: OddOrder/BG/Ch3_MaximalSubgroups/S11_ExceptionalMaximal.lean (Hyp 11.1 + Lem 11.1 + Cor 11.2/11.4/11.6 + Thm 11.3/11.5) and the single-theorem leaf S11_MsigmaANormal.lean (Thm 11.7 plus a Hypothesis111.of_sylow Sylow-swap helper). The factoring closely mirrors the book, with the standing hypothesis bundled as a structure (same design as the Coq formalization) and an auxiliary predicate IsAInvSylowIn (with existence constructor) standing in for 'A-invariant Sylow q-subgroup'. The only statement-level deviations are benign: Thm 11.5 is stated for arbitrary Sylow p-subgroups of M (full strength), Thm 11.7 is phrased as M ≤ N_G(M_σ ⊔ A) (equivalent to M_σA ⊴ M), and Cor 11.6(c) is an existence form that omits the (proof-internal) fact that A₁, A₂ are conjugates of A₀ while keeping everything used downstream. No gaps — this unit is complete.

units.summary: BG §12 (The Subgroup E, mmd L3053-3514) contains 19 numbered results (Lemmas 12.1-12.3, 12.8, 12.11, 12.17-12.19; Propositions 12.4, 12.15; Theorems 12.5, 12.7, 12.12, 12.13; Corollaries 12.6, 12.9, 12.10, 12.14, 12.16) plus the τ₁/τ₂/τ₃-E-notation setup. ALL are fully formalized and sorry-free — this unit is complete, spread over 21 dedicated S12_*.lean files (~16.5k lines) under OddOrder/BG/Ch3_MaximalSubgroups/. I read every headline Lean statement; each matches full book strength, with three documented faithful adaptations: (1) results asserting facts about the set τ₂(M) (12.7(a), 12.10(c), 12.11(a)) are stated in prime-restricted form because the repo's tau sets don't build in primality (BG's are implicitly prime); (2) Corollary 12.16's general conjugation form parametrizes the σ-disjointness input to avoid a §13 import cycle, but it is discharged in-repo by the sorry-free S13.sigma_disjoint_of_nonconjugate; (3) Lemma 12.17's cyclicity clause for M_σ∩M^g is assembled downstream as S16.Msigma_inf_conj_isCyclic (needs the §15 rank-1⟹cyclic step) — proved, just placed later in the import DAG. Two stale header comments in S12_E.lean/S12_ECore.lean still describe 12.16(b) as deferred and mention 'sorry scaffolds'; the code is fully proved — trust the declarations, not those headers.

units.summary: BG §13 (Prime Action, results 13.1-13.13 plus the prime/regular-action definitions) is COMPLETELY formalized and sorry-free — every one of the 13 numbered results has a Lean theorem at full book strength, verified by reading each actual statement, spread over 8 files in OddOrder/BG/Ch3_MaximalSubgroups/ (hub S13_PrimeAction.lean plus leaves S13_Lemma131/Corollary132/Theorem134/Lemma137/Lemma138/Theorem1310/PrimeActionTransition). The formalization is in places stronger or differently factored than the book: Theorem 13.10(c) is proved for every noncentralizing P (book: only the hypothesized one), Theorem 13.9's nilpotent case takes a direct Lemma 10.12 route instead of the book's Cor 12.6(f), and the book's compressed arguments (Lemma 13.8's Hall-(β∪β*) argument, Theorem 13.4's elided 'we can conclude' step) got substantial explicit helper layers (~7000 lines total for a 7-page section). Caveats found and resolved: several file-header comments still say 'proofs are all sorry (scaffold)' — these are stale pre-completion remnants (grep confirms zero real sorries, matching the repo-wide sorry census); and the book's conclusion bullets for 13.10/13.11 were dropped by Nougat OCR and were recovered from PDF images (noted in-file). No gaps remain; effort needed is zero across the unit.

units.summary: BG §14 (mmd L3787–4158) is essentially complete: all 13 numbered results are formalized sorry-free at full book strength, distributed over ~10 topic leaves in OddOrder/BG/Ch4_FamilyOfMaximal/S14_TypePCounting/ plus S16_PairIntersection/S16_Lemma1413/S16_MainResults (Thm 14.4(b) and parts of 14.7(d)/14.9 deliberately live in the S16 layer). The formalization is much more finely factored than the book — Prop 14.2 and Thm 14.7 are each split into 10+ named part-lemmas following the Coq BGsection14 decomposition, and includes faithfulness improvements over naive readings (a false conjunct of Prop 14.2 detected and removed; Cor 14.3's scaffold transposition repaired; τ₂-freeness in 14.13(a) stated prime-wise because the repo tau2 admits composite exponents). The only genuine gaps: Lemma 14.13(b) (a 5-line consequence of Thm 14.4, absent — Coq omits it too; effort S) and the M*-pinned form of two Cor 14.12 clauses (delivered in equivalent existential E-setup form, M*-identification proved internally but not surfaced; effort S). The 2 remaining S14 sorries (GlobalCounting.lean:808 sigmaLength_one_frobenius_type; TypePDuality.lean:1291 nonidentity_covered_by_sigma_pieces) block NO book result: both are explicitly frozen, consumer-free mis-encoded historical surfaces — the former a vacuous-hypothesis variant of Lemma 14.13(a) (faithful version proved as S16.non_disjoint_signalizer_frobenius), the latter a false-relative-to-BG variant of Cor 14.9 covering by M_σ^# instead of M̃ (faithful covering proved via the Mtilde/zTilde APIs and theoremE) — deleting or leaving them frozen is a housekeeping choice, not a formalization gap. SLIM VERIFICATION PASS (2026-07-16): no status changes — the Lem 14.13 'partial' label was confirmed after attempted refutation (14.13(b) absent from all of OddOrder/ under number-citation and descriptive-content greps, and Coq BGsection14.v:2409 formalizes only (a)), and the three most load-bearing results (Thm 14.4 sigmaLength_one_centralizer_structure, Thm 14.7 typeP_duality, Cor 14.9 sharpSubgroup_top_cover_reps_dichotomy/theoremE with an unconditional reps transversal) were confirmed at full book strength by reading their Lean statements.

units.summary: BG §15 is essentially completely formalized and sorry-free: all nine numbered results (15.1–15.9) have Lean counterparts in OddOrder/BG/Ch4_FamilyOfMaximal/S15_MF/ (8 topic leaves, ~11.5k lines, no sorries; the two remaining S14 sorries are frozen no-consumer mis-encodings, so nothing here depends on a sorry). Lemma 15.1, Corollaries 15.3/15.4/15.6, and Theorem 15.8 are at full book strength; Theorem 15.2, Corollary 15.5, Theorem 15.7, and Corollary 15.9 are proven in substance but their assembled Lean statements expose less than the book prints, with the missing conjuncts either living in helper/S16-bridge lemmas or deliberately dropped following the authoritative Coq formalization. Two deviations are documented book errors, not repo gaps: 15.7(c)'s printed equality M' = F(M) is an overstatement (weakened to M' ⊆ F(M), exactly as Coq's nonTI_Fitting_structure), and 15.9(c) is dropped (as in Coq, "not used later"; an earlier Lean draft of it was found unsound). Surprising factoring: the deep 15.7(e) trichotomy is fully proven but lives in §16 bridge form (isTypeI_of_isTypeF for type F, isTypeV_of_isTypeP1_mf_eq_msigma with the Singer/SL2 |W₁| ∣ p±1 divisibilities for type P1), and Theorem 15.8 required three "keystone" clauses of Coq's Ptype_structure/Fcore_structure absent from the repo's §14 API — all landed sorry-free. Several docstrings are stale (still saying "§14 gated/sorried" or "(8.8) not yet formalized" although everything cited is now clean).

units.unit: BG §16 The Main Results (Theorems A–E, Types I–V, Proposition 16.1, Theorems I–II) — local-analysis.mmd L4328–4576
units.summary: BG §16 is one of the most thoroughly formalized units in the repo: all of Theorems A–E, Proposition 16.1, and Theorems I–II have sorry-free Lean counterparts under OddOrder/BG/Ch4_FamilyOfMaximal/S16_MainResults/ (~7.7k lines across 6 leaves plus S16_PairIntersection and S16_Lemma1413), with the key monoliths (theoremA_maximal_structure_faithful, theoremC_paired_structure, proposition_type_classification, theoremII_tame_embedding, typeP_pair_inf_eq, non_disjoint_signalizer_frobenius) explicitly asserted axiom-clean in AxiomsCheck.lean; several docstrings still saying \"sorry-bearing/not axiom-clean\" are stale. The formalization is differently factored than the book: the Type I–V definitions are the Peterfalvi (8.1)–(8.8) data-structure variants shared with the Peterfalvi tree (OddOrder/GroupTheory/MaximalSubgroupType.lean), and Theorem I's full clause data (N_G(W₀)=W, S=W₁S′ factorizations) is delivered through the Peterfalvi-facing Section16MaximalPair/Section16TypePStructure bundles rather than the single dichotomy monolith. The genuine residual gaps are small sub-clauses: Theorem A's general \"M′/M_F nilpotent\" (only the hard type-P₁ case is a standalone lemma; type-P generally is carried by TypePData's U_nilpotent+derived_complement fields, leaving the type-F assembly), the reverse (⊇) half of Theorem C(9)'s identity A₀(M)−A(M)=𝒞_M(Ẑ), and — the largest — Theorem II's (Tii)(a)–(e) \"system of supporting subgroups\" packaging plus the tamely-imbedded-subset definition, whose raw ingredients are all proved but never assembled (Lemma 14.13(b)'s M-conjugation choice exists in neither Lean nor Coq); notably the Coq formalization also only formalizes \"the part of Theorem II relevant to the proof\" and drops (Tii)(a), so this gap mirrors math-comp. Two frozen mis-encoded surfaces with real sorries sit nearby in S14 (sigmaLength_one_frobenius_type, nonidentity_covered_by_sigma_pieces) but are documented no-consumer records and do not gate anything in §16. SLIM-PASS CORRECTIONS: Theorem E upgraded partial→formalized — its flagged-missing E(3) disjointness of 𝒞_G(Ẑ) from the M̃-cover is in fact proved sorry-free (S14.conjClassSet_T_Mtilde_disjoint + family_inf_msigma_union_eq, packaged as exceptional_disjoint_thickened in Peterfalvi.S10.nonTypeICovering_of_isTypeP); the partial/missing labels on Thm A, Thm C, Thm II, and Def tamely imbedded were re-attacked by number- and content-based greps (including the Coq analogs) and all confirmed, and load-bearing spot-reads of Thm B, Thm I, and Prop 16.1 confirmed full book strength.

units.summary: BG Appendix A (mmd L4585-4643) contains exactly five numbered results, Theorems A.1-A.5, and all five are fully formalized sorry-free in OddOrder/BG/AppA_PStabilityBasic.lean (A.1, A.2) and OddOrder/BG/AppA_PStability.lean (A.3, A.4a/b/c, A.5 parts 1-2), each verified by reading the actual Lean statements and cross-checked against Gorenstein's source definitions. Several statements are strictly stronger than the book: A.4(a) drops the solvability hypothesis, A.4(c) is proved without the O_{p'}(G)P ⊴ G normality hypothesis (parameter present but unused), A.1 needs no oddness of p, and A.5's generation hypothesis is generalized to any X below the sup of all P-normalized abelian p-subgroups. The formalization is factored differently from the book: A.4 is three theorems, A.5 is two, and the real content of A.4(c) (Gorenstein 6.5.3's condition (B)) lives in a substantial private engine (stabilityLiftAux / stability_perFactor, ~370 lines) doing the chief-series + ZMod p linearization + algebraic-closure base-change argument. p-stability itself is defined (IsPStable) in Gorenstein's representation-theoretic form over algebraically closed char-p fields, which I verified matches Gorenstein 1968 §3.8 (mmd L2200) up to a standard base-change equivalence. All theorems are registered in AxiomsCheck.lean and genuinely consumed downstream (thmA4b as BG Thm 6.1 in Ch2 §7-8, thmA5 in Appendix B), so this unit needs no further work.

units.unit: BG App.B The Puig Subgroup
units.summary: BG Appendix B is completely formalized and sorry-free across three files (OddOrder/BG/AppB_Puig.lean, AppB_PuigB3B4.lean, AppB_Thm62.lean): the Puig L-tower definitions, all seven parts of Lemma B.1, Lemma B.2, Lemma B.3, and Theorem B.4 (Puig 1976). The formalization is differently and more generally factored than the book: the relative-in-a-subgroup operators lRelIn/lNIn/lOddIn/lStarIn are the primitives (the book's absolute forms are the H = ⊤ case), and B.1(e)(f) plus B.2 are proved in strengthened relative versions that the B.3/B.4 proofs need; substantial extra API (φ-equivariance, characteristic-ness, cross-group and injective-hom covariance of L and Z(L(·))) exists beyond the text. The only literal statement not present is B.4(a)'s Frattini product G = O_{p'}(G)·N_G(Z(L(S))): closed issue 2002 records the deliberate design decision to instead prove the equivalent general normality form (Z(L(S)) ⊔ O_{p'}(G)).Normal (the 'Thm 6.2 general form', which implies (a) by a one-step Frattini argument whose tools are already in the file), so no gap of mathematical content remains. This appendix serves as the repo's self-contained substitute for Glauberman's Z(J)-theorem (BG Thm 6.2, omitted by Isaacs) and is actively consumed by BG S08/S09. The restated Theorem A.5 appearing in the App.B text is owned by the App.A unit and is fully formalized there (thmA5_part1/thmA5_part2, sorry-free).

units.summary: BG Appendix C is essentially complete: Theorem C and Lemmas C.1-C.3 are all machine-checked, sorry-free, and axiom-clean, with the final bridge (final_contradiction) wiring Theorem C against Peterfalvi Section 16's field-normalizer data to kill the minimal counterexample. The factoring is inverted relative to the book and is the one surprise: the finite-field and character halves live in OddOrder/BG/AppC_*.lean, while the generators-and-relations group argument of Lemma C.3 (Steps 1-4, Remarks (X)/(XI) via Isaacs Thm 4.34 coprime decomposition) is proved on the Peterfalvi side (S16_AppendixC3/S16_CoreSetup/S16_CoreBounds/S16_NonExistenceGCore) on the transported configuration, with FieldNormalizerData genuinely constructed (fieldNormalizerData_of_repr), not posited. The only specialization: Theorem C, hypothesis (B), and Lemma C.3 are stated for the S16 configuration (Q elementary abelian q-group, p,q odd, inside the odd minimal counterexample) rather than the book's abstract standalone form with an arbitrary finite abelian p'-group Q — full strength for FT, but the abstract Theorem C (e.g. the SL(2,2^q) instance) is not expressible. Genuine gaps are marginal: the illustrative SL(2,2^q) example (Remark II), the trivial odd-primes wlog (Remark V), and the out-of-scope literature items (Remark IV / Problem 1). units.unit: BG App.D CN-Groups of Odd Order
units.summary: BG Appendix D (pp. 153-156, mmd lines 5132-5199) is a 4-page reading guide for the Feit-Hall-Thompson CN-theorem containing exactly two numbered results, Lemmas D.1 (Sylow-TI in a minimal simple CN-group of odd order) and D.2 (P ≤ N_G(P)′); the tags (D.1)-(D.3) in the text are display equations inside D.1's proof, not results. The repo file OddOrder/BG/AppD_CNGroups.lean is a statement-level scaffold carrying all 3 of the unit's sorries with zero proof content, and its standing hypothesis MinimalSimpleCNHypothesis encodes minimal-simplicity/nonsolvability as opaque free Prop fields, so Lemma D.1 as literally stated asserts Sylow-TI for every odd-order CN group (false: an odd solvable CN group such as F_{3^6} ⋊ (C7 ⋊ C3) violates it) and none of the sorries is honestly dischargeable without first de-opacifying the hypothesis; the third sorry (cnTheorem_reduction) is even trivially dischargeable with True-instantiations, i.e. pure packaging. Supporting infrastructure is good: the ZJ input is sorry-free via the book-sanctioned L(P)/Thm B.4 substitute (AppB_Thm62.zCenter_lOdd_sup_oPiCore_normal) and the Focal Subgroup Theorem (BG Thm 1.17) is in mathlib (Subgroup.commutator_inf_eq_focalSubgroup); the one genuinely missing mathematical input is Gorenstein §14.1 solvable-CN structure theory (Cor 14.1.6, 3-step groups), absent from the entire repo and the dominant cost, making D.1 an L and D.2 an S conditional on it. Two structural caveats: math-comp/odd-order has no Coq analog of App.D, and since feitThompson is complete the honest minimal-simple-CN hypothesis is vacuous, so everything could be discharged vacuously — logically sound but defeating the appendix's expository purpose. Slim verification pass: all three flagged partial labels CONFIRMED after refutation attempts (no alternative formalization of CN-groups, Sylow-TI, focal-control, or 3-step exclusion found under any book tree or OddOrder/GroupTheory/**; mathlib and AppB citations verified by reading the sources); one strengthening — D.2 as stated is definitively false (G = C3 counterexample under True-instantiation), not merely 'likely false'.
