Substantial special cases of E.1/E.2 were already proved sorry-free for BG Prop 4.3: class-≤2 and class-≤3 collection formulas with pinned binomial exponents and the corresponding Ω₁-exponent-p / p-power-multiplicativity theorems (S04_SmallRankBasic.lean, CriticalSubgroup.lean, Isaacs Ch04 CommutatorBasics.lean) — so E.1/E.2 are partial, missing only the general-class (≤ p−1) versions, which require formalizing Hall's collecting process in full (L, the hardest single gap). E.3–E.5 have zero genuine content anywhere in the repo and no Coq analog (math-comp/odd-order formalizes only appendices A–C); E.3 is the big-ticket item (XL), E.4 is M given E.3's internals, and E.5 is mostly wiring (L) since its §12/§14/§15/§16 prerequisites are formalized. Closing this unit honestly requires rewriting all five statements, not just filling the sorries. Slim verification pass: all five flagged labels (partial/partial/missing/missing/missing) were confirmed against refutation greps (book-number citations, descriptive names, mathlib Hall–Petrescu search, Coq appendix listing) and the E.1/E.2 special-case and E.5 prerequisite claims were spot-read in the Lean sources; the only corrections are lean_name namespace fixes (OddOrder.BG.Ch1.S04 not OddOrder.BG.S04; Omega.exponent_eq_of_class_le_two lives in CriticalSubgroup.lean) plus adding the class-≤2 Hall–Petrescu special case in OddOrder/GroupTheory/CriticalSubgroup.lean to E.1.

units.unit: Peterfalvi §1-§2 (Introduction and Notation, pp. 1-4)
units.summary: The unit contains zero numbered results, as expected: §1 is historical/strategic prose plus a list of assumed-known results from Isaacs' Character Theory book, and §2 is a pure notation dictionary. The repo mirrors this with two docstring-only mapping files (OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S01_Introduction.lean, S02_Notation.lean; no declarations, sorry-free by construction). The one substantive mathematical statement in the unit — the unnumbered assumed fact from Isaacs Problem 2.2 (a Galois conjugate of an irreducible character is irreducible) — is formalized at greater-than-book strength as IsIrreducibleCharacter.mapRingEquiv (any ring automorphism of ℂ, with exists_complexRingEquiv_extends bridging from automorphisms of number fields), and its ZIrr corollary is also proved. Every notational concept §2 introduces has a real, verified carrier: ClassFunction G k for CF(G), supportedSubmodule for CF(G,A), ZIrr G for ℤ[Irr G], ClassFunction.induce for Ind, inertia for I_G(θ), IsTISubset for TI-subsets (a normalizer-parametrized design variant equivalent to the book's condition at L = N_G(A)), with the group-theoretic notation (exp, π(G), σ-parts, O_σ, F(G), Φ(G), Ω₁, ⋊, fixed-point-free actions) covered by mathlib plus repo files. One non-mathematical observation: the S02_Notation.lean docstring is stale — it still describes the RepresentationTheory infrastructure as "Wave 1a planned" and promises notation aliases "later", whereas all of that infrastructure now exists under descriptive names and the aliases were never needed.

results.name: Galois conjugate of an irreducible character is irreducible (χ^σ ∈ Irr G for σ ∈ Aut(Q_n))
results.notes: OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/GaloisCharacter.lean (statement read at line 344, sorry-free): stated for ANY ring automorphism σ : ℂ ≃+* ℂ, strictly stronger than the book's Aut(Q_n) version; CyclotomicGaloisAction.lean provides exists_complexRingEquiv_extends to lift number-field automorphisms to ℂ, so the book form follows. Also extended to virtual characters (mapRingEquiv_mem_ZIrr).

results.name: TI-subset: A^g = A or A^g ∩ A = ∅ for all g ∈ G
results.notes: OddOrder/GroupTheory/TISubset.lean:73. Design variant: predicate IsTISubset A L parametrized by a normalizer bound L (∀ g, overlap of A with A^g → g ∈ L); with L = N_G(A) this is equivalent to the book condition, and the file's API (disjoint_conj_of_not_mem, mem_of_conj_mem_conj) delivers exactly the book's uses. Not a weakening.

results.name: Virtual character = element of ℤ[Irr G]; ℤ[Irr G, A] = ℤ[Irr G] ∩ CF(G, A)
results.notes: ZIrr.lean:153 defines ZIrr G as a Submodule ℤ of ClassFunction G ℂ; ClassFunction.lean:255 defines supportedSubmodule A (= CF(G,A)); their intersection realizes ℤ[Irr G, A] throughout §4-§7 files.

results.name: CF(G), (α,β)_G, Supp, Ind/Res, 1_G, conjugate character, inertia group I_G(θ), Q_n, A^#, A^L, exp(G), π(G), σ-group/σ-parts g_σ, O_σ(G), F(G), Φ(G), ⋊, fixed-point-free action, Ω₁(G)
results.notes: Verified carriers: ClassFunction.lean:67 (CF(G) with inner product), InducedCharacter.lean:278 (induce; classical formula, since mathlib only has categorical Ind), Inertia.lean:194 (inertia). Group-theory notation covered by mathlib (exponent, Frattini, semidirect product, primeFactors) plus repo files (Fitting subgroup in Isaacs Ch2 tree, OmegaSubgroup.lean for Ω₁, PiElementDecomposition.lean for g_σ decomposition, coprime/fixed-point-free action files). No notation alias layer was ever added to S02_Notation.lean — descriptive names are used directly; the S02 docstring's 'Wave 1a planned / aliases later' text is stale but harmless.

results.name: Odd order: nontrivial irreducible character is not self-conjugate (χ̄ ≠ χ)
results.notes: Full strength and stronger: pointwise, cardinal (exactly one real irreducible), set-predicate, and χ−χ̄ nondegeneracy forms all proved in OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/BrauerPermutation{,Unconditional}.lean and OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S03_PreliminaryCharacter.lean. The proof's engine, Brauer's permutation lemma ([Is] Thm 6.32), is itself proved unconditionally (brauer_permutation_lemma').

results.name: Vanishing lemma: H ⊴ G, H ⊄ Ker χ, C_H(g)=1 ⟹ χ(g)=0
results.notes: Fully proved in OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S03b_Vanishing.lean (sorry-free) following the book's proof exactly: second orthogonality on G and G/H (column_orthogonality_diagonal), inflation bijection onto {χ : H ⊆ ker χ}, centralizer injection into the quotient, squeeze. Kernel condition expressed at class-function level. VERIFIED in slim pass: statement read, exact book hypotheses (H ⊴ G, ¬(H ⊆ characterKernel χ), centralizerInSubgroup H g = ⊥) and conclusion χ(g)=0.

results.name: CF(H,A) restriction/orthogonality criterion: (a) μ|A = (Σdᵢχᵢ)|A iff coefficient equations; (b) orthonormal image family ⟹ μᵢ|A = χᵢ|A
results.notes: Differently factored, at greater generality (OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/SupportedSpanOrthogonality.lean): the (a)-iff is the core equivalence 'D vanishes on A ⟺ D ⊥ every member of an A-supported spanning family Φ' for arbitrary conjugation-invariant A; instantiating D := Res μ − Σdᵢχᵢ and applying Frobenius reciprocity (inner_induce_eq_inner_restrict, also in repo) recovers the textbook coefficient form. (b)'s value identification μᵢ|A = χᵢ|A is restrict_apply_eq_on_of_induce_eq_sum; the '(μ ⊥ all μᵢ) ⟹ μ|A = 0' clause has no named declaration but is a one-line consequence of the (a)-core + reciprocity, and the masking engine eq_zero_of_mem_of_inner_supported_eq_zero states the equivalent orthocomplement fact directly. Heavily consumed by S05/S06/S12/S13. VERIFIED in slim pass: statements read; spanning-family form subsumes the book's basis hypothesis.

results.name: Isometry difference-pair structure: τ isometry on equal-degree family ⟹ (χᵢ−χ₁)^τ = ε(μᵢ−μ₁), μᵢ distinct irreducible, shared sign ε=±1
results.notes: Full strength in OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/IsometryDifferencePair.lean: n ≥ 2 distinct equal-degree irreducibles of H, τ a ℤ-linear map whose difference images are virtual characters vanishing at 1 with inner products preserved (a faithful unpacking of 'isometry ℤ[X,H^#] → ℤ[Irr G, G^#]'), conclusion a SignedIrreducibleDifferenceFamily (injective μ, single sign ε = ±1, images = signed differences). This is the coherence keystone cited throughout §7. VERIFIED in slim pass: statement read at lines 730-747; hypotheses and conclusion match the book (inner-product preservation required only on the differences, which is all the book's proof uses).

results.name: Induction from a normal subgroup (Clifford suite): (a) Res Ind θ = r·Σθ^g; (b) ‖χ‖² = r, irreducible if r=1; (c) conjugate sources give equal/orthogonal inductions; (d) χ(1)Resχ/‖χ‖² = |G:H|Σθ^g(1)θ^g; (e) odd order, θ≠1 ⟹ χ̄ ⊥ χ
results.notes: (a)-(c) formalized at full strength in InducedIrreducible.lean: (a) as |H|•Res(Ind θ) = |I_G(θ)|•Σ_{distinct conjugates} (equivalent, and stated for any class function); (b) as |H|·‖Ind θ‖² = |I_G(θ)| plus isIrreducibleCharacter_induce_of_inertia_eq for the r=1 clause; (c) both halves. (d) verbatim identity never stated — a one-line corollary of (a)+(b); the repo instead records the degree-sum forms actually consumed downstream (sumIrreducibleDegreeSq etc., docstring-cited as (1.5.d)). (e) SLIM-PASS CONFIRMED partial: all three general pieces exist (conj_induce: (Ind θ)̄ = Ind θ̄; conjBy_ne_conj_of_odd: θ^g ≠ θ̄ for odd |L|; inner_induce_eq_zero_of_not_conj), and the general constituent-level conjugate-distinctness forall_mem_conj_ne_of_odd (CliffordDecomposition.lean, any H ⊴ L odd, mult-free decomposition) is stronger packaging — but the verbatim named ⟨Ind θ, (Ind θ)̄⟩ = 0 for general H ⊴ G exists only in the Frobenius-kernel specialization. Closing (d)+(e) verbatim is a few hours of assembly.

results.name: Kernels and induction: (a) A ⊆ Ker θ ⟺ A ⊆ Ker Ind θ; (b) induction commutes with deflation to G/A
results.notes: (a) both directions: forward for any class function constant on A (S03_PreliminaryCharacter.lean, more general than the book), backward via Mackey + triangle-equality keystone for θ irreducible with H ⊴ G (exactly the book's hypotheses; the file's older docstring saying the converse 'is not formalised here' is stale — the InducedKernelDescent section later in the same file proves it). (b) the general identity Ind_H^Γ(inflation of χ̄) = inflation of Ind_{H/N}^{Γ/N} χ̄ is induce_compHom_subgroupMap_mk' (S11_MaximalII_III_IV/CliffordData.lean) for arbitrary class functions on the quotient; combined with exists_inflate_eq_of_subset_characterKernel (InflationCharacter.lean) this is the book statement for θ with A ⊆ Ker θ. A trivial-character instance also exists in InflationInduction.lean.

results.name: Clifford correspondence: (a) Ind_T^G ψᵢ distinct irreducible, Ind_H^G θ = Σeᵢχᵢ; (b) T/H abelian ⟹ uniform e, n = |T:H|/e²; (c) coprime case ⟹ e = 1, n = |T:H|
results.notes: CORRECTED (slim pass): the earlier claim that general (b) is missing and 'all repo versions route through the canonical extension theorem' is WRONG. (b) at full book strength (T/H abelian only, e possibly > 1, NO coprimality) IS formalized in InducedInvariantConstituent.lean + GallagherDecomposition.lean + CliffordSingleOrbit.lean, by exactly the book's regular-character/projection-formula argument (Ind(Res ψ) = ψ·Σ_λ Inf(λ), induce_restrict_eq_mul_sum_linearClassFunction): e·Ind_H^G θ = Σ_β Ind_T^G(ψ·Inf β) with each summand irreducible (induce_smul_eq_sum_induce_mul_of_invariant_inertia), every constituent of degree |G:T|·ψ(1) where ψ(1) = e·θ(1) (induce_inertia_constituent_apply_one_eq + restrict_eq_restrictionMultiplicity_smul_of_invariant — the book's χᵢ(1) = |G:T|·e·θ(1)), and uniform multiplicity e across constituents (induce_inertia_constituents_apply_one_eq + inner_induce_constituent_eq_of_apply_one_eq — the book's Ind = e·Σχᵢ), plus the derived-subgroup specialization (12.5) consumes. Only the numeric count n = |T:H|/e² has no named statement (few-line corollary of the e-uniform decomposition + card_mul_inner_self_induce_eq_card_inertia). (a): the irreducibility half ([Is] Thm 6.11) is fully general (CliffordCorrespondence.lean, θ-part counting, no abelian/coprime hypotheses); the general distinctness of the χᵢ (injectivity of Ind_T^G on Irr(T|θ)) and the verbatim Σeᵢχᵢ packaging remain unstated (distinctness is named only inside the abelian packagings via norm count). (c) fully formalized — under WEAKER coprimality (Coprime(|T:H|, o(det θ)·θ(1))) — as exists_extension_induce_eq_sum_distinct_irreducible, with distinctness, count |T:H|, degrees, multiplicity one. Remaining: general (a)-distinctness + the e² count, effort S (not M); nothing downstream is blocked.

results.name: Degree bound ψ(1) ≤ |G|/√(|C||D|) for B ⊴ C, B ⊆ Ker ψ, D/B ⊆ Z(C/B)
results.notes: Full strength, but shelved under an S08 label: theta_degree_le_index_mul_sqrt_index (OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S08_YsetInner/CharacterBreaks.lean, docstring-cited as the '(6.2) θ-bound') states θ(1) ≤ |K:C|·√|C:D|, which is algebraically identical to the book's |G|/√(|C||D|). Slightly stronger hypothesis-wise: only N ⊆ Ker(Res_C θ) is required rather than the book's global B ⊆ Ker ψ. Assembled from the a-half (induced-constituent degree bound) and the b-half [Is] Cor 2.30 (SchurCenterBound.lean, finrank_sq_le_index).

results.name: Cyclotomic Galois action: (a) Aut(ℚ_a) extends to Aut(ℚ_n) fixing ℚ_b; (b) automorphism v with χ^v(g) = χ(g^k) on a-elements, χ(g) on a'-elements
results.notes: Full strength, realized at ℂ ≃+* ℂ instead of Aut(ℚ_n) (deliberate: the repo's Galois-transport infra is parameterized by automorphisms of ℂ; every automorphism of ℚ_a is ζ ↦ ζ^k, so the CRT form covers the book's arbitrary u). (b) is strictly stronger than the book: one σ works uniformly for ALL virtual characters φ ∈ ℤ[Irr G] simultaneously (the book states it per character). In OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/CyclotomicGaloisAction.lean, including the transcendence-basis extension lemma for subfields of ℂ.

results.name: Cyclotomic congruences: (a) χ(xy) ≡ χ(y) mod (1−ε) for x of order p commuting with y; (b) n ∈ ℤ, (1−ε) ∣ n ⟹ p ∣ n
results.notes: Full strength in OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/CyclotomicCharacterCongruence.lean. (a) G-form: any finite group, ψ ∈ ℤ[Irr G], x^p = 1 (weaker than the book's 'order p') commuting with y, ψ(xy) − ψ(y) = (1−ε)·(algebraic integer) — the mod-(1−ε)-in-Z[η] congruence rendered via global algebraic integers of ℂ (matching Coq), reduced to the abelian ⟨x,y⟩ case. (b) both an abstract p-th cyclotomic-field form and the ℂ-form actually consumed by (12.16)/(13.5).

units.summary: Peterfalvi §3 (results (1.1)–(1.10)) is essentially complete: 8 of 10 results are fully formalized sorry-free, and the two remaining ((1.5), (1.7)) are partial only in specific sub-parts. The formalization is heavily factored away from the S03 files themselves into OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/** (a bespoke ClassFunction character theory — BrauerPermutation, SupportedSpanOrthogonality, IsometryDifferencePair, InducedIrreducible, CliffordCorrespondence/Decomposition, InducedInvariantConstituent, CyclotomicGaloisAction, CyclotomicCharacterCongruence), and is frequently STRONGER than the book: (1.1) comes with a full unconditional Brauer permutation lemma, (1.9.b) produces one automorphism uniform over all virtual characters, (1.10.a) needs only x^p=1, (1.7.c) needs only a weaker coprimality, and (1.8) — hiding under an S08 '(6.2) θ-bound' label — weakens the kernel hypothesis. The genuine gaps: (1.5.d)'s verbatim formula and the general-normal-subgroup packaging of (1.5.e) are unstated (though compositions of proved general lemmas, effort S), and for (1.7) only the numeric count n = |T:H|/e² and the general (1.7.a) distinctness packaging lack named statements (effort S). Nothing in this unit is covered by mathlib, which lacks induced-character/Clifford theory at this level. One stale docstring in S03_PreliminaryCharacter.lean claims the (1.6.a) converse 'is not formalised here' while a later section of the same file proves it. SLIM-PASS CORRECTIONS: refuted the earlier draft's claim that general (1.7.b) is missing — it IS formalized coprimality-free in InducedInvariantConstituent.lean (e-scaled decomposition into irreducibles, equal degrees |G:T|·e·θ(1), uniform multiplicity e, via the book's own regular-character argument), so (1.7) stays partial only for the e² count and general (a)-distinctness (effort M→S); the (1.5) partial label was confirmed (general pieces of (e) all exist, named composition only Frobenius-specialized); and (1.2)/(1.3)/(1.4) were verified at full book strength by reading the Lean statements.
units.unit: Peterfalvi §3 Preliminary Results from Character Theory, results (1.1)-(1.10)

results.name: Coprime coset collapse: Hg is the disjoint union of |H:C_H(g)| H-conjugates of C_H(g)g
results.notes: Lives OUTSIDE the book tree, in OddOrder/GroupTheory/CoprimeConjugacy.lean (sorry-free). Full strength: set equality Hg = union of H-conjugates of C_H(g)g, the count |K|=|H| (card_cosetConjImage), and the disjointness/rigidity (mem_centralizer_of_coset_conj_eq: equal conjugates force same C_H(g)-coset). The pi-part extraction is replaced by a CRT exponent (exists_pow_eq_self_and_forall_pow_eq_one) — no prime-set machinery needed. Fiber-count refinements used by (2.10) are in S04_InduceConjFinset.lean.

results.name: Dade hypothesis: A ⊆ L ⊆ N_G(A), L-fusion, C_G(a) = H(a) ⋊ C_L(a), coprimality
results.notes: Bundled structure in S04_DadeIsometryBasic.lean. Faithful: (a) = conj_in_L, (b) = centralizer_eq_sup + centralizer_disjoint + H_normalized (the ⋊), (c) = centralizer_coprime; plus subset_sharp (A ⊆ G#) and L_normalizes_A (the L ⊆ N_G(A) half). Used pervasively downstream (S05-S16, FeitThompsonCharacterData). Verified at source: all book clauses present at full strength (the only immaterial difference is that A-nonemptiness is not required, which only weakens nothing).

results.name: A is a TI-subset with normalizer L iff Hypothesis (2.2) holds with all H(a)=1
results.notes: Both directions proved, in the repo's relative-normalizer API (IsTISubset A L with A ⊆ L and L-normalization as side hypotheses); the book's closing remark N_G(A) = L is not restated as a separate equation but is immediate from the predicate. The repo even strengthens the reverse direction: EVERY (2.2) datum over a TI pair has H(a)=⊥ (H_eq_bot_of_isTISubset), giving uniqueness of the datum — stronger than the book.

results.name: (a) H(a^x)=H(a)^x for x∈L; (b) conjugate cosets aH(a), bH(b) force a ~_L b; (c) N_G(aH(a)) = C_G(a)
results.notes: Label verified against source (refutation attempted, failed). (b) fully proved (isConj_in_L_of_mul_H, via the CRT cross-rigidity isConj_of_isConj_mul). (a) is NOT derived from (2.2) in general: the S04_DadeIsometryBasic.lean docstring explicitly says HConjInvariant 'is kept as a predicate for now because the proof in the book identifies H(a) with a π'-core of C_G(a), and that π-core API is not yet part of the S04 scaffold'; it is threaded as an EXTRA assumption through (2.6)-(2.10) and proved only per-instance (all H(a)=⊥; restriction; concrete constructed data in S12_TypeIIDadeBase/S12_TypeIIFrobenius/S14_MaximalI/S15 files). Both halves of the general proof already exist (mem_H_of_mem_centralizer_coprime gives ⊇ after conjugation, card_centralizer_eq + card_centralizerIn_conj close the cardinality), so it remains a short S-effort lemma. (c) is absent as a normalizer-set equation (no analog of Coq norm_Dade_cover / Dade_cover_TI in PFsection2.v); however its functional content — the conjugating set 𝒜(g, H(a)a) is a single left coset of C_G(a) — IS proved (OddOrder.GroupTheory.card_conj_fiber and the textbook-remark form card_conjFiber_coset_eq_card_centralizer in S04_InduceConjFinset.lean), which is exactly what (2.7)/(2.10.3) consume, so nothing downstream is blocked.

results.name: The Dade map α ↦ α^τ: α^τ(g) = α(a) on (aH(a))^G, 0 elsewhere; well-definedness
results.notes: Verified at source: honest pointwise construction over any CommRing k (book: ℂ), no HConjInvariant needed. Well-definedness (dadeValue_eq) is exactly (2.4.b). Extras beyond the book: characterizing predicate IsDadeMap + uniqueness, k-linearity (dadeLinearMap), conjugation/star-compatibility (dadeMap_conj), support geometry (exists_base_of_map_apply_ne_zero).

results.name: Dade isometry: (a) (α^τ,β^τ)_G = (α,β)_L; (b) τ maps ℤ[Irr L, A] into ℤ[Irr G]
results.notes: Both parts honestly PROVED (sorry-free), bundled as fullDadeIsometryData — (a) via the (2.7) adjoint formula, (b) via the full (2.10) inclusion-exclusion. Sole narrowing vs the book: every statement takes the extra hypothesis hconj : hyp.HConjInvariant (= (2.4.a)), which the book derives from (2.2); once the (2.4) gap closes, this specialization disappears mechanically. All repo consumers (S05-S16, FT spine) discharge hconj, so nothing is conditional in practice.

results.name: Adjoint formula: (α^τ, χ)_G = (α, ψ)_L where ψ(a) = |H(a)|⁻¹ Σ_{x∈H(a)} χ(ax)
results.notes: Main equality fully proved for any IsDadeMap, with ψ an explicit input matching the averaging on A (so the book's 'in particular ψ = Res χ' case is a direct instantiation; the τβ-instance needed for (2.6.a) is adjointAverageFun_dadeMap_eq). Takes hconj (used for the orbit count sum_card_centralizerIn_eq, replacing the book's appeal to (2.4)); same shared (2.4.a) caveat as (2.6). Heaviest external export of §4 — applied directly in S07/S08/S09/S12/S13/S16.

results.name: M(B) = H(B) ⋊ N_L(B) for nonempty B ⊆ A
results.notes: Complete semidirect package: H(B)=⋂H(a) (hIntersection), N_L(B) built by hand as the L-set-stabilizer, disjointness H(B) ∩ N_L(B) = 1 (no hconj needed, matching the book), normality of H(B) and the IsComplement' decomposition plus |M(B)| = |H(B)|·|N_L(B)| (these need hconj, exactly where the book invokes (2.4.a)). Same shared (2.4.a) caveat.

results.name: α_B = α ∘ f_B ∈ CF(M(B)), f_B : M(B) → L with kernel H(B); preserves virtual characters
results.notes: f_B realized as M(B) → M(B)/H(B) ≅ N_L(B) ↪ L via the (2.8) IsComplement'; ker f_B = H(B) proved; the defining equation α_B(hx) = α(x) is alphaB_apply_mul; virtual-character preservation is alphaB_mem_ZIrr. Needs hconj (through the (2.8) complement) — same shared (2.4.a) caveat.

results.name: Inclusion-exclusion identity α^τ = -Σ_{B∈ℬ} (-1)^{|B|} Ind_{M(B)}^G α_B
results.notes: The full pointwise identity is proved (dadeMap_eq_neg_sum_mobiusTermCF): support side via a 5-step pipeline (orbit-averaging the transversal to the powerset, per-B weight collapse |orbit B|·|N_L(B)|=|L|, double-sum swap, toggle-a involution cancelling 𝒫(a) down to the B={a} survivor -|C_L(a)|, then Σ_{b∈a^L}|C_L(b)|=|L|); off-support side via (2.10.3) vanishing. Spread over S04_InduceConjFinset.lean + S04_DadeIsometry/MobiusAssembly.lean + S04_DadeIsometry.lean — far more granular than the book's one-page computation but faithful to it. Takes hconj — shared (2.4.a) caveat.

results.name: L-conjugation invariance: Ind_{M(B^x)}^G α_{B^x} = Ind_{M(B)}^G α_B
results.notes: Fully proved including the constituent conjugations H(B^x)=H(B)^x, N_L(B^x)=N_L(B)^x, M(B^x)=M(B)^x and the α_B transport. Takes hconj (the book proof cites (2.4.a) here too) — shared caveat.

results.name: C_{H(B)}(a) = H(B ∪ {a})
results.notes: Stated as C_G(a) ⊓ H(B) = H(insert a B); proved at full strength from Hypothesis (2.2) alone (no HConjInvariant), via the O_{pi'}-containment mem_H_of_mem_centralizer_coprime — exactly the book argument.

results.name: Evaluation of Ind_{M(B)}^G α_B: zero off ∪(aH(a))^G; on it, (α(a)/|M(B)|)·Σ_{b∈N_L(B)∩a^L}|𝒜(g,H(B)b)|
results.notes: Both cases proved: vanishing off the Dade support and the value formula (the b-sum over N_L(B) ∩ a^L with conjugating-set 𝒜(g,H(B)b) cardinalities, via the coprime membership test exists_mem_H_isConj_of_mem_conjFiber_coset using (2.1)/(2.2.c)). Takes hconj — shared caveat.

results.name: Restriction: Hypothesis (2.2) passes to L-stable A₁ ⊆ A, and τ₁ = τ restricted to CF(L,A₁)
results.notes: Verified at source: both claims proved at full strength. Hypothesis.restrict builds the (2.2) datum on A₁ field-by-field (genuine construction, H(a) inherited), and dadeMap_restrict shows the constructed Dade map of the restriction equals the domain-restriction of the original, proved via the (2.5) uniqueness IsDadeMap.unique. Also lifted to the bundled DadeIsometryData/FullDadeIsometryData packages; no HConjInvariant needed for the map equality itself.

units.unit: Peterfalvi §4 The Dade Isometry, results (2.x)
units.summary: Peterfalvi §4 (The Dade Isometry, results (2.1)-(2.11)) is essentially complete and entirely sorry-free: every numbered result including the three sub-lemmas (2.10.1)-(2.10.3) has a genuine Lean counterpart, spread over OddOrder/GroupTheory/CoprimeConjugacy.lean (for (2.1)) and the ~4,500-line S04 tree, and the main theorem (2.6) is an honest construction (Hypothesis.fullDadeIsometryData) including the full (2.10) Möbius/inclusion-exclusion proof of virtual-character preservation. The one real gap is (2.4.a): H(a^x) = H(a)^x is never derived from Hypothesis (2.2) in general — it is carried as an extra predicate HConjInvariant threaded as a hypothesis through (2.6)-(2.10) and discharged per-instance downstream (trivial-H TI cases and constructed §12/§14/§15 data); since the repo already has both needed halves (mem_H_of_mem_centralizer_coprime, card_centralizer_eq), closing it is well under a day and would mechanically de-specialize all the hconj-carrying statements. (2.4.c) (N_G(aH(a)) = C_G(a)) is absent as a normalizer equation, but its functional single-coset content and its only book use — the orbit count in (2.7)/(2.10.3) — are proved (card_conj_fiber / card_conjFiber_coset_eq_card_centralizer / sum_card_centralizerIn_eq), so nothing depends on it. Notable differences from the book: (2.1) is factored as a general coprime-conjugacy primitive with the pi-part argument replaced by a single CRT exponent, the repo adds uniqueness statements beyond the book ((2.5) IsDadeMap.unique; every (2.2) datum over a TI pair has H = ⊥), and the Dade map is constructed over any commutative coefficient ring rather than just ℂ. Slim verification pass: the (2.4) partial label was confirmed against source after refutation attempts (the S04 docstring itself records that the general (2.4.a) derivation awaits π-core API; no (2.4.c) normalizer statement exists, though its coset-form content card_conjFiber_coset_eq_card_centralizer was found and added to the notes), the three most load-bearing formalized entries ((2.2), (2.5), (2.11)) were read at source and confirmed full book strength, and all spot-checked Lean names exist — no status changes were needed.

results.name: TI-cyclic setup: W = W1 x W2 cyclic of odd order, V = W - (W1 ∪ W2) a TI-subset with normalizer W
results.notes: OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S05_TICyclic.lean. Also viewed as the H(a)=1 specialization of the §4 Dade Hypothesis (2.2).

results.name: Linear isometry σ : CF(W) → CF(G) preserving virtual characters, with (a) σ = Ind on CF(W,V), (b) 1_W^σ = 1_G, (c) σ is identity on V, (d) Irr(G) off Im σ vanishes on V
results.notes: S05_SigmaIsometry.lean (capstone exists_sigma bundles all six conjuncts); (a) via tau_eq_induce (the §4 Dade map IS induction, from isDadeMap_inducedDadeMap in S05_NormThree.lean); (d) stated in the stronger orthogonality form (any χ ∈ CF(G) ⊥ σ(Irr W) vanishes on V), which implies the book form. Statements take a FullDadeApplication parameter, but this is honestly constructible from (3.1) alone (S04 Hypothesis.fullDadeIsometryData + HConjInvariant.of_forall_H_eq_bot; done concretely in S06_CertainTypeCharacters.toTICyclicFullDadeApplication), so no free hypothesis. Integral (ℤ-linear) repackaging in S05_IntegralSigma.lean.

results.name: The linear characters ω_{ij} of W (ω_{i0} trivial on W2, ω_{0j} trivial on W1, ω_{ij} = ω_{i0}·ω_{0j}), exhausting Irr(W)
results.notes: S05_TICyclic.lean + index bridge in S05_Isometry32.lean. Indexed by the dual groups Hom(W_k, ℂˣ) instead of integers 0 ≤ i < w_k; omegaIrrEquiv : Ĉ₁ × Ĉ₂ ≃ Irr(W) is the 'Irr(W) = {ω_ij}' claim. A Fin |W1| × Fin |W2| re-indexing with 0 ↦ trivial (the book's literal indexing) exists as omegaGrid in S05_OmegaGrid.lean; the spanning fact Fourier expansion in S05_OmegaSpanning.lean.

results.name: The family α_{ij} = 1_W − ω_{i0} − ω_{0j} + ω_{ij} (i,j ≥ 1) is a basis of CF(W,V); dim CF(W,V) = (w1−1)(w2−1)
results.notes: S05_TICyclic.lean. Follows the book proof exactly: α defined as the product (1−ω_{i0})(1−ω_{0j}) hence supported on V, expansion into the 4-term ω-combination, biorthogonality against ω_{ij}, and the dimension count |V| = (w1−1)(w2−1) (card_supportInSubgroup_Vdiff + finrank_supportedSubmodule_eq_card).

results.name: Existence of the orthonormal family (χ_{ij}) ⊂ ZIrr(G) with χ_{00} = 1_G and Ind_W^G α_{ij} = 1_G − χ_{i0} − χ_{0j} + χ_{ij}
results.notes: Full statement = exists_chiFamily (S05_Isometry32.lean), covering all three case orientations (w1,w2 ≥ 5; w1 ≥ 5, w2 = 3; w1 = 3, w2 ≥ 5 — the book's 'w2 = 3 the proof is complete' plus symmetry). The proof-internal numbered steps are all present: (3.5.1) norm-3/Gram facts (S05_NormThree.lean: beta Gram matrix, Frobenius ⟨Ind α,1⟩ = 1; S05_SignedTripleGrid.lean: norm-3 virtual character = signed triple), (3.5.2) L/O lemmas (SignedTripleGrid + family forms in Isometry32), (3.5.3) sup(w1,w2) ≥ 5 (sup_card_ge_five), (3.5.4) sunflower |⋂A_{i1}| = 1 including the Case I/II sub-analysis (3.5.4.1)-(3.5.4.6) (abstract form SignedTripleGrid:1351, existsUnique_common), (3.5.5) decomposition β_{ij} = −χ_{i0} − χ_{0j} + χ_{ij} (gridFamily/symm_orthonormal_family/two_col_orthonormal_family). results.name: Coefficient decomposition ψ = Σ a_{ij} ω_{ij}^σ + β with β ⊥ Im σ, ψ vanishing on V; NC(ψ) = #{(i,j) | a_{ij} ≠ 0}

results.name: Additive separability of the coefficient grid: a_{ij} + a_{i'j'} = a_{ij'} + a_{i'j} (in particular a_{ij} = a_{i0} + a_{0j} − a_{00})
results.notes: S05_SigmaIsometry.lean. Book proof followed exactly (test element ω_{ij}+ω_{i'j'}−ω_{ij'}−ω_{i'j} ∈ CF(W,V), support disjointness). results.name: Trichotomy: if w1 < w2 and NC(ψ) < 2w1 then ψ = β, or ψ = a·Σ_i ω_{ij}^σ + β (one column), or ψ = a·Σ_j ω_{ij}^σ + β (one row)

Conclusions phrased as constant-nonzero single column/row of the coefficient grid, from which the book's NC(ψ) = w1 / = w2 counts are immediate. Beyond the book, the repo adds the (3.8)-consequence norm-2 rigidity eq_signed_sub_cTIiso (Coq PFsection3) as orthonormalGrid_diff_rigidity (S05_GridRigidity.lean) + Dade-image endgames (S05_SigmaTrichotomy.lean), used by (4.8)/(10.5)/§13.

results.name: (a) χ ∈ ±Irr(G) with χ|_V = ω|_V implies χ = ω^σ, and σ commutes with field automorphisms; (b) (ω^k)^σ = ω^{σu} and value-agreement at g of order prime to a; (c) ω^σ(g) ∈ ℤ for g of order prime to a

(b): u realized via the (1.9) CRT root-of-unity automorphism exists_complexRingEquiv_pow_and_fixed; k coprime to a = orderOf ξ. units.unit: Peterfalvi §5 (book §3): TI-Subsets with Cyclic Normalizers, results (3.1)-(3.9)
units.summary: The unit is 100% formalized and sorry-free: all nine numbered items (3.1)-(3.9), including every proof-internal numbered step of (3.5) ((3.5.1)-(3.5.5) with the (3.5.4.x) case analysis) and (3.8) ((3.8.1)-(3.8.3)), have full-strength Lean counterparts spread over 12 S05_* leaves (~7,100 lines) under OddOrder/Peterfalvi/. The formalization is factored more abstractly than the book: the (3.5) sunflower combinatorics is an abstract IsSignedTripleGrid theory, the (3.8) trichotomy is a module-generic grid lemma (grid_trichotomy) reused by §13/§15, V in Hypothesis (3.1) is kept abstract (with hVeq pinning the explicit W∖(W1∪W2) shape) so §6/§8 can reuse the interface, and the Dade-map input to (3.2) is a parameter that is honestly constructible from (3.1) via the §4 machinery (done in S06.toTICyclicFullDadeApplication). Several results are strictly stronger than the book: (3.9)(a)'s Galois commutation holds for arbitrary ring automorphisms of ℂ, and the repo adds beyond-book (3.8)-consequences (norm-2 rigidity orthonormalGrid_diff_rigidity, Dade-image endgames) plus integral/Fin-indexed repackagings (S05_IntegralSigma, S05_OmegaGrid, S05_OmegaSigmaGrid) serving the §10-16 spine. No gaps; nothing in this unit is missing, partial, or covered by mathlib alone.

results.notes: S06_CertainTypeClifford.lean. units.unit: Peterfalvi §6 — The Dade Isometry for a Certain Type of Subgroup, results (4.1)-(4.10)
units.summary: Peterfalvi §6 is completely formalized and sorry-free: every numbered result (4.1)-(4.10) has a Lean counterpart at full book strength, spread across eleven S06_*.lean files (~6,450 lines) plus (4.1) in OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/InducedIrreducible.lean. There are no gaps; this unit sat on the FT critical path (it is the character-theoretic engine behind the §8 coherence and the S12/S15/S16 endgame) and was driven to closure, with (4.8) and (4.9) heavily instantiated downstream including in the FT spine files. The formalization is finer-grained and in places strictly stronger than the book: (4.5)(b) additionally proves the exact count of w2 reducible-induced characters and injectivity of induction on them, (4.9) also delivers the R(mu_j) orthonormal family needed for (5.3.b) and its conjugation involution, and Hypothesis (4.6) is split into a Dade-free structural core plus the full Dade-carrying bundle for reuse. Two factoring notes rather than gaps: (4.9)(b) is stated as the §7 IsCoherent predicate for the Dade map (exactly the isometry-coinciding-with-tau content), and the (4.9)(a) lattice equality Z[T,L^#] = Z[T,A] appears as its two working halves (difference support in A + generation of Z[T,A] by column differences) instead of a verbatim set equality.

results.name: Coherence of (S, A, tau): isometric extension of tau from Z[S,A] to Z[S]
results.notes: OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S07_Coherence/NormInequalities.lean:480. Structure with fields nonzero (Z[S,A] != 0), extension, extension_inner_eq (isometry on the lattice Z[S]), extends_on_supported (agrees with tau on Z[S,A]), extension_mem_ZIrr (codomain Z[Irr G]). Matches the book definition; the isometry is deliberately lattice-relative (a global CF(L)->CF(G) isometry cannot exist when dim CF(L) > dim CF(G)), which is exactly what the book constructs. Galois transport IsCoherent.galoisTransport also provided.

results.name: Subcoherence hypotheses (a)-(e): conjugate-closed non-real S, lattice isometry, pairwise orthogonality, difference images R(chi), cross-orthogonality
results.notes: NormInequalities.lean:588 (field-for-field transcription of Coq subcoherent S tau R). The bundled record carries the 2-element R(chi) (CharacterDifferenceImage) suited to irreducible members; the general variable-length (5.2.d) family (needed for reducible mu_j, |R| = 2*w1) is OrthonormalCharacterImageFamily (DifferenceImage.lean:778), against which all downstream machinery ((5.4)-(5.7)) is stated. Both carriers sorry-free.

results.name: (a) S subset Irr L implies Hypothesis (5.2); (b) Hypothesis (5.2) for induced certain-type families under Hyp (4.6), with R(phi) orthogonal to the sigma-grid rider
results.notes: (a) fully formalized at book strength: irrSubcoherent (S07_Subcoherent.lean:129, Coq irr_subcoherent) assembles the six-field S07.Hypothesis; the per-member R-datum producer characterDifferenceImageOfIsometry derives (5.2.d) from ||tau(chi-chibar)||^2 = 2; subset restriction (Coq subset_subcoherent) also ported. (b) all content proven sorry-free but distributed, and partly at FT-instance generality: the reducible R(mu_j) = {delta_j w_ij^sigma, -delta_j w_ik^sigma} with orthonormality and (5.2.d) image equation lives at abstract Hypothesis46 level (S06_CertainTypeCoherence); (5.2.e) reducible-reducible at Hypothesis46; irr-reducible at Sibley-Dade level (S08_CaseBHortho); the rider R(phi) perp omega^sigma for all omega in Irr W only as type-II / type-P / at-T instances (S12_TypeIIColumnPin:298, S15_NuRowPin:181). No single bundled '(5.2) holds for the mixed family' statement — deliberately, since the fixed 2-element record cannot hold variable-length R; consumers use the general-family (5.7) engine instead.

results.name: Norm inequalities for the decomposition (chi - psi)^tau1 = X - Y against R(chi): (a) ||X||^2 >= ||chi||^2; (b) if ||Y||^2 >= ||psi||^2 then equalities and X = sum over E subset R(chi)
results.notes: NormInequalities.lean:28/301/383. Full book strength for general psi and general norms; conclusion (b) additionally records |E| = ||chi||^2 (used by (5.6.3)). The X/Y/coeff data is computed (not posited) by the smart constructor ofProjection via integral projection onto R(chi). Integer Cauchy-Schwarz infra in ZIrrFourier.

results.name: chi^tau1 = sum over E subset R(chi) for any isometry tau1 on Z[chi, chibar] agreeing with tau on chi - chibar (psi = 0 case of (5.4))
results.notes: NormInequalities.lean:445. Concludes Y = 0, tau1(chi) = X = sum over E, |E| = ||chi||^2. The book's most-cited section-5 hub (11 forward cites); consumed everywhere via the psi = 0 decompositions (memberExtensionDecomposition, certainTypeSeedDecomposition etc.).

results.name: Coherence union: S1 coherent + chi1(1) | chi(1) + 2 chi(1) chi1(1) < sum chi_i(1)^2/||chi_i||^2 imply S1 union {chi, chibar} coherent (sub-steps 5.6.1-5.6.3)
results.notes: Fully formalized, factored as an engine rather than one named theorem (mirrors Coq PFsection5). Sub-steps: (5.6.1) = CharacterFamilyBundle + crossDifference_inner + Y-decomposition; (5.6.2) = lambda_eq_zero_and_Z_eq_zero (integer quadratic forcing with the exact book inequality (c) as hD : 2a < sum (a_i/||chi_i||^2)^2 * ||chi_i||^2) collapsing Y = a*chi1^tau1; (5.6.3) = retarget_isCoherent* adjoining engines (CoherenceUnion.lean). One assembled book-shaped step: DadeChainStep (FamilyBundleDade.lean:1406) carries exactly the book hypotheses — (a) coherent S1, (b) a : Nat with chi(1) = a*chi1(1), (c) hdeg_c — and DadeChainStep.advance produces IsCoherent of the union; iteration via coherentPairChain / peterfalvi_66_coherence_of_X_from_dade. Reducible break characters (||chi||^2 > 1, book allows them) are handled by the scaled analogues S07_RetargetScaled (retargetS) + S08_RetargetReducible; the repo even has a strictly stronger norm-weighted variant (S08_CoherenceWeighted) beyond the book.

results.name: Constant-degree coherence: under Hypothesis (5.2), if chi(1) is constant on S then S is coherent
results.notes: Full book strength and more: uniform_degree_coherence_of_families (S07_PivotCoherence.lean:793, Coq uniform_degree_coherence) is norm-general — members may be reducible characters (the certain-type mu-columns of norm w1), exactly as the book's S allows; coherent_of_constant_degree (S07_CoherenceConstantDegree.lean:574) is the all-irreducible one-shot route following the book proof directly. All sorry-free.

results.name: Image of a reducible column mu_k under a coherent extension: mu_k^tau1 = delta_k sum_i w_ik^sigma or -delta_k sum_i w_ij^sigma, plus the second-case uniqueness rider
results.notes: The two-branch dichotomy is proven sorry-free as typeII_nu_tau2_dichotomy (S12_TypeIIColumnPin.lean:794) for the type-II S-side column, and the aligned positive-sign pin (the book's use of the rider when S contains an irreducible) as coherent_sOf_H0C_extension_muColumnSum_pin_of_irr (S13_Orthogonality.lean:292) for the type-III/IV S(H0C) family — i.e. at the FT maximal-subgroup instances rather than one abstract theorem at (4.6)/(5.3.b) generality. The abstract analytic core is fully general (S05_SigmaTrichotomy: V-vanishing sigma-coefficient grid, Fourier reconstruction, grid_eq_const_column_of_two_col at TICyclicHypothesis level), so an abstract restatement would be assembly work only. The literal uniqueness rider ('j and k are the only indices with mu_l in S of that degree' in the second case) has no direct Lean counterpart; the applications derive alignment by supplementary arguments instead (irreducible-member gamma-trick, third-column via Theorem (4.9)).

results.name: (a) coherent extensions commute with field automorphisms of Q_|G| on S; (b) for Supp(chi) in A union {1}, (chi - chibar)^tau = mu - mubar for some mu in Irr G
results.notes: (a) S07_CoherenceGalois.lean:109: full strength — arbitrary ring automorphism sigma_c of C (covers the book's Aut(Q_|G|), and even the wild extensions, since no star-commutation is needed), S subset Irr L, |S| >= 2, the span condition Z[S,L#] = Z[S,A] in unfolded form; the uniform-sign argument is the book's. (b) DifferenceImage.lean:1131: nu_eq_mu_conj derives nu = mubar (so tau(chi - chibar) = eps(mu - mubar), sign absorbed by renaming) from tau commuting with conjugation on the difference, which the Dade map satisfies on A-supported functions via dadeIntegralCharacterMap_mapRingEquiv_comm — the book's support hypothesis enters exactly there. Both sorry-free.

units.summary: Peterfalvi section 5 "Coherence" (repo S07, results (5.1)-(5.9)) is essentially completely formalized and entirely sorry-free — it is one of the most heavily developed units in the repo, spread over S07_Coherence/ (5 leaves), S07_{Subcoherent,CoherenceConstantDegree,PivotCoherence,RetargetScaled,CoherenceGalois,BridgeCoherent} and consumer-side leaves in S06/S08/S12/S13. (5.1), (5.2), (5.4), (5.5), (5.7), (5.9) are at full book strength; (5.6) is fully present but factored Coq-style into an engine ((5.6.1) family bundle + (5.6.2) integer-forcing with the exact degree inequality (c) + (5.6.3) retarget adjoining, assembled book-shaped in DadeChainStep.advance and iterated by coherentPairChain), with the reducible-break case and a strictly-stronger norm-weighted variant added beyond the book. The only generality gaps are (5.3)(b) and (5.8): all their mathematical content is proven, but the mixed irreducible/reducible (5.2.e) cross-orthogonality rider and the mu-column image dichotomy/pin are proven at the FT maximal-subgroup instances (Sibley-Dade, type-II, type-P S(H0C)) rather than as single abstract theorems at Hypothesis (4.6) generality, and (5.8)'s second-case uniqueness rider has no direct counterpart (applications derive sign alignment by other proven routes). Surprising strengths: (5.7) is norm-general (accepts reducible members, Coq uniform_degree_coherence), and (5.9)(a) is proven for arbitrary automorphisms of C without star-commutation, wider than the book's Q_|G| setting.
units.unit: Peterfalvi §7 (book section 5) Coherence, results (5.1)-(5.9)

results.name: Setup: K solvable normal in L, S = induced family {Ind_K^L θ}, filtration S(A) for normal A ≤ K
results.notes: Three carriers: SsubFiltration (S08_YsetConjugation.lean:43, Sibley instance K=H), inducedKernelFamily (S08_SixTwoGeneral.lean:53, general solvable kernel K ≤ L, matching Coq seqIndD, with the full mem/antitone/finite/conj-closed/anchor lemma suite), and abstract FiltrationData/DescentHypothesis (S08_YsetInner.lean). Faithful to book incl. reducible members for general K.

results.name: Coherence-break index bound: S(A) coherent, S(B) not, D/B ⊆ Z(C/B) ⟹ 2|L:C|√|C:D| ≥ |K:A|−1
results.notes: Fully proved (sorry-free) for the Sibley kernel K=H: six_two/six_two_central (Frobenius c1, S08_CoherenceCorePart2/SibleyBounds.lean:585/642) and _c2 variants (S08_Theorem65c2.lean). The general-(6.1) form six_two_general (S08_Theorem62_63_Standalone.lean:348) proves the θ-degree bound and arithmetic in full but takes the (5.6) break-member bound as an explicit oracle h56; that character-theoretic core (break pair with possibly-REDUCIBLE induced members of a solvable K) is built in S08_SixTwoGeneral.lean (inducedKernelFamily_SA_sum_le_two_psi_k, exists_coherentBreakPair_general) modulo per-member (5.2.d) decomposition data, and is fully discharged (sorry-free) in the §11–§13 consumer context (S12.Hypothesis muGrid data; S13_SixTwoBridge.lean:906 six_two_dichotomy_bound). No single unconditional general-K theorem; every instance the book uses is proved. Effort M = generic (5.2.d)-datum discharge for an arbitrary (6.1) instance.

results.name: Coherence descent: H/M nilpotent, S(H₁) coherent, |H:H₁| > 4|L:K|²+1 ⟹ S(M) coherent
results.notes: Sibley case (K=H, Frobenius) fully proved: six_three (SibleyBounds.lean:723; minimal-A/maximal-B descent, nilpotency-forces-centrality, √-arithmetic all done). General (6.1) form with K solvable ⊋ H: six_three_descent + six_three_of_six_two_oracle (S08_Theorem62_63_Standalone.lean:114/382) — everything proved except the (6.2) oracle h62/h56, which the §11–§13 consumers (S12_Noncoherence.lean:385, S13_Lemmas113To115.lean:87) discharge sorry-free. Slight specialization: repo assumes H itself nilpotent (book: H/M nilpotent); all book consumers have M=1 so this matches usage. Effort S given general (6.2).

results.name: Odd-order setup: (6.1) + |L| odd, K/M nilpotent, H₁/M = [K/M,K/M], L/H₁ Frobenius with kernel K/H₁
results.notes: Live encoding = SibleyDadeHypothesis (S08_CoherenceCorePart1.lean:494): odd |L|, H nilpotent normal ≠ ⊥, split L = H ⋊ W₁, TI, genuine §4 Dade datum — the K=H, M=1 instance the (6.8) capstone runs on; the Frobenius-quotient condition appears via cases/hF. General-M packaging exists only as the vestigial OddOrderSpecialization (S08_YsetInner.lean:377) whose quotient_nilpotent field is a free Prop (scaffolding, unused by the live chain); §11–§13 consumers restate (6.4)-shape hypotheses concretely instead.

results.name: If S(M) not coherent: (a) K/H₁ chief factor of L and |K:H₁| ≤ 4|L:K|²+1; (b) K/M non-abelian p-group; (c) |L:K| ∤ p−1
results.notes: All three parts' content proved sorry-free, factored as abstract cores + Sibley producers: (a) index bound = contrapositive of six_three (isPGroup_of_not_coherent, SibleyBounds.lean:776); chief-factor step as arithmetic contradiction (S08_CoherenceCorePart1.lean:67/111, two_mul_add_one_le_of_odd_dvd) rather than an explicit chief-factor conclusion; (b) p-group reduction in both FPF-Frobenius and c2 fixed-points-in-commutator forms (Part1:172/226, S08_PGroupReduction exists_isPGroup_H_of_{frobenius,c2}_of_card_le, incl. non-abelian p² ≤ |H:H′| via Burnside basis); (c) six_five_c_arith + the (6.5)(c) coherence producer nonempty_coherent_SOf_bot_of_index_dvd (S08_PGroupReduction.lean). Used at the (6.8) instance K=H, M=⊥; no single three-part statement under general (6.4).

results.name: For 1 ≠ Z ⊆ Z(K) normal with X = S − S(Z) ⊆ Irr L: X = {χ ∈ Irr L | Z ⊄ Ker χ} and X is coherent
results.notes: The X-characterization is proved generically in Z (S08_DegreeSums/CoherenceGlue.lean:489, exactly the book biconditional given X ⊆ Irr L). The coherence half — enumeration by degree, p-power degree divisibility ([Is] Cor 2.30 via degree_sq_le_index_of_central_quotient), repeated (5.6) adjoin steps — is proved sorry-free but only at the instances (6.8) consumes: Z = Z(H) ∩ H′ (Frobenius and c2-case-A, S08_CoherenceBasic.lean:1230/1265) and Z = W₂ (case B, S08_CaseBAnchoredSeed.lean:1314), driven by the generic adjoin-step engine (SibleyBounds.lean:1205). No standalone generic-Z (6.6) statement under bare Hypothesis (6.4).

results.name: Sylow-TI congruence: P Sylow, L = N_G(P) odd, P^# TI, Z ⊴ L in Z(P), |C_L(z)| constant, ψ ∈ Irr G constant on Z^# ⟹ ψ(z) ∈ ℤ and ψ(z) ≡ ψ(1) (mod |P|)
results.notes: Lives outside the book tree: OddOrder/GroupTheory/RepresentationTheory/{ClassSumAlgebra,ClassSumCongruence,SylowTICongruence}.lean. peterfalvi_67_of_odd (SylowTICongruence.lean:140) is the assembled odd-order form, faithful to the book setup; internal steps (6.7.1)–(6.7.3) exist as lemmas (fixed-point-free counting on class-product sets, collapsed structure-constant congruences, the trivial-character specialization a₁₁ ≡ 1 + a₁₂, coprime cancellation). Conclusion delivered as the algebraic-integer congruence [ALGMOD |P|]; the ψ(z) ∈ ℤ clause is factored to consumers (via isIntegral_rat_imp_int where Res_Z ψ decomposition supplies rationality) rather than concluded inside — full book content, slightly different packaging.

results.name: Main coherence theorem: L = H ⋊ W₁ odd, H nilpotent, H^# TI with normalizer L, (c1) Frobenius or (c2) Hypothesis (4.6) with w₂ prime, W₂ ⊆ [H,H] ⟹ S coherent
results.notes: Complete and sorry-free (S08_CoherenceTheorems.lean:52; ~38-leaf S08 tree). Hypotheses encoded faithfully: SibleyDadeHypothesis carries the genuine §4 Dade datum with dade_H_eq_bot (τ = Dade isometry agreeing with Ind on the supported lattice) and cases (c1) Frobenius ∨ (c2) full Hypothesis46 (incl. the ambient (3.1) TI-cyclic, deliberately strengthened 2026-06-13 after the weaker CertainTypeHypothesis encoding proved unfaithful) + w₂ prime + W₂ ≤ ⁅H,H⁆ + Hall coprimality (implied by book (4.2.a)). Proof dispatches X-empty / (c1) / (c2)-case-A (Z(H) ∩ W₂ = 1) / case-B (W₂ ⊆ Z(H), split W₂ ⊊ H′ bootstrap vs W₂ = H′ edge), i.e. all of (6.8.1)–(6.8.3) incl. the (6.7)-wiring (Sylow transfer sylow_map_subtype_of_coprime, η₁^τ₁ constancy). IsCoherent carries the extension as data, hence noncomputable def. Consumer interface to (7.10): IndChainDecomposition.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §8 (results (6.1)–(6.8)) is essentially fully covered, sorry-free, and was the workhorse of the FT character spine: the capstone Theorem (6.8) is proved at full book strength (sibleySetup_is_coherent) over a faithful hypothesis carrier (genuine Dade datum, full Hypothesis-(4.6) case (c2)), with all internal steps (6.7.1)–(6.7.3), (6.8.1)–(6.8.3) discharged, and (6.7) proved as a standalone general Sylow-TI congruence outside the book tree (peterfalvi_67_of_odd). The main deviation from the book is factoring, not gaps: (6.2)/(6.3) are unconditionally proved for the Sibley kernel K = H (both Frobenius and certain-type variants), while their general solvable-kernel (6.1) forms (six_two_general, six_three_of_six_two_oracle) expose the (5.6) break-member bound for reducible induced members as an oracle hypothesis that is fully discharged only in the §11–§13 consumer contexts (muGrid decomposition data) — every instance the book actually uses is proved, but no single unconditional general-K theorem exists. Similarly (6.5) and (6.6) are proved as abstract group-theoretic cores plus the Sibley-instance producers that (6.8) consumes (Z = Z(H) ∩ H′ and Z = W₂) rather than as packaged statements under general Hypothesis (6.4); the (6.5)(a) chief-factor clause exists only as contradiction arithmetic. Surprising strengths: the repo's case-B ((6.8.2)) machinery is substantially more developed than the book's two-page sketch, and (6.6)'s X-characterization avoids [Is] Lemma 2.21 entirely; one vestigial scaffold remains (OddOrderSpecialization with a free Prop field), unused by the live chain.
units.unit: Peterfalvi §8 Some Coherence Theorems, results (6.1)–(6.8)

results.name: Hypothesis (2.2) + Dade isometry τ; the averaging map ρ (χ^ρ(a) = |H(a)|⁻¹ Σ χ(ax)) and A^τ
results.notes: OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S09_NonexistenceCertain/Hypothesis71.lean. Structure bundles the S04 Hypothesis (2.2), a chosen Dade map with IsDadeMap, and H(-)-conjugation equivariance (needed to make χ^ρ a class function; automatic for TI-sets via of_isTISubset). A^τ is hyp.dadeSupport. Faithful to the book, sorry-free.

results.name: (a) α^{τρ} = α on CF(L,A); (b) ‖χ^ρ‖² ≤ ‖χ‖², equality iff χ ∈ im τ
results.notes: (a) fully proved, both pointwise on A and as class functions on L. (b): the inequality is proved via the adjoint formula + orthogonal decomposition (the book's proof), but the 'equality if and only if χ is in the image of τ' clause is nowhere stated or proved. Verified by targeted repo-wide search (book-number citations, eq_iff/norm_sq_eq name patterns, Dade-image membership iff, descriptive content): no match anywhere in OddOrder/. Coq analog leC_norm_invDade (PFsection7.v) carries the equality condition via mathcomp's lerif ('?= iff'), so the Lean form is strictly weaker than book/Coq on this clause. Its only downstream use at full strength (the 1_G equality case feeding (7.5)) is instead proved directly as the cardinality identity card_dadeSupport_div_card_G_eq_card_A_div_card_L. Adding the iff is easy from the existing decomposition ⟨χ,χ⟩ = ⟨φ,φ⟩ + ⟨χ−φ,χ−φ⟩ already in the proof of chiRho_norm_sq_le.

results.name: Integral inequality |G|⁻¹ Σ_{A^τ} |χ|² ≥ ‖χ^ρ‖², equality iff χ constant on each aH(a)
results.notes: The inequality is fully proved (book's proof: restrict χ to A^τ, apply (7.2.b)). The 'equality iff χ constant on every coset aH(a)' clause is not formalized — the theorem docstring states the iff but the statement carries only ≤; verified by repo-wide search (including the promisingly-named S14_MaximalI/RhoConstancy.lean, which is §12 material, not this). Coq analog leC_cfnorm_invDade_support carries the equality condition (lerif). The one place the book uses the equality case — χ = 1_G in (7.5), giving |A^τ|/|G| = |A|/|L| — is proved directly and sorry-free (card_dadeSupport_div_card_G_eq_card_A_div_card_L, via τ(1_A) = 1_{A^τ} exactly and isometry). chiRho_apply_eq_of_forall_coset gives the pointwise collapse under constancy (one direction ingredient).

results.name: Family (A_i, L_i, τ_i) each satisfying (7.1), with pairwise disjoint A_i^{τ_i}; G₀ = G − ⋃ A_i^{τ_i}
results.notes: Hypothesis71.lean. Indexed by Fin k rather than an arbitrary index set I (no loss: G is finite and the A_i^{τ_i} are disjoint nonempty, so I is finite). Carries per-index Fintype/Invertible instances as fields plus IsDadeIsometry for each τ_i.

results.name: Master family inequality: |G|⁻¹(Σ_{G₀}|χ|² − |G₀|) + Σ_i(‖χ^{ρ_i}‖² − |A_i|/|L_i|) ≤ 0
results.notes: Hypothesis71.lean:725. Statement re-verified this pass: exact displayed inequality, proved for any norm-one class function (book states it for χ ∈ Irr G — the Lean form is slightly more general, matching what the proof needs). Uses per-index (7.3) plus the 1_G cardinality identity; sorry-free. Confirmed full book strength.

results.name: Normal-subgroup case: H ⊴ L, A = H^#, T = {Ind_H^L θ | θ ∈ Irr H} = {ζ₀,…,ζₙ} distinct, degree ratios d_i
results.notes: NormalCase.lean (structure) + S09_Building78C.lean (constructors). The structure carries all book data (induced-ness, injectivity/distinctness, exhaustive cover, degree ratios, support facts) plus the (7.7.a) decomposition as a certificate field. Constructor signature re-verified this pass: hypothesis76OfDade (S09_Building78C.lean:1001) takes only Hypothesis71 + IsDadeIsometry + H ≤ L + L-conjugation-stability of H + A = H \ {1} — the certificate is genuinely discharged via chiRho_decomp_induced, nothing posited. Confirmed.

results.name: (a) explicit formula χ^ρ(x) = Σ_{i≥1} c̄_i/‖ζ_i‖² ζ_i(x); (b) double-sum formula for ‖χ^ρ‖²
results.notes: (a): at structure level it projects the Hypothesis76 certificate, but the honest content — the CF(L,A)-basis/spanning argument for induced families — is proved sorry-free as chiRho_decomp_induced (S09_Building78C.lean:750; statement re-verified this pass: takes only the induced family data hinj/hcover/hdeg/support + geometric facts, all dischargeable from (7.1)+normality) and wired into the hypothesis76OfDade constructor, so (a) holds at full book strength. (b) chiRho_norm_sq_double_sum (NormalCase.lean:393; statement re-verified this pass) is proved outright for any χ ∈ CF(G) under any Hypothesis76, exactly the book's formula ((ζ_i,ζ_j) − ζ_i(1)·conj(ζ_j(1))/|L|). Confirmed full book strength.

results.name: Coherent case: (a) β = 1_G − ζ^ν + a·Σ φ(1)/(e‖φ‖²) φ^ν + Γ with a ∈ ℤ, Γ ⊥ S^ν ∪ {1_G}; (b) under e ≤ (h−1)/2: ‖ζ^{νρ}‖² ≥ 1 − e/h and ‖Γ‖² ≤ e − 1; (c) χ ⊥ S^ν ⇒ χ^ρ(x) = (β,χ) and ‖χ^ρ‖² = (|A|/|L|)(β,χ)²
results.notes: All three parts have genuine sorry-free proofs, but factored differently from the book. (c) is at full book strength: chiRho_eq_inner_beta_induced proves the pointwise identity for any induced coherent family, hypothesis78OfDade constructs Hypothesis78 with the certificate discharged from (7.1)+coherence data alone, and the norm-square corollary (c.ii) is proved outright. (a): betaDecompOfFacts/betaDecompOfDade construct the full decomposition with integer a (exists_betaDecomp_a, via ZIrr integrality) — most source facts derived for induced families, but a few book-internal steps ((ζ^ν,1_G)=0, ‖ζ‖²=1) remain explicit parameters at the abstract level, discharged only in the Frobenius-family layer (S09_FrobeniusEstimate.hzeta0nu) and the S14 witness packages. (b): the two norm estimates are proved sorry-free per Frobenius-family member (hypothesis78_zetaNuRhoNormSq_ge_at, hypothesis78_gamma_inner_self_re_le); the abstract Hypothesis78-level form is a conditional assembly (normEstimates_of_*) parameterized by the u,v,w formula and source data. Every use the book makes of (7.8) — in (7.10) and in Pf §12/§14 — is covered; a single self-contained '(7.6)+coherent ⇒ (7.8.a)(b)' statement deriving all facts internally does not exist.

results.name: Two coherent families over odd-order G with disjoint A_i^{τ_i}: (β₁,ζ₂^{ν₂}) ≠ 0 or (β₂,ζ₁^{ν₁}) ≠ 0
results.notes: TwoFamilies.lean + S09_ParityPrimitive.lean + S09_FrobeniusParity.lean. The full book proof is assembled sorry-free for pairs of members of a FrobeniusFamily (hypothesis79_conclusion) — the exact context (7.10) needs. The book's (1.1)-parity step is a proper standalone primitive (cfdot_real_vchar_even: (Δ₁,Δ₂) even for real virtual characters over odd-order G). The abstract Hypothesis79-level theorem takes the (5.9)-realness of Δ_i, cross-orthogonality (ζ₁^ν,ζ₂^ν)=0 (book's (4.1) step), and parity as explicit inputs; these are derived only in the Frobenius instantiation. So book generality (arbitrary coherent normal-subgroup pairs) is not a single self-contained theorem, but Frobenius-pair strength is fully proved.

results.name: k ≥ 2 Frobenius subgroups with pairwise-coprime TI kernels force (|G₀|−1)/|G| ≥ (e−1)((h−2e−1)/(eh) + 2/(h(h+2))) for some i
results.notes: S09_FrobeniusCardG0LowerBound.lean, sorry-free, exact displayed inequality over ℚ, hypotheses (a)-(d) faithfully bundled in FrobeniusFamily. ONE genuine specialization: nilpotence of each Frobenius kernel is an explicit hypothesis (hnilp), whereas the book derives it inside the proof from Thompson's theorem ('By a theorem of Thompson, H_i is nilpotent'). Thompson's general Frobenius-kernel-nilpotency theorem (Isaacs 6.22-6.24) is NOT formalized — only the solvable-group version exists (OddOrder.BG.frobeniusKernelIsNilpotent, BG Thm 3.7, requires [IsSolvable G], useless here without FT itself). In every repo consumer the kernels are nilpotent by construction (maxNilpotentNormalHall), so the gap never bites. Closing it = formalizing Thompson's theorem, an Isaacs Ch06 item (~L effort, belongs to that unit).

results.name: Main theorem: no group satisfying the hypothesis of (7.10) has G₀ = {1}
results.notes: S09_FrobeniusCardG0LowerBound.lean (unconditional form) + FrobeniusFamily.lean (8 conditional consumer forms). not_trivial_G0 is sorry-free and consumed on the live FT spine (Pf S10_MinimalSimpleStructure, S14_MaximalI/TypeICovering). Inherits the same nilpotent-kernel hypothesis as (7.10) (book cites Thompson). Note the file header's caution: this is Peterfalvi's §9 formulation of the final contradiction, deliberately distinct from BG App.C Theorem C (p ≤ q) — both exist in the repo as different routes.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §9 (results (7.1)-(7.11)) is essentially complete and entirely sorry-free, spread over 22 S09_*.lean files plus the S09_NonexistenceCertain/ directory (~15k lines); the chain culminates in card_G0_lower_bound (7.10) and not_trivial_G0 (7.11), which are live consumers on the FT spine (Pf S10, S14). The formalization is factored far more finely than the book: (7.7.a) and (7.8.c.i) are structure certificate fields with genuine standalone discharges (chiRho_decomp_induced, chiRho_eq_inner_beta_induced, and 'no-certificate-assumed' constructors hypothesis76OfDade/hypothesis78OfDade), while (7.8.a)/(7.8.b)/(7.9) exist as abstract conditional assemblies whose source facts are fully discharged in the Frobenius-family layer — exactly the strength (7.10) and the later §12/§14 consumers need, but not as single self-contained book-generality statements. The only real content gaps are (i) the equality-iff clauses of (7.2.b) and (7.3) (only the inequalities are proved; the one equality case the book uses, χ = 1_G, is proved directly as the cardinality identity |A^τ|/|G| = |A|/|L|), and (ii) the nilpotent-kernel hypothesis added to (7.10)/(7.11), where the book invokes Thompson's unformalized Frobenius-kernel-nilpotency theorem (repo has only the solvable-case BG Thm 3.7 version; all repo consumers supply nilpotence by construction). Mildly surprising finds: the parity step of (7.9) is a clean reusable primitive (cfdot_real_vchar_even), several results are proved slightly stronger than stated (7.5 for any norm-one class function, 7.7.b for arbitrary CF(G)), and the file headers explicitly document that Pf §9 (7.11) and BG App.C Theorem C are different formulations of the final contradiction, both present in the repo. Verification pass: no labels changed — the partial labels on (7.2)/(7.3) were confirmed by exhaustive repo search (the equality-iff clauses exist nowhere in OddOrder/, though the Coq analogs leC_norm_invDade/leC_cfnorm_invDade_support carry them via lerif), and the three most load-bearing formalized results (7.5) family_inequality, (7.6) hypothesis76OfDade, (7.7) chiRho_decomp_induced + chiRho_norm_sq_double_sum were re-read at statement level and confirmed at full book strength.
units.unit: Peterfalvi §9 Non-existence of a Certain Type of Group of Odd Order, results (7.1)-(7.11)

results.name: Type F groups (M = H ⋊ U with inertia subgroup U₁ and Frobenius sub-complement U₀)
results.notes: OddOrder/GroupTheory/MaximalSubgroupType.lean, aliased in Peterfalvi/S10_StructureSetup.lean. Field-for-field match with the book / Coq of_typeF: H = M_F nontrivial, complement U, abelian normal U₁ with C_U(x) ≤ U₁ for x ∈ H^#, U₀ ≤ U with exp(U₀)=exp(U) and H⋊U₀ Frobenius.

results.name: Type-F basics: |U₀| = exp(U); Frobenius ⟺ Sylows of U cyclic; I(θ)∩U ⊆ U₁
results.notes: (a) proved via Z-group exponent theory. (b) both directions present but factored: converse = typeF_frobenius_of_card_eq_exponent (cyclic-Sylow encoded as |U| = exp U); forward = isZGroup_of_isFrobeniusGroup_of_odd (odd Frobenius complement is a Z-group). (c) proved in S14_MaximalI/Hypothesis.lean via Brauer's permutation lemma, stated with the type-F hypotheses unbundled (coprime |U|,|H| + the (8.1.b) centralizer condition). All sorry-free.

results.name: Type I maximal subgroups (type F + one of: H^# TI / H abelian rank 2 / exponent conditions)
results.notes: Matches Coq of_typeI exactly. Alternative (c) uses O_{p'}(H) cyclic where the book prints O_{p'}(M) — same reading as Coq (BGsection16.of_typeI). TI condition phrased with normalizer bound N_G(H) (= M for maximal M by simplicity).

results.name: Type P maximal subgroups (M = M' ⋊ W₁, M' = H ⋊ U, W = W₁W₂, N_G(X) = W for X ⊆ V)
results.notes: Faithful with two documented care points fixed in review (issue 7008): (8.4.b) encoded as W₁ ≤ N_G(U) (not U ◁ M'), and (8.4.c) uses the real Fitting F(M) = H ⊔ (U ⊓ C(H)). The Coq (8.4.a) 'Hall M W₁' coprimality is not a field — it is derivable in the ambient minimal-simple context (S12.typePData_W1_hall_coprime) and W_cyclic is carried as a (derivable) field. The (8.4.d) reusable form C_{M'}(W₁) = W₂ is proved (derivedInG_inf_centralizer_W1_eq).

results.name: Type-P basics: F(M) = HC_U(H); [U,U] ≤ C(H) and U ⊄ C(H) if U ≠ 1; V is TI with normalizer W
results.notes: (a) F(M) = H ⊔ (U ⊓ C(H)) is the fitting_eq field of TypePData (proved when instances are constructed via the sorry-free BG.Ch4.S16.typePData_of_isTypeP_of_inputs chain). (b) both halves proved in S11_MaximalII_III_IV/WielandtSetup.lean. (c) proved in S10_MinimalSimpleBasic.lean (TI with normalizer bound W; N_G(X) = W is the normalizer_V field). Spread across files but all sorry-free.

results.name: Types II, III, IV (type P + U ≠ 1, |W₁| prime, F(M)^# TI + per-type N_G(U)/abelianness conditions)
results.notes: One deliberate deviation: the (8.6.a) TI clause is recorded for M_F^# (maxNilpotentNormalHall) instead of the book/Coq F(M)^# — a weaker datum, but the taxonomy is proven extensionally equivalent to BG's (BG.Ch4.S16.proposition_type_classification: IsTypeII ↔ IsTypeP2 etc., sorry-free), so no strength is lost for maximal subgroups of the minimal counterexample. Witness-independence of the type-II N_G(U) ⊄ M clause proved (typeII_normalizer_not_le_of_typePData); core transfer between witnesses proved (TypePNontrivialCore.transfer).

results.name: Type V (type P with U = 1 + one of three alternatives incl. |O_p(H)| = p³)
results.notes: Exact match with Coq of_typeV: H^# TI, or p with |W₁| | p−1 and O_{p'}(H) cyclic, or p with |O_p(H)| = p³, |W₁| | p+1, O_{p'}(H) cyclic.

results.name: Dichotomy: all maximals Type I, or a Type-P pair S, T with W = W₁×W₂, S∩T = W covering everything up to conjugacy
results.notes: VERIFIED at statement level: theoremI_nilpotentHall_conjugacy_and_type_dichotomy (TaxonomyOutput.lean:1018) carries the full package — the nilpotent-Hall N_G(H)-fusion-control assertion of BG Theorem I plus the dichotomy with S ≠ T, W = W₁⊔W₂ cyclic, S⊓T = W, non-Type-I S,T, (b2) one Type II, (b4) covering; the Peterfalvi-facing maximalSubgroup_type_dichotomy drops the W data. The (b1) semidirect identifications S = S'⋊W₁ / T = T'⋊W₂ are carried by the Section16MaximalPair carrier (FeitThompsonSection16Core.lean) + BG.Ch4.S14.typeP_derivedInG_isComplement_kappaHall + BG.Ch4.S16.typeP_pair_W_structure (all proved). Content complete but factored across BG §16 and the FT §16 core rather than one statement.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §10 is essentially complete: of its 18 numbered items, 15 are fully formalized and sorry-free, with the taxonomy (8.1)–(8.7) living in the shared OddOrder/GroupTheory/MaximalSubgroupType.lean (proven equivalent to BG's F/P₁/P₂ taxonomy via the sorry-free BG §16 Proposition 16.1) and the theorems heavily but faithfully re-factored onto BG §14–16 endpoints (Theorem I for (8.8), Theorems B/D for (8.12)/(8.13), the faithful M̃-cover for (8.17)). Notable non-obvious placements: (8.2.c) is in S14_MaximalI/Hypothesis.lean, (8.5.b) in S11 WielandtSetup, and (8.16) in S12_TypeIIDadeBase/Frobenius — the original S10 encodings of (8.16) and of the (8.14) kernel were found FALSE-as-stated/unsatisfiable during formalization and were replaced by honest versions (issues 8021/9008; the .mmd is also missing p.48 with (8.14)–(8.17), recovered from the PDF here). The only real gaps: (8.11)'s Sylow-normalizer conjunct is unassembled though all ingredients are proved (S effort); (8.15) exists as per-type Dade-hypothesis instantiations (types I, P₁, II, including the (4.6) carrier) rather than one universal statement including the (5.2) clause; and (8.18) is proved only for type-I pairs (all the spine needs). The two remaining BG sorries (nonidentity_covered_by_sigma_pieces, sigmaLength_one_frobenius_type) are vestigial with zero consumers and do not touch this unit. Slim verification pass: the (8.11) partial label was CONFIRMED after a targeted refutation attempt (the Hall conjunct is fully proved at S10_StructureSetup.lean:393; no Peterfalvi-shaped Sylow-normalizer statement exists anywhere, though the assembly pattern appears inline in S16 TypeBridges.lean:867-891), and the three most load-bearing formalized items (8.8)/(8.13)/(8.17) were re-read at Lean-statement level and confirmed at full book strength — no status changes made.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §11 (book section 9, results (9.1)–(9.11)) is essentially completely formalized and fully sorry-free — roughly 24,000 lines across 23 S11_* files plus substantial generic infrastructure (the Wielandt formula (9.1) is proven unconditionally in OddOrder/GroupTheory via a chief-series assembly discharged by a modular kernel-FPF argument, deliberately factored for reuse). Results (9.1)–(9.6), (9.8) and (9.9) are at full book strength, with (9.6) notably CORRECTING a book overstatement (the unconditional |W2| = p is false for type II; only the image |W̄2| = p holds) and (9.8)–(9.10) having gone through a deliberate count-faithfulness audit (issue 2030). The three items marked formalized_specialized are packaging rather than mathematical gaps: (9.7)'s case-(a) embedding lands in ((𝔽_p)ˣ)^{q−1} instead of the book's order-a cyclic coordinates and case-(b)'s W1 ≅ Aut F identification lives as generic semilinear infrastructure rather than one three-story isomorphism; (9.10) assumes case (b) rather than deriving it from the trigger (a one-line dispatch done at consumers); and the main coherence theorem (9.11) — whose entire (9.11.1)–(9.11.8) engine is landed, mirroring Coq's Ptype_core_coherence — is stated per consumer (types III/IV via S13.coherent_sOf_H0Cprime with its side conditions discharged unconditionally; type II via separate, even stronger, S/T instances in §15) with no single generic declaration over Hypothesis (9.5). Closing the literal-statement gaps would be one S-level assembly each for (9.7)/(9.10) and an M-level uniform re-statement for (9.11); no new mathematics is required anywhere in the unit.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §12 (results (10.1)–(10.11), pp. 58–63) is essentially completely formalized and sorry-free, spread over ~23k lines in S12_MaximalIII_IV_V_Core/{Hypothesis,CharacterParameters,Isometry105,Isometry106,DadeCalculations}.lean plus ~15 support leaves (S12_Noncoherence, S12_TypeVCaseC, S12_Prop109, S12_TypeII*, S12_MaximalBasic, S12_HcBound, S12_Section9Counts). The only deviation from full strength is (10.11): its first assertion (|W1|,|W2| prime) is a standalone theorem, but the Type-II remainder (H elementary abelian of order p^q, S coherent — Coq FTtypeII_prime_facts) exists only as the §15 S/T-pair instances (P/Q_elementaryAbelian, card_P_eq, sSet_coherent_indS/indT_A), not for an arbitrary Type-II maximal — hence formalized_specialized. units.summary: Peterfalvi §13 (book results (11.1)–(11.9), pp. 64–68) is essentially completely formalized and sorry-free across the twelve S13_*.lean leaves (plus the S13_CoreStructure/ directory), with (11.7)'s two-case chief-kernel refutation in S13_ElementaryAbelianKernel.lean and the (11.9.a) Galois layer in S13_TypeIIIGalois.lean. The repo's factoring differs from the book in two systematic ways: (i) the character lemmas (11.4)–(11.8) are parametrized on the (11.3) non-coherence as an explicit hypothesis, discharged everywhere by the unconditional S_H0C_not_coherent_unconditional (built on the unconditional Theorem (10.8)), so composed strength equals the book; (ii) (11.8) is stated existentially (one canonical ζ ∈ S(HC) with the grid non-orthogonality) rather than for every ζ ∈ S(HC) — the only genuine, mild strength gap in the unit (the (11.8.1)–(11.8.6) machinery is ζ-generic, so a universal restatement is ~S effort). Surprises on the strong side: (11.6)'s U-centralizes-H0 clause is proved unconditionally with no character input, and (11.9.c) is strengthened well beyond the book to a universal Type-IV exclusion (no maximal subgroup of a minimal simple odd group is Type IV), feeding the §15/§16 endgame. Several docstrings still mention 'remaining sorries' from mid-development — stale text; all S13 files are sorry-free. Note the missing Nougat page (p. 66) contains only proof steps (11.8.1)–(11.8.4), recovered from the PDF; no numbered result was lost.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §14 (Maximal Subgroups of Type I, results (12.1)-(12.17)) is FULLY formalized and sorry-free, in OddOrder/Peterfalvi/S14_MaximalI/ (12 topic leaves + hub, ~11.7k lines); the headline theorems ((12.6) coherence, (12.7) type-I-Frobenius, (12.16) endgame, (12.17) case-B) are all asserted axiom-clean in AxiomsCheck.lean, and the deep obligations that older docstrings still describe as "sorried" (sibleyTarget_frobI, the (11.9.c)/(9.7.b) kernel reduction) were closed by 2026-07-14 — trust AxiomsCheck over the stale docstrings. The formalization is at or above book strength throughout: (12.2.a) is proved for general (non-Frobenius) type-I subgroups including the (8.2.c) inertia bound, and (12.5) exists in both a coherence-based form and a coherence-free form matching the book's R(χ)-orthogonality hypothesis exactly (needed for the non-Frobenius counterexample M). Two benign factoring differences: (12.2.b)'s "Hypothesis (5.2) holds" is realized through the S07 CharacterDifferenceImage/orthonormal-image machinery rather than an explicit §5-hypothesis instantiation, and (12.7)-(12.16) thread an explicit no-type-V hypothesis that is discharged by the proven S12.no_typeV_maximal_unconditional (the book's Theorem (10.10)). No gaps; nothing to do in this unit.

units.summary: Peterfalvi §15 (repo S15_*, results (13.1)–(13.19)) is fully formalized and sorry-free — the largest Peterfalvi cluster in the repo (52 S15 files plus S16 spill-over), with the (13.1) hypothesis realized as a rich constructed carrier (S15.Hypothesis, built sorry-free on the FT path in FeitThompson.lean) rather than a free-field scaffold. All 19 numbered results have genuine Lean counterparts at essentially book strength; the only genuine narrowing is (13.8), where only the T-side instance (the one (13.10) actually consumes) is instantiated and the S-side form exists only as the side-agnostic norm engine. The formalization is heavily refactored relative to the book, largely following the Coq PFsection13 restructuring: the (13.5)–(13.10) norm cascade splits into generic ℚ/Parseval engines plus honest correction packages (CaseBEndgameSupply), (13.2.e)'s normedTI splits into A(S)-TI + Dade=Ind + A₀ no-escape + a type-P₁ full-A₀ TI theorem, and (13.3.b)/(13.12)/(13.15) are exported as λ-dichotomy forms; the repo even proves (13.4), which Coq skips. Surprises: the repo fixed two book/legacy overstatements (the (13.18) grid-orthogonality conjuncts and an unconditional (13.17.c) small-branch exclusion, both rolled back per issue 3003, the latter deferred to its true (14.5) location), and several legacy carrier records (BasicStructureData) still contain True-placeholder Prop fields and stale 'gated/sorried' docstrings even though the honest theorems now exist — cosmetic debt, not mathematical gaps.

units.unit: Peterfalvi Part II Appendix: A Theorem of Suzuki (pp. 97-134; Chapters I-IV)
units.summary: This unit is essentially unformalized: its only Lean counterpart is OddOrder/Peterfalvi/Appendices/Suzuki.lean, a 5-sorry scaffold (theoremA, general_structure, first_case_theorem, structure_of_H, psu_characterization) whose Hypothesis/Conclusion structures consist of opaque free Prop fields, so even the statements are not at book strength - each sorried theorem is technically trivially dischargeable and encodes no mathematics, meaning all ~30 numbered results are effectively missing. The one genuine sorry-free asset is Appendices/SemilinearField.lean (Peterfalvi Appendix I Prop 2(a)+(b): Schur+Wedderburn field structure and semilinearity), which this unit consumes at Ch I §2 Prop 3 and throughout; Appendices/Huppert.lean also carries real fpf/cyclic support for Appendix I Prop 1 (though its fpf Lemma chain has 1 real sorry), while the other supporting Part II appendices this unit cites (Near-Fields, Suzuki 2-groups/Higman, Feit-Sibley) are scaffold-only apart from a genuine sorry-free NearField class and twisted near-field construction. The dominant external gaps are the target-group libraries - mathlib has only a bare ProjectiveSpecialLinearGroup definition with no PSL(2,q) theory, and Sz(q), PSU(3,q)/PGU(3,q), and the Zassenhaus-group classification ([HB] XI.11.16, assumed as known by the book) exist nowhere - plus three missing classical theorems: Thompson fpf-nilpotency ([H] V.8.14, Isaacs 6C not started), the Hall-Wielandt weakly-closed transfer theorem, and Isaacs Ch.8-style permutation-group basics (Isaacs tree stops at Ch07, though mathlib's MultipleTransitivity file covers 2-transitivity itself). Two practical warnings: math-comp odd-order has NO analog of Peterfalvi Part II (PFsection files cover Part I only), so no Coq crib exists; and the 05.6 mmd has a missing OCR page ([MISSING_PAGE_EMPTY:136]) swallowing items (5)-(9) of Ch IV §2, so the PDF must be consulted there. SLIM-pass verification: all 32 missing labels were re-attacked and CONFIRMED (no status changes), but three notes were corrected - the Wielandt fixed-point theorem [HB] XI.12.4 is NOT missing (it is fully formalized sorry-free as OddOrder.GroupTheory.wielandt_fixedPoint_frobenius = Peterfalvi (9.1) in OddOrder/GroupTheory/WielandtFixedPoint.lean, so it drops off Thm B's external-needs list, along with Clifford theory (CliffordCorrespondence.lean) and Isaacs Ch05 transfer/focal-subgroup machinery which are also present), Huppert.lean's Appendix I Prop 1 support was overstated as sorry-free (pGroup_cyclic_fixedPointFree carries 1 real sorry in the irreducible non-cyclic case, issue 2004), and I.1 Prop 2 gains adjacent dihedral-inversion/Matsuyama/Baer-Suzuki infrastructure in Isaacs/Ch02_Subnormality/Theorem211Wielandt.lean.

results.name: Odd-order D faithful and transitive on E^# (E elementary abelian q-group) => F(D) cyclic, fixed-point-free on E, D/F(D) abelian
results.notes: VERIFIED: stated at full book strength (all three conclusions: IsCyclic F(D), fpf, commutator D <= F(D) = D/F abelian) in OddOrder/Peterfalvi/Appendices/Huppert.lean (line 886). The whole assembly is written and proof-complete: conjugate-stabilizer bridge, per-prime O_p step, O_p(F(D)) = O_p(D), nilpotent Z-group => cyclic, C_D(F)=F via centralizer_fitting_le_fitting. Its ONLY gap is inherited transitively from the Lemma's single sorry (via opCore_isCyclic_and_fpf_of_transitive -> pGroup_cyclic_fixedPointFree); closing the Lemma closes Prop 1 with essentially zero additional work — hence effort S (contingent, not independent). Minor statement deviation: adds [IsSolvable D] as hypothesis where the book derives solvability from odd order via Feit-Thompson; since FT is proved in this repo, the hypothesis is dischargeable at every use site. All nine listed Lean names confirmed present.

results.name: p odd, P a p-group faithful on elementary abelian q-group E with |P_a| constant on E^# => P cyclic and fixed-point-free
results.notes: VERIFIED: this is the location of the file's single sorry (Huppert.lean line 575, inside pGroup_cyclic_fixedPointFree at line 531). Fully proved: part (1) at greater-than-book generality (arbitrary P-permuted iSupIndep decompositions, not just two summands), the operator-Maschke reducible case, the abelian/cyclic irreducible case, and the cyclicity endpoint (Huppert V.8.15 = BG Prop 3.9, OddOrder.BG.Ch3.S12.isCyclic_of_coprime_fpf_pgroup_action in S12_Theorem1212.lean:55, with coprimality q!=p derived from fpf). The sorried piece is exactly the irreducible NON-cyclic case (p. 136): Schur => End field => Z(P) cyclic, [H] III.7.5 normal type-(p,p) subgroup R, transitive permutation of the p subgroups T_i, and E = (+) C_E(T_i). Blocker refutation attempted and failed: [H] III.7.5 = Gorenstein 5.4.10 for CYCLIC-center nonabelian p-groups is still deferred — the deferral docstring and the abelian-center-only theorem exists_normal_isElementaryAbelian_card_prime_sq_of_prime_sq_dvd_card_omega1Center now live in BG/Ch1_Preliminary/S04_SmallRankBasic.lean (lines ~906-993; the survey's cited S04_PGroupsSmallRank.lean is the prefix-split TAIL file after the 2000-line split); no repo-wide hit for the cyclic-center case under any descriptive name (type-(p,p), Hilfssatz, III.7.5, prime_sq greps). Tracked in issues/pending/2004-gorenstein-5410-normal-pp.md (still parked). Minor statement deviations: hypotheses q != p and Nontrivial E added (both degenerate-derivable from the book's hypotheses). Effort M covers Gorenstein 5.4.10 cyclic-center case + Schur/Z(P)-cyclic bridge + the direct-sum decomposition plumbing (part-(1) consumer machinery already exists).
